PracticeIf you believed it you would drop the decision matrix wherever the cues are valid and your feedback has been fast — and keep it everywhere else, which is most places.
After AIIt is the argument against forcing structured evaluation on experienced reviewers — and the conditions that would license it are exactly the ones a fast-changing toolchain removes.
contestedThe power of mental simulation

People can picture only about three moving parts in their head

Klein found that the stories people run in their heads to work out what will happen next are small: about three moving parts and about six steps from one state to another.

Becausethe regularity comes from 79 cases drawn from fireground records, published accident analyses and interviews, and nobody has since tried to confirm or refute it; the constraint tightens sharply when the parts interact rather than act in turn.
LimitsA count taken from cases collected for other purposes, never replicated. Klein says so himself, and the number has survived thirty years mainly through not being tested.
PracticeFailure-mode review — when a review needs more than three moving parts held at once, write them down or split the change; do not simulate it in your head.
After AIA generated change can touch more parts than the reviewer can hold, and nothing in the diff says how many. The size of the change, not the quality of the code, is what decides whether review is possible.
evidenceThe power of mental simulation

People keep a wrong story alive by excusing each odd detail

When the story someone is running in their head is wrong, it fails by absorbing the evidence: each detail that does not fit gets a small, cheap excuse. Nobody keeps count of how many excuses have been made.

BecausePerrow's *de minimus* explanation names the move, the physicists decided someone must have built the dock that morning, and Klein's own orienteering accommodated a creek not on the map and a curving path meant to be straight until the map had to be turned 180 degrees.
LimitsCase evidence and a named mechanism, with no measured rate at which discounting predicts failure. The remedy — counting — has not itself been tested.
PracticeCognitive forcing — keep the tally: write down each thing you explained away, and treat the third one as a signal to throw the frame out rather than patch it again.
After AIAn assistant's account arrives pre-built and carries someone else's confidence, so the discrepancies are being explained away against a story the reviewer never assembled. That is why the counting has to be forced by the interface rather than left to the reviewer.

Descartes' Error, Antonio Damasio

evidencethe chapter A modern Phineas Gage and its results table

A patient passed every reasoning test and still could not choose

The tests built to measure reasoning do not measure whether a person can actually decide. Damasio's patient Elliot scored normal or better on every one of them and still could not choose what to do.

BecauseElliot scored superior or average on every WAIS subtest, normal on Rey and Benton, six categories in seventy sorts on the Wisconsin, a valid normal MMPI profile, and on a purpose-built social battery exceeded controls on consequences — then said he still would not know what to do
LimitsA single patient carries the strong form of the claim, and the batteries of 1994 are not those of today. Later work found ventromedial patients answering moral dilemmas differently rather than failing them.
PracticeCalibration log — score your decisions, not your reasoning, because the instruments that grade the reasoning miss this.
After AIBenchmark scores are instruments of exactly this kind. A system can be superior on every subtest and have nothing in it that terminates a decision.
evidencethe chapter Unpleasantness in Vermont; figure 45.1

Damage to one brain area ruins judgment and leaves intelligence untouched

Damasio argues that following social rules, behaving ethically and choosing in your own interest all depend on one brain system, and that system can be destroyed in a person whose attention, perception, memory, language and intelligence are all unharmed.

Becausethe 1994 reconstruction of Gage's skull placed the damage bilaterally in the ventral and inner prefrontal cortices and left motor, premotor, Broca's and the lateral prefrontal cortices untouched — the tissue his contemporaries assumed was best fitted to sustain such an injury
LimitsMacmillan's history argues the standard account overstates the ruin, since years of demanding stagecoach work in Chile implies substantial re-adaptation. The lesion is a simulation derived from a skull, not an autopsy.
PracticeThe stays-human list — draw the list around what this system does — choosing under consequence — rather than around tasks a machine cannot yet perform.
After AIThe list of what stays human is usually drawn around capabilities. This draws it around a faculty that can be removed from a person while every measurable capability remains.
opinionthe chapter The somatic-marker hypothesis; figure 45.5

Damasio says a gut feeling narrows the options before reasoning starts

Damasio argues that the feeling attached to an imagined outcome (his somatic marker) works before reasoning, not in place of it. It pushes attention onto that outcome and can rule an option out at once, leaving reasoning a smaller field to work over.

Becauseit is offered as a hypothesis, with the 2005 preface doing most of the qualifying — markers do not deliberate, are not sufficient for deciding, need not be unconscious, and do not substitute for reasoning; skin conductance was an index of a marker and never the marker
LimitsA 2006 review found the evidence for markers as the book states them thinner than the presentation suggests. The working-memory half of the hypothesis is stated in the book and never tested.
PracticeCognitive forcing — withhold the recommendation until you have imagined the outcome yourself, since the marker only fires on an option you have entertained.
After AIA recommendation that arrives before you have imagined the outcome occupies the slot the marker filled, and leaves the deduction running over a field that somebody else pruned.
opinionthe opening of The somatic-marker hypothesis and its business-meeting example

Damasio says weighing every cost and benefit will not fit in memory

Damasio's objection to cost-benefit reasoning is not that it is wrong but that it cannot be run: attention and short-term memory are too small to hold the totals. It describes how a patient with ventromedial (front-underside) brain damage decides, not how anyone else does.

Becausethe case is made from the example and from the patients' behaviour — half an hour of reasons for and against two appointment dates — rather than from any measurement of capacity
LimitsTetlock's superforecasters do run explicit weighing and beat intuitive judges, which shows the limit is on unaided capacity and moves once the ledgers are written down.
PracticeCognitive forcing — force the explicit weighing only where the field has already been cut down, and give it external structure when you do.
After AIA model can hold the ledgers, which makes the cool strategy available for the first time. What it cannot supply is the signal that told you which options deserved a ledger at all.
contestedthe chapter's closing section, Since 1994

Damasio's general point was accepted but his specific mechanism was not

Damasio's broad position, that emotion sits inside reasoning rather than outside it, is now the standard view. The specific machinery of bodily markers he described has thinned as criticisms of his card game accumulated.

Becauseboth halves are documented — ventromedial damage reliably produces the pattern and the region became the standard site for subjective value, while the card game's critiques accumulated — and the dispute over the mechanism is live
LimitsEkman's facial feedback failed a large multi-laboratory replication before meta-analyses recovered a small effect, and Macmillan's history revised the Gage case in the other direction.
PracticeDomain audit — when citing a book, audit which half of it you are citing, the position or the mechanism.
After AIA model summarising a field will report the half that travelled, because that is the half the literature repeats. The audit is the same one you would run on a confident secondary source.
evidencethe later part of A modern Phineas Gage; figure 45.2

Damasio's patients lose decision-making and feeling from the same brain damage

Damasio found that the same prefrontal damage that ruins a person's decisions also flattens their feelings, in eleven further patients besides Gage's modern counterpart. Not one of them had one defect without the other.

Becauseeleven further patients with the same prefrontal damage produced the pairing and not one separated the defects, and the same combination appears from elsewhere — anosognosia after right somatosensory damage, and a bilateral amygdala patient at normal intelligence
LimitsThe series is small and clinically selected, and the leucotomy cases carry uncontrolled damage. The historical cases are described retrospectively.
PracticeFailure-mode review — when reviewing a decision that went wrong, ask what the decider felt about the option, not only what they knew about it.
After AINothing in an assistant produces a body state, so whichever of these two outputs the marker contributes is simply absent from the loop when the deciding is handed over.
evidencethe card game in Testing the somatic-marker hypothesis; figure 45.6

Damasio's patients still felt penalties but could not learn to expect them

Damasio's patients had not lost their reaction to punishment; they avoided a losing deck right after a penalty just as healthy players did. What they lost was turning that penalty into an expectation, which is why knowing the rule does not restore their play.

Becausethe inverted schedule, punishment first with reward interspersed, restored normal performance, which disposes of simple insensitivity to punishment; in the original the patients avoided a deck immediately after a penalty exactly as controls did and then, unlike controls, came back to it
LimitsThe decks confound punishment frequency with magnitude and healthy players over-select one of the bad ones. The game has aged much worse than the clinical core it was built to test.
PracticeCalibration log — log the prediction before the outcome, so the penalty has something to attach itself to.
After AIA postmortem you read is a rule; the conversion these patients lost is built from penalties you actually took. Reviewing a model's work supplies a great deal of the first and almost none of the second.
evidencethe slide study in Testing the somatic-marker hypothesis

Damasio's patients understood upsetting pictures and felt nothing at all

A person can understand what a situation means, name the emotion it should produce, and have no bodily reaction to it at all — knowing without feeling.

Becausecontrols produced abundant skin-conductance responses to earthquakes, burning houses and injured people while the frontal patients produced flat recordings, with startle and a deep breath having established the machinery was intact, and afterwards the patients described the content, named the appropriate emotion and ordered the set
LimitsA small patient series with a coarse autonomic index; other channels were not recorded. The patients' reports are self-report about an absence.
PracticeWitness practice in review — notice, during review, whether anything in you responded to the change, or only your account of what it means.
After AITo know but not to feel is also an accurate description of what a model does with a description of harm, and it is the reason the description is not yet the judgement.
contestedthe third study in Testing the somatic-marker hypothesis; figure 45.7

Healthy players sweat before a risky card but brain-damaged patients do not

In Damasio's card game, healthy players' hands began to sweat in the seconds before choosing from a risky deck, and sweated more as the game went on; the patients showed no such response. Both groups reacted normally to wins and losses after they arrived.

Becausethe original recording is clear and the patient-control difference is stark, but what the anticipatory response tracks has been reassigned since, and several of the surrounding claims did not survive
LimitsThe response has been shown to track the size of the reward or penalty on offer rather than a deck's long-run value; the claim that players choose advantageously before knowing why did not survive finer questioning; patients with pure autonomic failure have been reported playing normally.
PracticeFailure-mode review — treat an anticipatory signal as a prompt to look, not as a verdict about long-run value.
After AIThe measurement that made the hypothesis famous is the half that thinned. That is the usual shape — the mechanism story travels and the index it rested on does not, which is worth remembering about any confident summary of a field.

Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance, John D. Lee and Katrina A. See

evidenceA dynamic model of trust and reliance

A fault you cannot predict costs more trust than a big one

Lee and See report that what damages trust is not how big a fault is but how unpredictable it is. People will keep using a machine they know to be faulty as long as they know how it fails.

Becausea small fault with unpredictable results cost more trust than a large fault of constant error, and a fitted first-order differential equation explained 60–86% of the variance in reliance over time
LimitsEstimates of the reliability level at which trust collapses disagree across studies — 90%, 70%, 60% — which the paper reads as evidence that the level is the wrong variable, though it is equally consistent with the level mattering and the microworlds differing.
PracticeFailure-mode review — keep a written list of how your tools fail rather than how often, and treat a failure mode you cannot describe as a reason to withdraw the task, not to add a check.
After AIThis is the sharpest available statement of what makes a jagged frontier expensive: the failures are not large, they are unpredictable, and the paper's own evidence says that is the condition under which trust cannot settle anywhere useful.
opinionImplications for creating trustable automation

A weaker tool you can check may beat a stronger one

Where results depend on the person relying on the tool at the right moments, a simpler and less capable system can be worth more than a complex, better-performing one.

Becauseit follows from the distinction between trustworthy and trustable rather than from a measurement — the algorithms that perform best are often the ones no operator can follow
LimitsLee and See offer no case in which a worse system actually produced better joint performance; the argument is deductive. It also assumes the operator's judgment is worth preserving, which Vaccaro 2024 shows is false wherever the machine is the better partner.
PracticeThe stays-human list — where the work depends on your being able to tell a good answer from a bad one, prefer the tool whose reasoning you can check over the tool that scores better on a benchmark.
After AICynthia Rudin's interpretable models and the whole argument for smaller, inspectable systems are this guideline restated, and the industry has gone the other way — capability first, legibility never.
evidenceA dynamic model of trust and reliance (the trust–self-confidence comparison feeding the intention to rely) and the calibration section (misuse and disuse).

People check a machine only when they trust themselves more than it

Lee and See argue that whether someone checks a machine's output depends on how their trust in the machine compares with their confidence in doing the job themselves. More trust in the machine means less checking; more self-confidence means more.

Becausethe paper's model is a review of the experimental trust-in-automation literature (Lee and Moray's process-control studies, the misuse and disuse cases of Parasuraman and Riley), and the same comparison predicted reliance in later survey and lab work.
LimitsThe model treats trust as one quantity; the paper itself says calibration, resolution and specificity can come apart, and later work found the comparison weaker when the person has no way to judge their own competence.
PracticeAudit reliance by task: where trust in the tool exceeds your own confidence, add a check that does not depend on either.
After AIThe automation Lee and See studied was a boiler or an autopilot with a fixed capability; a model whose capability moves by task makes the comparison harder to keep calibrated, which is what the jagged-frontier result shows.
evidenceRisko Gilbert 2016 — A metacognitive model of the decision; Lee See 2004 — trust minus self-confidence

People set reminders from doubt about memory, not from poor memory

How often people set reminders depends on how confident they feel about their memory, not on how good their memory actually is. That confidence carries over from unrelated tasks, such as judging brightness.

Becauselower memory confidence predicted more reminders with objective ability held constant, and people less confident in a brightness judgement, at matched accuracy, set more reminders in the memory task; the correlation has since been demonstrated causally by manipulating confidence without touching ability.
LimitsThe domain-general result is a correlation across two unrelated judgements, and the confidence measured is self-reported; how stable the disposition is over months is unmeasured.
PracticeTrack when you reach for the tool, and ask what your confidence was doing rather than the task. A bad week or simple tiredness moves reliance without moving the difficulty.
After AIReliance on an assistant rises when you feel least able, which is when you are least able to check it. The loop closes faster with a tool that answers everything than with a notebook.
opinionCalibration, resolution, and specificity; Implications for creating trustable automation

The aim is trusting a tool as much as it deserves

Lee and See argue the goal is to trust a machine exactly as much as it can deliver, not to trust it more. Trusting too much leads to misuse and trusting too little leads to refusing useful help; both are the same error.

Becausethe symmetry of misuse and disuse is an argument from two accident reports and Zuboff's paper-mill operators, not a measured quantity
LimitsTwo accidents and one field study carry the symmetry. A 2011 meta-analysis of trust in human-robot interaction found machine performance dominating everything else, which leaves the paper's long sections on disposition and culture resting on thin evidence.
PracticeReliance audit — record, per task, whether you used the tool and whether you should have, and treat a refusal you should have accepted as the same size of error as an acceptance you should have refused.
After AIWritten about autopilots and pump controllers, the rule now bites hardest on a delegate that is fluent in every domain at once: there is no single level of trust to match, because capability is jagged, so the calibration has to be redone per task rather than per tool.
opinionPerformance, process, and purpose

Trust based on one thing alone swings; trust based on three holds

Lee and See argue that trust built on only one thing — what the machine does, how it works, or what it was built for — swings easily. Trust built on all three stays steady.

Becausethe three bases are a tidy collapse of fourteen published dimension lists, and the stability claim is offered as an explanation for why trust sometimes looks fragile and sometimes immovable rather than as a measured result
LimitsIncoherence between levels is said to damage trust as much as a poor record does, on interpersonal evidence about managers whose stated intentions disagree with their actions; the transfer to machines is asserted. The transparency literature that grew from the process recommendation has mixed results — more explanation raises workload without reliably improving calibration.
PracticeReliance audit — before relying on a tool for something that matters, say out loud what you know about its record, its mechanism and its design intent, and treat a blank in two of the three as a reason to verify.
After AIProcess is the basis that has gone missing: nobody, including the builders, can give an account of how a language model reached an answer, so trust is left resting on performance and on stated purpose, which is exactly the volatile configuration the paper warns about.
evidenceAnalytic, analogical, and affective

Trust is a feeling built on evidence people cannot put into words

Lee and See argue that trust is in the end a feeling rather than a calculation. It moves on evidence the person cannot put into words, such as a bodily reaction that steers them off a risky choice before they can say why.

Becauseventromedial prefrontal lesion patients keep reasoning and lose deciding, and healthy participants produced anticipatory skin-conductance responses that steered them off the risky decks before they could say the decks were risky
LimitsThe gambling-task evidence is about decisions under risk generally, not about trust in automation; the transfer is Lee and See's argument rather than their result. The affective route is also where the paper's own warning lands — the devices that calibrate trust can manufacture it.
PracticeWitness practice in review — when a tool's output feels right, treat the feeling as a datum about your state rather than about the output, and name it before you act on it.
After AIA conversational partner engages the affective route directly and continuously, so the unstatable evidence is now mostly about prose style: fluency, politeness and pace are doing the work that the colour of the fire once did for Zuboff's boiler operator.
evidenceA dynamic model of trust and reliance

Watching for failures stops working when the watcher has other jobs

People told only to watch an automated system caught almost every failure. People given other work at the same time did not. Ten minutes of taking the controls by hand brought their detection back up.

Becauseoperators responsible only for watching detected almost all automation failures and operators with other work did not, replicated with experienced pilots and with rare faults, and ten minutes of manual control handed back by adaptive automation substantially improved subsequent detection
LimitsThe restoring effect is measured over minutes in a laboratory task, not over the months across which a professional skill decays. The paper does not say how much manual control is needed, or how quickly the benefit fades.
PracticeManual flying hours — schedule work you do unassisted, and do not count reviewing a generated draft as monitoring; the finding is that a monitor with a second job is not monitoring.
After AIReviewing model output is precisely the divided-attention condition in which detection failed, and it is now the default arrangement of knowledge work — the reviewer is also the person with the deadline.

When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful, Michelle Vaccaro and others

opinionWhat the analysis cannot settle

A person who catches rare costly errors is worth keeping

Where a rare mistake costs far more than its rarity suggests, a person who catches those mistakes is worth keeping, even when the machine is more accurate on average.

Becauseit is an argument about how to weight outcomes — the paper asks for composite measures carrying time, cost and the cost of each kind of error — not a result the meta-analysis produced
LimitsThe argument licenses keeping a person in almost any loop, since some error is always catastrophic in retrospect; it needs the cost asymmetry to be stated in advance, and the paper supplies no method for that.
PracticeFailure-mode review — before handing a task over on an accuracy comparison, ask what the worst error costs and how often you would be the one to catch it.
After AIIt is also the standard defence of human review in every deployment that has none of the composite measurement the paper asks for — the exception is invoked, the arithmetic never done.
evidenceWho was better alone

AI helps people most where they should not be involved

The measured improvement over working alone is largest exactly in the cases where person and machine together do worse than the machine on its own. The tool looks most impressive where the human is subtracting.

Becauseaugmentation peaked at g = 0.74 in the subgroup where the machine was the better partner — the same subgroup whose synergy was −0.54
LimitsBoth quantities are subgroup estimates from a sample dominated by decision tasks, and the two measures are computed from the same effect sizes, so the divergence is arithmetic as much as it is a finding about people.
PracticeReliance audit — treat a large measured improvement over your unaided self as a reason to check whether the machine alone would do better still.
After AIThis is the mechanism by which enthusiasm and harm arrive together: the felt improvement is real and large, and it is largest in the work where you should not be in the loop at all.
contestedDecisions and creations

Human-AI teams do worse at choosing and no worse at making

Vaccaro's review found that people working with an AI did worse on tasks that pick among fixed options (effect size −0.27), and no worse on tasks that make something (+0.19, which cannot be told apart from zero).

Becausethe creation estimate has an interval from −0.09 to 0.48 and rests on 34 effect sizes against roughly 85% of the sample being decision tasks, so what is reliable is the difference between the two, not the creation number itself
LimitsThe authors' explanation — that a creation task splits itself into the part each partner is better at — is a conjecture, and the moderator did not reach significance for augmentation. METR's 2025 developers were 19% slower on a creation task, which is a caution against reading it as a licence.
PracticeDomain audit — mark each task as choosing or making, and put your review effort on the choosing.
After AIThe sample predates generative systems almost entirely, so the creation result is the least tested part of the paper and the one most often quoted at it.
evidenceWho was better alone

Human-machine teams gain only when the person was better alone

Whether combining a person and a machine helps depends most on which of the two was better working alone. That predicts the outcome better than anything else measured.

BecauseF(1,104) = 81.79 — where the person was better the pair beat both (g = 0.46) and where the machine was better the pair fell below the machine (g = −0.54) — and Cabrera 2023 reproduced the reversal with interface and machine accuracy held constant
LimitsWhich partner is better alone is measured inside each experiment on that experiment's task; it is not a property of a person or a model that transfers. And the sample is dominated by bounded classification, where being better alone is easy to define.
PracticeDomain audit — sort your work by who is actually better at it, and hand over whole the tasks where the machine wins rather than reviewing its output on them.
After AIThe moderator is the same finding Dell'Acqua's frontier names, and it is harder to apply now, because with a general model the answer changes task by task rather than tool by tool.
evidenceWorse than the better of the two

People working with machines do worse than the better partner alone

Pooling 370 effect sizes from 106 experiments, Vaccaro and his co-authors found that a person working with an AI performed worse on average than whichever of the two performed better working alone.

Because370 effect sizes from 106 experiments pool to g = −0.23 (95% CI −0.39 to −0.07, P = 0.005), with 58% of effect sizes below the better partner, and the estimate survived four sensitivity checks
LimitsI² was 97.7%, so the average sits on enormous spread and almost none of the variation is noise. Studies qualified only if all three performances were measured, which excludes every task neither partner can do alone — the cases where combining them is most obviously worth it.
PracticeReliance audit — measure the machine alone as well as yourself and the pair; a comparison that omits the machine cannot tell you whether you are adding anything.
After AIThe search window closed in June 2023, so almost the whole generative era is outside the sample: what was pooled is mostly classifiers judged by paid online workers. The pattern has held where retested, and the missing number is still the machine working alone.
evidenceWho was better alone

Showing explanations or confidence scores did not improve human-AI teamwork

Vaccaro's meta-analysis found that the field's two main fixes — showing the AI's explanation and showing its confidence — changed neither whether the human-AI team beat both members working alone nor whether it beat the person alone.

Becauseacross more than 300 effect sizes neither moderator reached significance for either outcome, and nor did whether participants were domain experts or paid crowdworkers
LimitsA null moderator across heterogeneous studies is weak evidence that explanations never help; it says the literature's explanations, as implemented, did not move the average. Buçinca's cognitive-forcing designs did move accuracy, and they are a different intervention.
PracticeCognitive forcing — stop expecting a better interface to fix reliance; change what the task asks of you instead, by committing to an answer before you look.
After AIChain-of-thought output is an explanation display at enormous scale, offered by default and unverified against the computation that produced the answer, which puts it squarely in the category the meta-analysis found inert.
opinionWho was better alone

Trusting the machine well requires being good at the task

Vaccaro and colleagues argue that in these studies the person's real job is deciding whose answer to use, theirs or the machine's. Someone who cannot tell a hard case from an easy one cannot tell when the machine is wrong.

Becausein more than 95% of the systems sampled the person made the final call after seeing the machine's output, and the inference that someone who cannot tell a hard instance from an easy one cannot tell when the machine has gone wrong is the authors' reading rather than a measured mediation
LimitsFleming Know Thyself is the direct counterweight: metacognitive sensitivity dissociates from ability, so knowing whether an answer is right is at least partly a separate faculty. The paper's claim is about task-level discrimination, not about self-knowledge, and the two are being run together.
PracticeDomain audit — do not accept a reviewing role in work you could not do yourself; deferral is a skilled act, and the skill is the task's own.
After AIThis is the argument against the reviewer-of-machine-output job description that is now being written into most knowledge work, and it is the strongest reason to keep doing the work you intend to supervise.
evidenceSynergy and augmentation; Worse than the better of the two

Vaccaro's analysis shows the chosen comparison decides whether AI looks useful

The same experiments that make human-AI teams look worse than the better party alone show a large gain (g = 0.64) over the person working alone. Which comparison you pick decides whether the tool counts as a success.

Because314 of the same 370 effect sizes are positive against the human baseline, a medium-to-large pooled effect drawn from the identical sample that produced the −0.23
LimitsEgger's regression indicated publication bias for the augmentation estimate (β = 1.96, P = 0.002), which the authors left uncorrected. Augmentation is also the right test where full automation is barred by law, ethics or safety.
PracticeReliance audit — state which baseline a claimed gain is measured against before you accept it, and ask for the other one.
After AIEvery vendor benchmark and internal pilot reports the person-alone baseline, because that is the comparison that flatters; the machine-alone number, which decides whether the person is adding or subtracting, is the one nobody publishes.

The Jagged Technological Frontier, Fabrizio Dell'Acqua and others

evidenceThe task built to defeat it

AI makes a case better argued without making it more correct

Dell'Acqua and colleagues found that consultants using the AI wrote clearer, more persuasive, better-organised arguments whether or not their recommendation was the right one. Graders who did not know the correct answer scored the assisted groups higher either way.

Becausetwo independent grader pools, blind to the correct recommendation, scored the treated groups 1.05 and 1.47 points higher on clarity, persuasiveness and coherence, and the advantage held among those who got the answer right and those who got it wrong
LimitsGraded coherence is a rubric judgment by students and consultants, on one task. Whether better argument makes a wrong conclusion more likely to be accepted downstream was not tested here.
PracticeFailure-mode review — review a recommendation against the evidence it omits, not against how well it reads; in this experiment the best-argued answers were as often the wrong ones.
After AIThis is the clearest measured statement of the cost of fluency: the same system that raises the quality of the case raises it equally for the case that should not be made.
evidenceThe task built to defeat it

Just beyond AI's range the same tool made consultants wrong more often

On a case built to fall just outside what the model handles well, 373 consultants got it right 84.4% of the time without the model, 70.6% with it, and 60.0% with it plus prompt training.

Because373 consultants on a case where the spreadsheet pointed one way and the interview notes the other fell from 84.4% correct in control to 70.6% with the model and 60.0% with the model plus prompt training — about 19 points — while finishing 18% and 30% faster
LimitsOne task outside the frontier against eighteen inside it, and the outside task was built by the authors to produce exactly that drop. The design shows such a task exists inside ordinary professional work and that trained people walk into it; it cannot say how often.
PracticeCognitive forcing — on a judgment where the obvious data and the awkward detail disagree, form and record your own recommendation before you open the model.
After AIThe degradation appeared not because the system was visibly unreliable but because it performed so well on the tasks next door, which is the condition every general assistant now creates by default.
opinionA frontier nobody can see; The task built to defeat it

Nothing warns you when a task falls outside what AI handles

The one task the model made consultants worse at felt no different from the eighteen it helped with. Nothing about it announced that it sat on the far side of a line.

Becauseit is an interpretation of the contrast rather than a measurement — same firm, same population, same incentives, same fluent output, and participants who did not need the model used it anyway, which Dell'Acqua calls falling asleep at the wheel
LimitsInvisibility was not measured — nobody asked participants whether the task felt different. The concept has since become a diagnosis applied after the fact, and the paper's own recommendation that organisations evaluate each task has no method behind it.
PracticeDomain audit — decide in advance, per class of task, which side of the line it sits on, and write the decision down; you will not detect the crossing while working.
After AIThe frontier moves with each release, so a map made this quarter expires; what survives is the warning that fluency is uninformative about which side of the line you are on.

Know Thyself, Stephen M. Fleming

evidenceKnowing me, knowing you

Being overconfident overall is not the same as missing your own errors

How overconfident a person is on average and how well they tell their right answers from their wrong ones are two different things. Someone can rate themselves far too highly overall and still spot each particular mistake.

Becausebias slides both confidence distributions together while sensitivity is how far apart they sit, and 94% of American university professors in one study rated their teaching above average while remaining able to notice the occasion they got wrong
LimitsThe separation is a property of the statistical model fitted to confidence ratings, and the models differ in their assumptions; the above-average surveys are self-report on ill-defined criteria.
PracticeCalibration log — record whether your confidence separated your right answers from your wrong ones, not whether its average was too high; the second is easy to fix and tells you nothing.
After AIMost talk about model calibration is about bias — whether stated confidence matches the base rate — and the quantity that decides whether a person can supervise a system is sensitivity, which is rarely reported for either party.
evidenceAvoiding self-awareness failure; Decisions about decisions

Fleming shows confidence is built separately from accuracy and can rise alone

Fleming shows that the brain builds a feeling of confidence rather than reading it off how accurate you actually were. Raising that feeling without raising accuracy makes people seek less information and change their minds less often.

Becausethe positive-evidence manipulation raises the brightness of signal and noise together, leaving difficulty unchanged and confidence higher, and Rollwage found reduced mind-changing, with contradicting evidence close to undecodable from magnetoencephalography on high-confidence trials
LimitsThe manipulation works on a perceptual decision about dot motion; whether professional judgment can be inflated the same way is an extrapolation. The undecodability result is one imaging study.
PracticeCalibration log — when confidence rises without new evidence, treat it as a reason to seek information rather than to stop.
After AIA system that agrees with you raises confidence by exactly this route — more apparent evidence on both sides of the decision, no more accuracy — and the downstream effect the book measures is that you then stop looking.
evidenceKnowing me, knowing you

Judging your own answers is a separate ability from answering well

Knowing whether your answer is right is a different ability from getting it right. In a sample of nearly a thousand people, IQ predicted how well they did the task but not how well they judged their own answers.

Becausein a sample of nearly a thousand, IQ predicted task performance and not metacognitive sensitivity; patients with anterior prefrontal tumours removed had normal IQ and impaired sensitivity; and Shimamura's 1989 double dissociation separates the two in both directions
LimitsMeasurement is argued over: meta-d′ assumes confidence draws on the same evidence as the decision and is sensitive to where confidence criteria fall. Fleming's own frontal-pole localisation rested on thirty-two volunteers, and correlations of this kind need samples in the thousands to stabilise.
PracticeCalibration log — score your confidence separately from your answers, and treat a run of confident errors as a fault in a different faculty from the one that produced them.
After AIThe faculty the evidence isolates is exactly the one a fluent assistant supplies no help with: it will produce an account of its reasoning on demand, and that account need not correspond to the computation that produced the answer.
opinionAvoiding self-awareness failure

Judging yourself stays inaccurate because the feedback is slow and vague

Fleming argues that judgements about yourself stay wrong because the world corrects them slowly and vaguely. Misjudge the size of a cup and you knock it over at once; talk over everyone in a meeting and you get raised eyebrows, years late.

Becausethe argument runs on illustrations — misjudge the size of a cup and you knock it over, while the person who talks over everyone collects raised eyebrows rather than a spilled drink — with fluency effects supplying the illusions
LimitsFluency effects are the evidence, and some of them have not held — pronounceable company names and disfluent fonts among them; Sans Forgetica did not improve memory in independent tests.
PracticeCalibration log — manufacture the missing feedback: write the prediction down, date it, and go back to it, because nothing in the situation will do this for you.
After AIA tool that answers instantly and agreeably is a fluency machine, so it strengthens the exact illusion this claim identifies, and the loop it feeds back into is still nobody's job.
opinionSelf-awareness in the age of machines

Machines will not learn to judge their own answers by getting better

Fleming argues that a machine will not start knowing when it is wrong simply by becoming more capable. The ability to check its own answers has to be designed and built in on purpose.

Becausethe argument is structural — a network's knowledge sits in the weights, held in the network rather than for it, as Clark and Karmiloff-Smith put it — with working demonstrations (a second network betting on the first, a drone predicting its own crashes) rather than a general result
LimitsChick sexers and expert putters are the analogy carrying the claim, and analogy is not proof that capability never brings self-evaluation with it. Modern systems do report confidence, and the reports are sometimes informative.
PracticeReliance audit — do not treat a stated confidence, or a stated chain of reasoning, as a readout of the mechanism; keep your own metacognition interfaced with the system instead.
After AIIt has aged in the shape he predicted rather than the one expected: language models produce fluent accounts of their own reasoning that need not match the computation, which is Gazzaniga's interpreter in silicon, and training them to please raters makes calibration worse.
evidenceDecisions about decisions

People bad at judging their own accuracy hold more rigid opinions

People poor at telling their right answers from their wrong ones (metacognitive sensitivity) held more rigid political opinions and were less willing to look for new information. This held equally on the left and the right.

Becausesensitivity on a dot-counting task was the best single predictor of dogmatic political views in Fleming's laboratory and also predicted not seeking further information
LimitsA correlation between a laboratory perceptual measure and a survey of political attitudes, from one group; the causal direction is not established, and dogmatism scales have their own problems.
PracticeCognitive forcing — treat a refusal to look at disconfirming material as a symptom rather than a position, in yourself first.
After AIRetrieval systems make it trivially easy to be supplied with confirmation, so the disposition this predicts now has an instrument built for it.
evidenceAvoiding self-awareness failure

The habit of checking yourself breaks down under pressure and stress

People only check their own thinking when they seem to need to, and that checking breaks down worst under heavy load and stress. Those are the moments when it would help most.

Becauselaboratory estimates of off-task attention run from 15% to 50% and rise with practice; making a task harder and faster raised parietal, premotor and visual activity while lowering the prefrontal network; and higher cortisol in a social stress test predicted worse metacognition, with hydrocortisone lowering sensitivity against placebo
LimitsKlein Sources of Power is the counterweight: under time pressure experts in the field make good decisions without deliberation, so degraded reflection is not the same as degraded performance.
PracticeCognitive forcing — build the check into the task rather than relying on noticing; under deadline you will not notice.
After AIAssistance is adopted precisely to work faster under more load, which is the condition the evidence says removes the faculty that would catch the assistance going wrong.
contestedSelf-awareness in the age of machines

Training people to judge their own accuracy works but gains are small

People can be trained to judge better whether they got an answer right, and the improvement carries over to tasks they did not train on. The gains are small.

Becausetwenty minutes a day for two weeks of practice with feedback on confidence rather than accuracy raised sensitivity and transferred to an untrained memory task, and two weeks of meditation training did the same in Baird and Schooler, against Fleming's own caution that the plasticity is asymmetric
LimitsSmall samples, short training, and nothing training can add compares with what disease takes away. Fleming also notes that more accurate self-appraisal is not always kinder.
PracticeCalibration log — take the feedback on your confidence rather than on your answers; that is the manipulation that produced the transfer.
After AIThe training regime — repeated judgments with quick feedback on confidence — is one of the few things a model is well suited to run, and nobody is shipping it.

Dispositional Differences in Cognitive Motivation, John T. Cacioppo and others

evidenceA motivation, not an ability

Enjoying hard thinking is about wanting to, not being clever

People differ in how much they want to think hard, and that is separate from how clever they are. The measure correlates .24 with verbal intelligence and -.03 with abstract reasoning ability.

Becausepooled correlations are .24 with verbal intelligence, .26 with entrance scores and −.03 with abstract reasoning ability, and the disposition predicted recall of a message's arguments after the variance explained by measured intelligence was removed
LimitsThe separation leaned on college entrance scores as the ability measure; it has since been confirmed with better instruments. Education correlates .25 and the direction of that relation cannot be told from the data available.
PracticeWhere someone is not scrutinising an answer, ask what would make it worth their while rather than whether they can.
After AIA tool that removes the effort from producing an answer removes the occasion on which the disposition used to show itself, which makes it a question about who still chooses the harder path when nothing forces it.
evidenceScaling the difference

Enjoying hard thinking is one trait, not several separate ones

How much someone enjoys hard thinking (need for cognition) is a single trait rather than a bundle of them. The eighteen-item questionnaire measures one thing, and the one serious attempt to split it into three failed.

Becausethe short form has α = .90, correlates .95 with the long one and takes 37% of the variance on its first factor, replicated in physicians' patients (38.8%, α = .88) and in Dutch translation, while Tanaka's three proposed subscales loaded at −.01, .70 and .28 across samples against .76 for the single factor
LimitsFactor structure is evidence about a questionnaire, not about a mechanism. Items are face-valid enough that the original authors had to embed them among others and administer them anonymously.
PracticeTreat willingness to think as one trait you can measure in eighteen questions, and stop looking for separate capacities behind it.
After AIThe single factor has held for thirty years, which makes this the most durable part of a review whose persuasion architecture and bias findings have not held.
evidenceEnjoyment, and where the difference disappears

Liking to think only shows when the situation is moderately demanding

The difference between people who enjoy thinking and people who do not (need for cognition) shows up only when a situation makes middling demands. When nothing is at stake nobody thinks hard; when everything is, everybody does.

Becauseeight weeks before a presidential election high scorers reported thinking about it more than low scorers, and by election day the two groups reported the same
LimitsThe review's summary figure carries no numbers in the original and is schematic; the election study is self-report about how much people thought.
PracticeDomain audit — raise the demand of the task rather than selecting for the trait; the differences you are trying to manage disappear where the stakes are plain.
After AIRoutine assisted work sits in the low-demand region where nobody scrutinises, and it is dressed up as high-stakes work, which is the combination that hides the failure.
evidenceEngagement in effortful cognitive endeavors

People who avoid hard thinking will do it given a reason

People who score low on liking effortful thought are not unable to examine an argument. They examined it when the speaker was untrustworthy or the framing was unexpected, and not otherwise.

Becausethey examined the arguments when the source was untrustworthy and not when he was trustworthy, and when the framing was unexpected and not otherwise, while high scorers' attitudes tracked argument quality in every condition
LimitsThe manipulations are laboratory persuasion studies on undergraduates with low personal stakes; whether the same levers work on professional judgment under deadline was not tested.
PracticeCognitive forcing — manufacture the reason: make the source untrustworthy by default, or put the answer in an unexpected frame, rather than exhorting people to think harder.
After AIAn assistant is the trustworthy-source condition by default — fluent, unhesitating, apparently disinterested — which is the condition in which low scorers did not look.
evidenceEnjoyment, and where the difference disappears

People who enjoy hard thinking lose that enjoyment when they are paid

Liking hard thinking (what Cacioppo and Petty call need for cognition) works like enjoyment of the activity itself. Paying people for it reduces it in exactly the people who had it: after paid brainstorming, high scorers played with the extra puzzles less.

Becauseafter brainstorming with or without pay, high scorers played with the extra puzzles more when unpaid and low scorers more when paid, and low scorers loafed in a shared-responsibility group while high scorers did not — though both loafed at screwing nuts onto bolts
LimitsTwo experiments, with brainstorming as the task and undergraduates as the sample. The theory that the disposition grows out of competence feedback and is worn away by surveillance and time pressure has never been tested.
PracticeDo not pay, measure or deadline the part of the work you want people to find interesting; the undermining effect lands on the people who were enjoying it.
After AIThroughput metrics on assisted work are exactly the extrinsic reward the result warns about, and they fall on the people whose willingness to think was the thing being relied on.
evidenceEngagement in effortful cognitive endeavors

People who enjoy thinking behave differently but only a little

People who score high on enjoying hard thinking do behave differently from people who score low, but the differences are small: about a fifth to a third of a standard deviation.

Becauserecall of task-relevant material pools to d = .355 across twenty-two tests, task-relevant thoughts listed to d = .205, information seeking to d = .457, annoyance at demanding tasks to d = −.447 and enjoyment to d = .306
LimitsEricsson Peak is the counterweight: what predicts performance is structured practice, not disposition, and a trait explaining this little leaves most of the variance elsewhere.
PracticeUse the measure to predict tendencies in a group, not to sort individuals; a third of a standard deviation will not tell you about the person in front of you.
After AISmall stable differences in who bothers to check become larger in consequence when checking is the only thing left that the person is doing.
contestedEngagement in effortful cognitive endeavors

People who enjoy thinking correct a bias once it is pointed out

People who score high on need for cognition (they enjoy effortful thinking) are not more impartial. Mood, framing and priming move their judgments too. What they do differently is adjust for an influence once it has been named.

Becausemood, framing and priming shifted high scorers' thoughts with their attitudes following, while the same manipulations moved low scorers directly or not at all — and several of these demonstrations belong to the 1980s–1990s social-priming literature that largely failed to replicate after 2011
LimitsThe review's own caveat is the load-bearing one: a correction is not an accurate judgment, since nobody knows the true size of the influence being adjusted for. And the priming evidence would now have to be redone.
PracticeCognitive forcing — name the likely bias out loud before the judgment rather than after; correction only arrives once the influence is visible.
After AIThinking more about model output is not thinking more impartially about it; what helps is being told in advance where this particular system goes wrong.
evidenceEngagement in effortful cognitive endeavors

People who enjoy thinking follow the argument, others follow the surface cue

People high in need for cognition (those who enjoy effortful thinking) change their minds according to how good the argument is. People low in it go by the cue instead: who is speaking, how many reasons are promised, how confident it sounds.

Becauseeleven tests of the interaction pool to d = .312, and to d = .539 across five studies where participants rated message quality directly; only low scorers were moved by a speaker's claim to be giving ten reasons rather than two, and only when the topic was not personally relevant
LimitsThe architecture behind the result — the elaboration likelihood model's split between a central and a peripheral route — was challenged within three years by single-process accounts and is now one position among several.
PracticeCognitive forcing — in a review, separate the cue from the argument explicitly: who produced it, how confident it sounds, how long it is, then the case itself.
After AIModel output supplies cues in quantity: length, structure, hedging, a confident register. The disposition predicts who reads past them, and the cues have never been cheaper to manufacture.

Using Cognitive Psychology to Understand GPT-3, Marcel Binz and Eric Schulz

evidenceTwelve vignettes (Figure 1B)

GPT-3 answered classic psychology puzzles the way a person would

On twelve famous psychology problems GPT-3 got six right and answered all twelve the way a person might — the Linda conjunction error, the correct answer on the taxicabs, the small-sample mistake on the hospitals, and all three reflection questions wrong in the usual way.

Becausethe run is Davinci at temperature zero, with a third answer added wherever a problem offered only the correct one and the standard human error, so a human-like wrong answer could be distinguished from an idiosyncratic one.
LimitsThe same performance comes apart under edits no person would be troubled by, so the vignettes license nothing about reasoning; these are also the most famous items in psychology and were certainly in the training data.
PracticeLog the moment a model's human-like error makes you feel you understand it. The resemblance is the strongest anthropomorphic cue in this literature and it survives knowing better.
After AIInstruction-tuned successors answer the reflection test correctly and the intuitive errors disappeared, which means the human-likeness was a property of one model at one moment — and nobody can say whether the change was reasoning or contamination.
evidenceDecisions from descriptions

GPT-3 shows three of prospect theory's six effects and not the others

Tested on the contrasts Kahneman and Tversky used, GPT-3 showed three of prospect theory's six effects: framing, the certainty effect and the overweighting of small probabilities. The reflection effect, the isolation effect and magnitude perception did not appear.

Becausethe contrasts are the ones Kahneman and Tversky used, run on the model's choice probabilities rather than on a sample of people, which makes each signature a separate measurement rather than an impression.
LimitsThese contrasts are also textbook items, so exposure cannot be excluded; the split may be a fact about which of the six are more often written down rather than about the model.
PracticeLog the resemblance claim you are tempted to make, then check it signature by signature. Half the pattern appearing is the normal result, and it is not what 'it thinks like a person' describes.
After AIA split result is the honest finding and the hardest one to report. Both the parrot reading and the human-likeness reading have to absorb half of it, and neither predicted the split.
evidenceDecisions from descriptions

On newly generated gambles GPT-3 beat chance but lost to people

On more than 13,000 gambles generated fresh by a program, so they could not have been in its training data, the model chose better than chance but worse than the human participants.

Becausethe Peterson 2021 benchmark scored by regret gives t(29134) = −16.85 against chance and t(29134) = −11.50 against people, and only Davinci beat chance, with Ada, Babbage and Curie failing.
LimitsOne benchmark of described gambles at one moment, on a model family now several generations old; scale within the family predicted the result, so the finding is partly about model size.
PracticeAudit capability on problems generated fresh rather than on published ones. The gap between the two scores is the size of the contamination you cannot otherwise see.
After AIThis is the design worth copying: procedurally generated items where the answer key is computed, not remembered. It is the only kind of evaluation that has not aged badly.
evidenceSince 2023

The GPT-3 result went stale within a year but the method lasted

Within a year the score was out of date: later models trained to follow instructions answered the reflection test correctly, and the intuitive mistakes seen in the GPT-3 family were gone. The design lasted, and checking for contamination became standard.

BecauseHagendorff, Fabi and Kosinski reported the vanished biases in the same year, and Ullman 2023 showed that trivial alterations to theory-of-mind vignettes collapse the performance the unaltered versions appeared to demonstrate.
LimitsThe reversal is documented; what caused it is not, and the data cannot separate better reasoning from items leaking into training. The paper's own successors decline to choose.
PracticeReview any measurement of a model with a date attached, and keep the method rather than the number. The number describes one endpoint at one moment; the design is what you can run again.
After AIEverything measured about a model dates within a year. Anyone building a practice on a published capability figure is building on the least durable part of the result.
evidenceDirected and random exploration

The model beat people at a gambling task without exploring like them

On a repeated choice task where you must balance trying unknown options against sticking with good ones, the model did better than people. It showed none of the exploring that people do.

Becausemean regret was 2.72 against a human 3.24, t(38878) = −5.03, while in Wilson's horizon task there was an effect of estimated reward difference but no interaction with horizon and no horizon effect under unequal information — so neither directed nor tuned random exploration was present — together with a strong bias toward the machine it had seen more often, which the authors trace to next-word prediction treating a recent phrase as likely to recur.
LimitsOne paradigm, one model, and an exploration analysis that rests on the absence of an interaction — a null result — rather than on a positive alternative account.
PracticeAudit the domains where good performance would come from exploring rather than exploiting. A system that beats you on average while never exploring is exactly the collaborator that will not find the option nobody has tried.
After AIBetter outcome and alien process is the characteristic finding of this whole literature. It is also the reason the outcome cannot be used to infer the process, in either direction.
evidenceSeeing versus doing

The model ignored cause and effect and was right by accident

Given the same facts arranged once as a common cause and once as a chain, which call for different answers, the model gave identical numbers. It does not use cause-and-effect structure, so the answers that looked correct were accidents.

Becausethe Waldmann and Hagmayer design, put as chemicals in wine casks, produced identical estimates under two structures that require different answers, and the model also failed to lower its estimate of C after observing that B was absent; the authors' own phrase is that it failed spectacularly in using an underlying causal structure.
LimitsOne design on one model generation; causal competence was claimed for GPT-4 the following year, though on published suites, and scores on freshly built interventional tasks remain far below scores on recall.
PracticeReview the failure modes in any work where the difference between seeing and doing matters — root cause, incident analysis, anything counterfactual. This is the capacity the evidence says is missing, and a fluent answer will be supplied anyway.
After AIOf everything in this unit, this is the failure most likely to be live in current systems and least likely to be visible in the output. The answer will have the right shape.
evidenceModel-based and model-free learning

The model planned on one task and gave snap answers on another

There is no single answer to whether the model thinks things through. On a two-step planning task it behaved like a planner, t(1982) = −6.16 and t(1814) = 2.33 across 200 simulations, while it gave the fast wrong answer to all three reflection questions.

Because200 simulations of twenty rounds made it less likely to repeat a first-stage choice after treasure through a rare transition, t(1982) = −6.16, and more likely to repeat after a rare transition that paid nothing, t(1814) = 2.33 — the pattern a planner produces.
LimitsTwo paradigms with opposite verdicts, which is a finding about the inadequacy of the question rather than about the model; the reflection items are famous and the two-step task is not, so exposure differs between them.
PracticeAudit deliberation per task, not per system. A model that plans on one structure and answers reflexively on another is the normal case, and the two-system vocabulary does not transfer.
After AISystems trained to reason before answering have made the older stimuli harder to read still, since a battery designed to catch a shortcut in a fast answer says little about a system that deliberates.
evidenceProblems with vignette-based investigations

The model's good answers break when the puzzle is reworded slightly

The model's performance on the classic reasoning puzzles falls apart under changes no person would be bothered by, such as a reordered list or a swapped word. The puzzles therefore license no conclusion about whether it reasons.

Becauseasking for the probability that the cab was black, a colour not in the problem, returned 0.2; reordering Wason's cards from A K 4 7 to 4 7 A K changed the answer from A and 7 to A and K; and restating the first reflection item so the bat costs a dollar more than the bat left the answer at ten cents.
LimitsThree demonstrations on one model; the strong form — that no famous item can test anything — is an inference, and models since have become far more robust to reordering without becoming robust enough to skip the check.
PracticePerturb before you trust: change a name, reorder the options, alter a number that should not matter. If the answer moves, what you measured was the wording.
After AIUllman showed the same thing for theory-of-mind vignettes in 2023, and the check is now routine. This is the single most transferable practice in the unit, and it applies to any eval you are shown.
opinionSeeing versus doing

Watching data cannot teach what happens when you act on things

A record of what happened, however large, almost never reveals what would happen if you intervened. Binz and Schulz argue that more training data alone will not give a model causal reasoning; systems that act on an environment might.

Becausethe recommendation is argued from the training objective rather than demonstrated, and the evidence since is mixed: causal competence claimed for GPT-4 rests on published suites, while scores on freshly built interventional tasks remain far below scores on recall.
LimitsAn argument from the training objective, offered as a direction rather than a result; agentic systems that act and observe are now common and the prediction has not been cleanly tested.
PracticePut causal judgement on the list of things that stay with you. Where the question is what would have happened if you had done otherwise, the record the model was trained on does not contain the answer.
After AIThe distinction between seeing and doing is the sharpest line anyone has drawn between what these systems have and what supervision requires. It is also the one least visible in how they perform.

Machine Psychology, Thilo Hagendorff and others

evidenceGood behavioural experimentation

A model's low test score may just mean it was asked badly

When a model scores low on a test, you cannot tell whether the model lacks the ability or the question was put badly. Telling it to think step by step raises scores on many tasks, and sampling several reasoning paths raises them further.

Becausethe elicitation results come with a set of procedures — multiple-choice formats cut reasoning off before it happens, answer order should be shuffled, model sizes should be run across since the largest is not always the most capable, and a marker string separates the answer from the reasoning for scoring.
LimitsThe elicitation gains are themselves scale-dependent and were measured on models where chain-of-thought was still a prompting technique rather than trained-in behaviour.
PracticeSpecify how you asked before reporting what a model could not do. Elicitation is part of the measurement, and a failure you have not tried to elicit past is not a finding.
After AIMost public claims that a model cannot do something are elicitation results in disguise. The same is true in the other direction, which is why both need the procedure stated.
opinionWhat the held-out test set no longer does

Benchmark tests no longer measure what a language model can do

Holding back a set of test questions no longer measures anything. Training data scraped from the whole internet makes a test hard to keep unseen, and the behaviours worth studying were never what the model was trained to do.

Becausethe argument is that the most interesting evaluations are not held-out exemplars of the training task, with in-context learning as the standard case of a capability nobody encoded.
LimitsStated as a prescription rather than demonstrated, and held-out sets still work where the data is genuinely new — private corpora, freshly generated items, tasks invented after the training cut-off.
PracticeStop treating a benchmark score as a measurement and start treating it as a claim about what the model saw. Where you need to know whether a system can do your work, the test has to be one you built.
After AIEvery published benchmark is now in the training data of the next model. The measurement problem is structural and gets worse with each release, not better.
evidenceGood behavioural experimentation

Hagendorff says a model's self-description tells you about the prompt

Hagendorff argues that questionnaires given to a model measure the prompt, not the model. Scores on personality, morality and clinical tests shift so far with wording and the order of options that researchers use differently prompted copies to stand in for different human groups.

Becausethe survey-instrument results have held since the paper predicted them, so a measured personality is now reported as a property of a prompt, and self-report is kept only to characterise a default and to measure steerability.
LimitsInstability under rewording is well established; whether there is a stable underlying disposition that better instruments could reach is not settled, and steerability measurements assume there is a default to steer from.
PracticeLog every time you take a model's statement about itself as information — its confidence, its preferences, its account of its limits. None of it is a reading of anything durable.
After AIUsers ask assistants about themselves constantly, and vendors publish the answers as character. The circuit-level finding is the same from the other side: the account and the computation are different processes.
opinionThe many aspects of intelligent behaviour

Hagendorff says a test without a control proves little either way

Passing a test without a control condition is weak evidence that a model has an ability, and failing one is weak evidence that it lacks it. What a system does on the day and what it can do are different things.

BecauseChomsky's 1965 performance-competence distinction was carried to machines by Firestone in 2020 and Lampinen in 2022, and the everyday case is that people make mistakes on easy arithmetic without lacking arithmetic.
LimitsA borrowed distinction argued by analogy; it cuts both ways and can excuse any failure, which is why it needs the control it recommends rather than standing alone.
PracticeReview both directions of your evidence. A model that failed your task may fail your prompt, and one that passed may have seen it — and neither result means much without a control condition you designed.
After AIThe asymmetry matters for hiring a system as much as for hiring a person. Most deployment decisions rest on a handful of passed tests with no control at all.
opinionBehaviour rather than weights

Hagendorff says watching what a model does is a real explanation

Hagendorff argues that studying what a model does when you use it is a proper way to explain it, because its outputs cannot be predicted from what is known about its weights. For a closed commercial model it is the only way open to outsiders.

Becausefour arguments are offered for the level — where people meet the model, complexity beyond what weights explain, behaviours that appear only at scale, and access through an interface — set against mechanistic interpretability, which must simplify the data, the model or both to make its interventions possible.
LimitsAn argument for a method rather than a result; circuit-level work now explains particular behaviours the behavioural level can only describe, and the two levels have not been reconciled.
PracticeAudit the systems you use by what they do, in your domain, on your work. It is the level you have access to, and for a closed model it is the only evidence anyone outside the laboratory has.
After AIThe model is the first research subject that answers questions on demand and cannot be opened. That combination is why psychology's instruments were borrowed, and why its measurement problems were inherited with them.
contestedThin and thick descriptions

Hagendorff says words like believes and wants really do explain machines

Describing a model as believing or wanting something explains its behaviour better than a purely mechanical description, even though nothing inside the model corresponds to those words. Hagendorff notes that this is already true of the words we use about people.

Becausethe ethnographic distinction is borrowed and argued by symmetry rather than tested; the counter-case is that the mechanisms differ and the words are normatively loaded, widening the gap between what specialists mean and what the public hears.
LimitsContested and conceded in practice: the thick description won by default, adopted by writers who never pause over whether the word is earned, which is at once what the paper argued for and what it warned about.
PracticeLog which mental words you use about a system and what each one would have to mean to be earned. The vocabulary is useful and it is also the mechanism by which projection becomes permanent.
After AIThe words are now standard in technical writing, which means the argument was settled by usage rather than by evidence. That is worth noticing every time one of them does explanatory work in your own reasoning.
contestedSince 2023

Newer models stopped showing human biases and nobody knows why

The human-like reasoning errors found in one generation of models had largely gone in the next. Two explanations fit equally well, better reasoning or test items that leaked into the training data, and the evidence cannot tell them apart.

Becausethe reversal is reported against Binz and Schulz's own finding and the paper declines to choose between the explanations; Dasgupta 2022 sits on the other side, finding that models, like people, reason more accurately about believable familiar material than about the same logic stated abstractly.
LimitsContested because it is undecidable with the available evidence, not because the sides disagree about the facts; a decisive test would need a model whose training data could be inspected.
PracticeLog the interpretation you are inclined to give a model improvement, and note that the contamination explanation is always available and rarely tested. Holding both is the honest position.
After AIImprovement and exposure are confounded in every published capability trend. That is a permanent condition of evaluating systems trained on everything, and it applies to the ones you are buying.
evidenceGood behavioural experimentation

One phrasing of a question measures nothing about a model

Testing a model with a single phrasing measures nothing, because its answers shift with where things sit in the prompt, with how common the words were in training, and with the answer most often shown in the examples.

Becausethe prompt-sensitivity results collected there are why a battery of varied prompts rather than an item is the unit of measurement.
LimitsPrompt sensitivity has fallen with each generation without disappearing, and a battery is expensive, which is why single-prompt results remain the norm in practice.
PracticeRun anything you care about several ways before concluding the model can or cannot do it. One prompt is one sample, and the variance between phrasings is often larger than the difference between models.
After AIThe sensitivity traces back to a mechanism with no intrinsic sense of order, patched from outside. That is the clean line from the architecture to the measurement problem.
opinionGood behavioural experimentation

Testing a model with a published puzzle measures what it has read

Hagendorff argues that a test item copied word for word from a published experiment measures how much of that paper the model has seen as much as its ability. Only an item rebuilt with the same structure and new wording tests anything.

Becausethe rule is stated as a prescription — keep the structure and change everything else, wording, agents, order of events, actions — with procedurally generated tasks named as less exposed by construction; the warning has aged better than the results it was aimed at.
LimitsA prescription rather than a finding, and a hard one to satisfy: rebuilding a task around its structure may change what it measures, and there is no way to confirm that it has not.
PracticeSpecify your evaluations by structure rather than by item. Write down what the task is testing, then generate instances — it is the only form of test that survives the next model release.
After AIThis is the most durable advice in the unit, and it is the reason the paper outlived the results it was surveying.

Being You, Anil Seth

contestedExpecting yourself

Rubber-hand experiments may only measure how suggestible the volunteers are

Seth reports that experiments which make people feel a rubber hand is their own produce weak effects that rise and fall with how suggestible the volunteer is. The research built on them therefore cannot support claims about how body ownership works.

BecauseLush and Dienes, with Seth as an author, found illusion strength tracking hypnotic suggestibility, most published studies never controlled for it, and the challenge is unresolved
LimitsSuggestibility explaining variance does not prove it explains the whole effect, and the clinical dissociations stand whatever happens to the rubber hand. Seth is an author on the challenge to his own literature, which is a reason to trust it and not a reason to call it settled.
PracticeBefore citing a demonstration, ask what the participants were told to expect; if the expectation and the effect cannot be separated, the demonstration is not evidence about mechanism.
After AIThe same problem has moved into model evaluation. A demonstration in which the operator knows which condition is which, and what the result is meant to show, measures the operator as much as the system.

Mindwise, Nicholas Epley

evidenceHow, and how not, to be a better mind reader

Imagining another person's view does not improve accuracy and can worsen it

Trying to work out what someone thinks by imagining yourself in their position does not make you more accurate, and can make you less accurate, because it runs your own mind inside a stereotype.

Becausein 104 couples the control condition reached r = .5 with average error 1.5 and the perspective-taking condition .39 with error 1.7; the fisheries negotiation collapsed fastest under perspective taking, and the result was extended across two dozen experiments in 2018
LimitsImprovement does appear when people are given the other's perspective directly rather than imagining it, so the failure is of imagination and not of perspective. Klein's expert intuition literature finds the opposite in domains with valid cues and fast feedback.
PracticeStop writing specifications by imagining what the user wants; write down the question you would have to ask them, and ask it.
After AIThe move is now made against a model as well: imagining what the system will do with a prompt is the same substitution, and the cheap alternative — run it and look — is the equivalent of asking.
evidenceAn overconfident sense

Knowing someone longer raises confidence but not accuracy at reading them

Epley reports that confidence in reading another mind far outruns accuracy, and that longer acquaintance raises the confidence without raising the accuracy. Dating partners predicted each other's answers 44 per cent of the time and thought they had got 82 per cent right.

Becausedating partners predicted each other's answers 44 per cent of the time and believed they had got 82 per cent right, and length of relationship predicted confidence and was unrelated to accuracy
LimitsThe accuracies are modest rather than zero, and the sense beats chance nearly everywhere it has been tested. The gap is the finding; nothing here says mind reading does not work.
PracticeWrite down what you think a colleague will say before the meeting, then score it; the number, not the feeling, is what you know about them.
