Some of the largest steps in mental growth add no new skill, only a new way of managing old ones. Spread one of two matching rows of eggs apart and five-year-olds say there are more eggs; seven-year-olds say the number is the same.

Becausemany younger children answer correctly when the experiment is only described, or performed behind a screen, so they have the ideas and lack knowledge of when to use them; but Piaget's conservation results were contested within a decade, by James McGarrigle and Margaret Donaldson in 1974, who found children pass when the transformation looks accidental.
LimitsDrill can make a child appear to conserve, but the structures that result transfer only to situations almost identical to the ones they were learned in. The engineering half did not survive: the layers of management the principle made central are what no working system has needed.
PracticeDreyfus mapping and tutor-only rule — when someone is stuck, ask whether they lack the piece or lack the rule for when to reach for it. Teaching the piece again is the usual and usually wrong answer.
After AIIn finished work, someone who has every piece and cannot tell when to use it is indistinguishable from someone who can — and an assistant supplying the missing judgement hides exactly that difference.
evidencethe opening pages, before The world of blocks

The problems a four-year-old solves were the hardest ones to program

Work that educated adults call hard gave way to small programs — mathematical logic in 1956, college calculus in 1961, each holding no more than a hundred or so facts. Work a four-year-old does without noticing resisted for decades.

Becausethe asymmetry was measured against working programs, and Minsky and Papert spent a decade on a robot arm with pressure sensors in its fingertips and a television camera for an eye that still stacked blocks badly; it acquired the name Moravec's paradox in 1988 and is still cited under it.
LimitsThe observation was about hand-written programs. Machines built by the tradition Minsky argued against now do much of what the blocks robot could not, so the line has moved even though the asymmetry held long enough to be named.
PracticeThe stays-human list — when deciding what to hand over, sort the work by how hard it was to write down rather than by how hard it felt to do. The parts that take a degree are often the cheap ones.
After AIThe sorting rule has changed: what a model does well is what was written down often, not what is simple. Judging a room, or telling which of two similar cases you are in, is still the expensive half.

The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha

opinionOn liberation — Śikhidhvaja and Cūḍālā

Cudala's husband heard from a boy what he refused from his wife

Queen Cūḍālā worked the argument out first and alone and told her husband, who laughed and told her to go and enjoy herself. Eighteen years later she returned as a boy brahmin named Kumbha, said the same things, and was heard.

Becausethe story holds the content fixed and varies only the speaker, which is the shape of an experiment, but it is one invented case, and the eighteen years are also spent on the husband's mind ripening, so the two explanations are not separated.
LimitsThe text explains the failure as the husband's unripeness rather than his contempt, which quietly excuses the person who would not listen. And Cūḍālā's remedy is to impersonate someone with standing rather than to fix the hearing, which works in the story and is not available to anyone else.
PracticeWhen a proposal is rejected, re-run it later from a different mouth before concluding it was wrong, and keep a note of whose proposals have needed that.
After AIThe boy brahmin is now the model. Teams accept from it, in its confident register, proposals they refused from the colleague who made them first, and the eighteen years compress to an afternoon without anyone noticing whose argument it was.

Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation

evidenceAutomation bias, the paragraph on interventions

Telling operators to check the aid changed nothing; being held accountable did

Neither a briefing on how decision aids fail nor an instruction to verify the aid changed the error rates, in 181 non-pilots or 48 glass-cockpit pilots, and a redundant second crew member changed nothing. Participants who expected to justify their accuracy made fewer errors and used the checking tool more.

Becausethree interventions that ought to work were tested against a fourth in comparable tasks, and only the one that changed what the operator had to answer for moved both kinds of error
LimitsAccountability here means expecting to explain your accuracy to an experimenter, not the standing kind that also punishes; Edmondson Fearless Organization finds accountability without safety produces silence rather than checking. Buçinca's designs did change behaviour, so the pessimism is about telling, not intervening.
PracticeReplace the reminder to review carefully with a record of what the reviewer checked, which someone will read. Awareness training is the cheapest intervention and the one the evidence rules out.
After AIAlmost every current safeguard is one of the interventions that failed: a banner saying the model can make mistakes, a policy requiring human review, a second reviewer. The one that worked is the one nobody ships.

Language Models in a Programming Course

evidenceThree uses, three correlations

A student's overall model use predicted the unassisted exam mark

Averaging a student's reported use of a language model across generating code, debugging and asking for explanations predicts the two-hour unassisted mark about as well as any single use does — a rank correlation of −0.347, interval −0.626 to −0.044, p 0.026.

Becausethe composite is the fourth row of the paper's correlation table, and it sits between the two significant single uses rather than above or below them, so overall reliance carries the signal on its own.
LimitsThe average is built from three items on a five-point scale, two of which correlate negatively on their own, so it is not independent evidence. Thirty-two students, self-report, no randomisation.
PracticeReliance audit — a crude count of how much you lean on the tool is already diagnostic, so audit the overall level before arguing about which kind of request is acceptable.
After AIThe paper offers it as a summary statistic; read against the split it reports, it is the weaker finding of the two. Reliance predicts, but what you ask for predicts better, and only the second is a thing you can change on Monday.
opinionNine weeks with the tools, one without

Skill left by a course shows only in a task done unassisted

Nine weeks of assisted coursework tell you nothing about what a student can do, so Jošt and colleagues made their only outcome a two-hour invigilated application, on material already covered, with the models removed and the documentation left in.

Becauseit is a choice of design rather than a result, but the marks it produced were spread from 0.50 to 10 with a mean of 6.72 against a median of 8.00, a tail no assignment grade had shown.
LimitsOne two-hour task is a narrow measure of a skill that forms over years, and taking the tool away measures work under a condition nobody will meet again. A mark earned without a model may understate what a person can do with one.
PracticeManual flying hours — put one piece of real work a week through your own hands with the tools off, and treat that, not the shipped output, as the reading of what you still have.
After AIThe productivity literature measures what was shipped while the tool was in hand; this measures what is left in the person when it is gone. For a team, the equivalent reading is not a metric anyone currently collects.
evidenceThree uses, three correlations

Students who had a model write or fix their code scored lower

In a ten-week React course at Maribor, how often a student used a language model to generate code and to debug both went with a lower mark on an application written two hours later without one — rank correlations of −0.305 and −0.360, with both 95 per cent intervals below zero.

Becausethirty-two second-year students, nine weeks of unrestricted model use across four assignments, then one invigilated two-hour task with only Google and the React documentation; p 0.045 for generation and 0.021 for debugging.
LimitsThirty-two students, one library, ten weeks, and use measured by what each student remembered weeks later on a five-point scale. No control group and no randomisation, so the correlation carries no direction on its own.
PracticeDreyfus mapping and tutor-only rule — on material you are still learning, let the model explain and write and debug the code yourself; the two things it is most useful for are the two that cost most.
After AIWritten about students, it describes any adult meeting an unfamiliar stack. The two uses that cost most are the two an agentic editor now performs unasked.
opinionGeneration and debugging against explanation

Teach students to write and fix code before giving them a model

Jošt and colleagues recommend introducing language models later in a curriculum, once a student can write and debug code unaided, so that the productivity arrives without costing the competence that lets the student judge the output. They argue about sequence and do not propose a ban.

Becauseit is the instructional conclusion the authors draw from the ordering across the three uses rather than from any single correlation, and the timing they propose was never itself tested.
LimitsNo arm of the study delayed the tools, so the recommendation is an inference from a correlation on thirty-two students. It also assumes an instructor can hold a line nobody can see being crossed at home.
PracticeDreyfus mapping and tutor-only rule — set the allowed kind of request by the person's stage in that domain rather than by policy for everyone, and move the line as they pass competence.
After AIIn a workplace nobody schedules the stages, so the same rule has to be set by the individual against work they have chosen. The person deciding when they are ready is the one who benefits from saying they already are.

The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking, Hao-Ping (Hank) Lee and others

evidenceFrom execution to stewardship

The effort moved from producing the work to verifying and steering it

Lee's workers described three displacements, not a saving: gathering information became verifying it (111 faster, 56 checking), solving a problem became fitting the answer in (77 tailored, 19 making it usable), and doing a task became overseeing one (129 automating, 48 steering a drifting response).

Becausethe three patterns come from coded free text on 936 tasks with counts on both the reducing and increasing side, reported by workers describing their own week rather than inferred.
LimitsSelf-report cannot weigh the two sides: 111 saying information came faster and 56 saying it had to be checked is not a net figure. One developer found matching generated code to his own cost more than writing it himself.
PracticeFailure-mode review — plan the new work rather than assuming it away: verification, fitting and steering are the tasks that grew, so they get time in the estimate and a checklist of their own.
After AINothing on the increasing side is new work in kind — verifying, fitting and steering were always somebody's job. What has changed is that they are now one person's job, and that person used to do the producing.
opinionFrom execution to stewardship

The production was delegated and the accountability was not

Lee's authors call the worker's new role stewardship rather than teammate, collaborator or supervisor: the making of the thing has been handed over and the responsibility for it has not, which makes verification a standing cost rather than a stage on the way to trust.

Becauseit is the authors' reading of why the human-to-human words are wrong, argued from the displacement pattern in the free text; no measurement bears on it.
LimitsAccountability is a fact about institutions, not tools, and institutions can move it — insurers and vendors already absorb responsibility for machine output elsewhere. If that happens here, the asymmetry dissolves.
PracticeThe stays-human list — write down what the team will not hand over and why, and treat verification as a line in the plan with a name against it, not as something that will shrink as the tool improves.
After AIThe vocabulary problem is the real finding. Every available word for the relation borrows from human working relationships in which responsibility travels with the task, and none of them describes one where it does not.

Why Language Models Hallucinate, Adam Tauman Kalai and others

opinionSince 2025

A scoring rule with no credit for I don't know selects guessers

A scoring rule that pays nothing for saying "I don't know" will select, from any population of candidates, the ones most willing to make something up. Nothing in the argument is about language models; it holds wherever answers are scored one point for right and none for anything else.

Becausethe proof underneath assumes only a grader and a candidate holding beliefs, so the generalisation to people is an inference the chapter draws rather than a result the paper measures.
LimitsIt is an argument by analogy from a theorem about graders to a claim about institutions, with nothing measured on the human side here. Human examinations that deduct marks — JEE, NEET, GATE, the American competitions, the older SAT — show the fix is old, not that the selection effect is large.
PracticeLook at what "I don't know" costs a person in your review, your standup, your interview loop. Where it costs the same as a wrong answer, the confident people will rise and you will not find out why the estimates were wrong.
After AIThe paper was written to explain a machine, and the mechanism it names was running in organisations long before. That the fix is one line in the instructions, and that the field has not written it, says more about who maintains the scoreboards than about what is hard.

The Mythos of Model Interpretability, Zachary C. Lipton

opinionWhat an interpretation is wanted for, the fair and ethical decision-making paragraph

An explanation you cannot contest leaves the decision exactly where it was

Lipton sets one condition on an explanation: it must reason from statements that could be shown false, and offer a way of challenging them and changing the decision when they fail. Almost nothing in the published work, he found, addressed that at all.

Becausethe condition is drawn from the second word of the European proposal then being drafted, that algorithmic decisions be contestable, and the survey behind it is Lipton's own reading of the literature; the decisions at stake are credit lines, job applications and recidivism scores
LimitsA condition, not a method: Lipton supplies no design that meets it. The regulations he cited came into force in 2018, and Wachter, Mittelstadt and Floridi had already argued they grant no right to an explanation of a particular decision, which leaves contestability where he found it.
PracticeFor any decision a system makes about a person, write out what the affected person could say back and what would then change. If nothing changes whatever they say, you have built a notification and should not call it oversight.
After AIAn assistant will produce a reason for anything on request and accept any challenge to it without the decision moving. Fluent grounds are now free, which makes the part he said was missing the only part worth asking for.

GPS and the Cognitive Map, Louisa Dahmani and Véronique D. Bohbot

opinionWhich way the arrow runs

Dahmani and Bohbot blame instructions that leave nothing to decide

What costs a driver their sense of a place is not that the device competes for attention but that a turn-by-turn instruction leaves no decision to make. An aid that gives bearing and distance and lets the user pick the turns should cost less.

Becausethey argue it by contrast rather than by test. Gardony's 2013 aid impaired spatial memory by dividing attention, but it left the route decisions to the user; Spiers's group found in 2017 that hippocampal activity tracked a route's demands only when participants chose their own turns. The neural evidence is circumstantial and the paper says so.
LimitsNobody here was scanned, and no condition varied the instruction's form, so the comparison with Gardony's aid is across studies. Devices have since started naming landmarks and showing the intersection, and the paper cannot say whether that leaves a driver more engaged.
PracticeChoose the form of the help, not just the amount. Ask for the material a decision needs and keep the decision; the version that hands over the answer costs the capacity.
After AIThe same tool sits on both sides of the line: asking a model to explain what it would do leaves the decision with you, and asking it to produce the thing does not.
contestedThree years later

Drivers retested after three years declined in step with their GPS hours

Thirteen of the fifty drivers came back after an average of 3.23 years, and the more hours of guided driving they had logged in between, the further their spatial memory had fallen — the same people, declining with the dose.

Becausewith baseline performance and baseline GPS use held constant, hours logged tracked the fall on the flexibility probe at r = −0.68 and the drawn map at −0.52, with the neuropsychological tests unchanged; but with thirteen people the interval on the strongest result runs from −0.91 to −0.10.
LimitsAn unplanned follow-up: most of the sample had left the city, the intervals are one-tailed, and the authors say spurious correlations are possible. It is the standard citation only because nobody else has tested the same people twice with their hours recorded.
PracticeTreat hours under guidance as the quantity that matters, not the decision to use the tool. If the relation is a dose relation, the counter-dose is scheduled unassisted hours.
After AIThree years is roughly how long an assistant has been in daily use, and nobody recorded a baseline first. The within-person comparison this paper barely managed is one no team can now run.
evidenceFifty drivers

Drivers with more lifetime GPS hours navigated worse without the device

Among fifty Montreal drivers aged 19 to 35, the more hours of their lives a person had spent under satellite navigation, the worse they did on navigation tasks taken with no device at all: fewer landmarks noticed, worse maps drawn from memory, more errors where a map-like memory was needed.

Becauselifetime hours, reconstructed by interview, gave r = −0.22 on the twelve-arm probe and −0.26 on landmarks noticed, while lifetime driving hours correlated with nothing, so time at the wheel is not the explanation.
LimitsSmall effects: −0.22 accounts for about five per cent of the differences between people, and no interval sits far from zero. The design is cross-sectional, and the mazes measure learning a place seen once, not a neighbourhood lived in for years.
PracticeAsk of each thing you have handed over for years what you would score on it today, unaided. The cost of a delegation shows up on the day the tool is absent, which is not a day that arrives on its own.
After AIA delegation nobody debated, measured a decade in. The assistant now does for writing and analysis what the windscreen device did for routes, and nobody's week contains the equivalent unaided test.
evidenceFifty drivers

Heavy GPS users were worse at the strategy they still chose

Among the seventeen participants who used the landmark-and-map strategy from the first trial, more lifetime GPS hours still went with noticing fewer landmarks, r = −0.37. Heavy users were not simply picking the other way of finding a route; they were worse at this one.

Becausethe subgroup was defined by the verbal reports before the correlation was run, so strategy choice is held fixed by construction, and every other spatial measure in the subgroup leaned the same way.
LimitsSeventeen people, and only the landmark count reached significance; the rest of the measures point the same way without support. The subgroup is also self-selected in the sense that strategy use was itself one of the outcomes.
PracticeDo not count still choosing to do something yourself as proof that you still can. Keep the unassisted hours anyway, and look at the result rather than at the decision to attempt it.
After AIThe reassuring version of delegation is that you can always do it yourself when it matters. Here the people who did still do it themselves had got worse at it in proportion to how often they had not.

Why Are There Still So Many Jobs?, David H. Autor

evidencePolanyi's paradox: will it be overcome?

A robot fits windscreens on the line and a person replaces them

Whether a task gets automated is decided by how controlled its setting is, not by how hard the task is. Car plants fit windscreens with robots; aftermarket replacement of the same glass uses technicians, because removing a broken screen and preparing the frame demands adaptation no affordable robot can manage.

Becausetwo cases of the same physical task fall on opposite sides of the line, and a third separates setting from task outright — Kiva Systems, bought by Amazon in 2012, automated warehouses without solving picking, its robots moving shelves across a level floor while a human handles the merchandise.
LimitsThe price of regularising is usually invisible and usually enormous — to run cars at all, humanity has levelled, graded and asphalted a meaningful fraction of the earth's surface. And control fails at the edges: a self-driving car matches its sensors against hand-curated maps, and hands the driver back control at exactly the detour or the crossing guard nobody preprocessed.
PracticeSpecification discipline — before deciding a tool cannot do something, change the setting rather than the instruction: fix the inputs, the format and the surrounding process, and try again.
After AIMuch of what looks like a model becoming capable is a workflow becoming regular — structured inputs, retrieval, a fixed output format. That is Autor's first route again, and it fails the same way, at the case the setting did not anticipate.
opinionHow automation and employment interact

Automating part of a job raises the value of the rest

A job is a bundle of tasks, and a process fails if any task in it fails. So making the machine's tasks cheaper and more reliable raises what the remaining human tasks are worth, rather than lowering it.

Becausethe mechanism is Michael Kremer's O-ring production function, named for the seal that destroyed the Challenger, applied to a historical record rather than tested against a counterfactual. The record is real: American agriculture fell from 41 per cent of the workforce in 1900 to 2 per cent in 2000 without employment collapsing.
LimitsIt is a mechanism, not a guarantee, and it runs only as long as the complementary task survives. Acemoglu and Restrepo attribute most of the change in the American wage structure since 1980 to displacement never balanced by new work, and argue that a tax code favouring capital produces automation just good enough to replace a worker and no better — on which reading the complementarities are real but too small.
PracticeThe stays-human list — when a tool takes part of a job, name what is left and treat it as the part now worth investing in, rather than as a residue to be automated next.
After AIAutor assumed the machine's half of the bundle was the writable-down half, which left judgement to the human. A general model takes bits of both, so the remainder is no longer reliably the part that matters.
opinionHow automation and employment interact

Autor gives three conditions for automation to raise a worker's pay

Whether the gain from automation reaches a particular worker depends on three things: whether she supplies the task the machine now needs done, whether other people can enter that task easily, and whether demand for the output grows as it gets cheaper.

Becausethe conditions are argued from cases rather than estimated — the construction worker expert with a shovel who cannot drive an excavator, the teller who can tally currency but cannot sell — though the third has a record behind it: farm productivity rose and the food share of household income fell, while medical productivity rose and the health share rose.
LimitsThe three are named, not weighted, and Autor does not say which will bind. The demand condition can hold for an economy while failing for a person: income freed in one sector is spent in another, often on what William Baumol called technologically lagging services, and consumption has kept pace with productivity rather than approaching satiation.
PracticeDomain audit — for each part of your work a tool now touches, answer the three questions in order. If the complementary task is one anyone could pick up in a week, the gain will not stay with you.
After AIThe second condition now bites hardest. When the complementary task is prompting and checking, entry is nearly free, so the gain is competed away fastest exactly where it is largest.
evidenceHow automation and employment interact

Cash machines quadrupled and the number of bank tellers went up

American cash machines rose from about 100,000 to 400,000 between 1995 and 2010. Over the thirty years to 2010 the number of bank tellers rose too, from about 500,000 to about 550,000, because cheaper branches meant more branches and the job turned into selling.

Becausethe counts are James Bessen's, and the two mechanisms are measured separately — tellers per branch fell by more than a third between 1988 and 2004 while urban branches, helped by deregulation, rose by more than 40 per cent.
LimitsAutor presents it as an illustration and not a law, and it has aged into a caution: teller employment peaked around 2007 and has fallen substantially since. Part of the branch growth came from deregulation rather than the machines, and a teller who could count currency but could not sell lost anyway.
PracticeThe stays-human list — before cutting a role whose main task a tool now does, ask what the role would have to become, and whether the person can supply it.
After AIThe example is quoted as reassurance, and the thirty-year window is what makes it reassuring. Run the series to the present and it shows a job that grew for three decades and then went — which is the shape people have to plan for.
evidenceDoes employment polarisation lead to wage polarisation?

Jobs split into high and low paid but wages did not

Employment moved to the two ends of the pay scale without pay following it. The wages of cleaners, drivers, guards and home health aides rose through the tight labour market of the 1990s and then fell after 2000 even as their numbers grew.

Becausethe fall is in the wage series — real wage growth was negative below roughly the fifteenth percentile between 1999 and 2007 — while the explanation is Autor's three conditions failing at the bottom: information technology barely touches this work either way, demand for it is price-inelastic, and anyone can enter.
LimitsGrowth at the top faltered too and Autor cannot say why: the obvious explanation, computers climbing into professional work, does not fit an investment record that had fallen back to its 1995 share of output. The compression of American wage inequality between 2020 and 2022, which Autor documented with Dube and McGrew, runs the other way.
PracticeDomain audit — count jobs and pay separately. A role growing in number is not evidence that the people in it are doing better; it may be where the displaced are landing.
After AIThe paper reassures by showing the jobs survive; this section is where that stops being reassuring. Surviving in larger numbers at falling pay is an outcome the mechanism permits, and it is the one to watch for in any role a tool has made easy to enter.
evidencePolarisation in the American labour market

Middle-paying jobs shrank in every one of sixteen European economies

Computerising the middle of the pay scale grows both ends. The four middle-skill American occupation groups fell from 60 per cent of employment in 1979 to 49 in 2007 and 46 in 2012, and across sixteen EU economies between 1993 and 2010 the middle-paying share fell in every single country.

Becausetwo independent series agree. The American groups are sales, office and administrative support, production and operatives, against a service share flat until 1979 and rising ever since; the sixteen European falls run between 4.9 and 14.9 percentage points, with high-paying and low-paying shares rising in each.
LimitsA share falling is not a count falling, and the series say which occupations shrank, not why — Chinese import competition after 2001 is a rival explanation Autor names without ranking. The pattern is also not permanent: through the early 2020s the bottom of the American wage distribution gained fastest.
PracticeDreyfus mapping and tutor-only rule — check whether the roles your people would have moved through next still exist. If the tool now covers the middle of the ladder, someone has to build a replacement route to the top.
After AIAutor's middle is defined by codifiable work, and the tasks generative systems take are not that middle. What repeats is the shape rather than the boundary: the rungs that go are the ones on which people used to become senior.

Who is doing the work

The Mythology of Conscious AI, Anil Seth

opinionThe temptations of conscious AI

Calling a model's mistake a hallucination already treats it as conscious

Seth argues that the words already used for a model's mistakes hand it an inner life: a hallucination is a conscious experience that has lost its grip on the world, while a confabulation is only something done. The word settles the question in advance.

Becausethe case rests on the everyday clinical meanings of two words rather than on any study of what the vocabulary does to readers
LimitsA word's clinical meaning is not its technical meaning, and practitioners using hallucination as a term of art are not thereby committed to anything about experience. The claim is about connotation, which is hard to test.
PracticeReplace hallucination with confabulation in your own writing and watch which sentences stop making sense. Those are the ones that were carrying an assumption.
After AIThe word has since hardened into the field's standard term, and the vocabulary now runs ahead of the argument in both directions — reasoning, understanding, wanting, refusing. Each settles a question before it is asked.
opinionWhat not to do

Machines that merely seem conscious are the closer danger

Seth argues that the nearer danger is not conscious machines but machines that only seem conscious, and that the impression may persist even when you know better.

Becausethe Müller-Lyer comparison is an analogy Seth concedes is an analogy, and the claim about imperviousness has not been measured for this case
LimitsThat the seeming is as impervious as the Müller-Lyer figure is asserted, not shown. The Garland test Seth cites tests the observer rather than the machine, which is his point but also the reason no measurement is available.
PracticeAssume knowing better will not stop the impression, and design the working arrangement for a person who will keep feeling that something is there.
After AIThis is the part of the essay that has already come true, and the moral cost he names — either extending concern and distorting it, or withholding it and coarsening ourselves — is now a daily rather than a future problem.
opinionThe temptations of conscious AI

Seth argues intelligence and consciousness need not go together

Seth argues that being intelligent and being conscious are two separate things. They occur together in humans, and that gives us no reason to think they must occur together anywhere else.

Becauseit is an argument from Nagel's formula set against the doing-definition of intelligence, with general anaesthesia as the contrast case, not a finding
LimitsNothing licenses the inference either way; the separability is as unproven as the pairing, and Seth concedes that biological naturalism is a minority position with no knock-down argument behind it.
PracticeSay which of the two you mean before you use either word about a system, and refuse to let a demonstration of one stand as evidence for the other.
After AIThe separation is now the practical question rather than the philosophical one: a system can be relied on for doing without any claim about being, and the confusion costs most when it leaks into how much weight its output is given.
contestedConsciousness and computation · Brains are not computers

Seth says a brain has no software separate from its biology

Seth argues that a brain does not divide into software and hardware the way a computer does. A single neuron is a self-maintaining living machine, so you cannot assume a mind would run the same on any material.

Becauseit rests on Chintaluri and Vogels on neurons that fire partly to clear metabolic waste, plus an energetic argument that such a separation would be expensive to maintain
LimitsOne finding about metabolic firing and one evolutionary plausibility argument are asked to carry a strong conclusion, and Seth's own enthusiasm for neuromorphic and analogue machines leaves the door he is closing partly open.
PracticeStop treating the brain as a substrate running a program when you reason about minds, and stop treating the analogy as evidence when you reason about models.
After AIThe neural-network family that made the brain-as-computer metaphor feel like a discovery is the same family now doing the work, which makes the metaphor harder to dislodge, not easier. Seth's reply is that the resemblance runs the other way.
opinionConsciousness and computation · Simulation is not instantiation

Seth says a simulated brain is conscious only if consciousness is computation

Simulating something creates the real thing only when that thing is itself a set of steps: a simulated calculation really calculates, but a simulated rainstorm leaves nothing wet. A simulated brain would therefore be conscious only if consciousness is computation.

Becausethe rain and digestion cases make the point by analogy; whether consciousness falls on the algorithm side is exactly what is in dispute
LimitsIt is an argument about sufficiency and settles nothing about necessity; Seth says twice that nothing in the essay rules out artificial consciousness in some other substrate.
PracticeRefuse the move from a faithful simulation to the thing simulated unless you can say what makes the thing an algorithm. Ask what the simulation would have to be wet with.
After AIThe argument bites hardest on uploading rather than on anything built today, and Seth notes the trap: wanting the simulation detailed enough to be you is itself a reason to think the detail is doing non-algorithmic work.
opinionThe temptations of conscious AI

Seth says language is what makes people call a machine conscious

Seth argues that language is the feature that makes people call a machine conscious. Nobody says AlphaFold, which predicts protein shapes, is conscious, even though the machinery underneath it is much like a language model's.

Becausethe three biases and the AlphaFold contrast are offered as an argument about why the attribution comes easily, not as a measurement of how often it is made
LimitsAnthropocentrism, exceptionalism and anthropomorphism are named rather than measured, and the pareidolia framing borrowed from Becker is a diagnosis of motive that cannot be falsified by anything a builder says.
PracticeKeep a log of the moments you caught yourself reading intent into a model's output, and look for the trait that triggered it. It is almost always language.
After AIThe trait that trips the attribution is exactly the one the current systems are built around. Nobody calls a protein-structure predictor conscious, though under the hood it is much the same machinery, which is the cleanest evidence that the reaction is about language and not about capability.
opinionSoul machine

Seth says mistaking AI for minds makes us think less of ourselves

Seth argues the nearest harm of confusing AI with conscious minds falls on us, not on the machines. We build them in our own image, then read ourselves back as machines, overrating what they do and underrating what we do.

BecauseVallor's mirror is offered as a diagnosis of what the confusion does to self-understanding, not as a measured effect
LimitsA claim about a cultural effect, with no measurement of it. The mechanisation of the mind has a long history before AI, and attributing the current form to this particular confusion is an interpretation.
PracticeNotice when you have started describing your own thinking in the machine's vocabulary — context, prompt, retrieval — and check whether the description is doing any work.
After AIThe mirror is now two-way and fast: the vocabulary of models is already the vocabulary people use for their own attention and memory. Seth's worry was that we would sell ourselves cheaply, and the discount is applied in ordinary speech.
contestedWhat not to do

Seth says we will see minds in AI that are not there

Seth argues that our biases will make us wrongly credit AI with consciousness more often than wrongly deny it, because AI resembles us in the ways that do not matter for consciousness and differs in the ways that may.

Becauseit is asserted, and the history Seth invokes on the other side — consciousness withheld from animals and from other humans — is a history of false negatives
LimitsThe essay supplies the counter-evidence itself. The record of withheld moral concern is long and one-sided, and the claim that this case reverses the direction rests on the assertion that AI resembles us only in the ways that do not matter.
PracticeWhen you are weighing whether you are over-reading a system, ask which error the situation is set up to produce rather than trusting the feeling of caution.
After AIThe asymmetry is now commercially useful in one direction, which Seth notes: pronouncements of imminent machine consciousness cluster among people with something to sell. That is a reason to expect false positives that has nothing to do with cognition.

Consciousness Across Three Worldviews, Sarvapriyananda, Agüera y Arcas and Rovelli

opinionWhere the analogy strains, and the bridge

A self begins wherever something maintains a boundary against the world

Sarvapriyananda's lectures argue that evolution produces individual selves the same way Vedanta says they arise: by drawing a distinction. The boundary it draws is both physical, like a cell membrane, and conceptual, like an animal's sense of its own world.

Becausethe most basic form of the interface is a cell membrane, and von Uexküll's umwelt supplies the conceptual side, with an inner aspect of hunger, pain and satiety; the parallel is an interpretation, not a result.
LimitsVedanta holds the subject-object distinction to be finally illusory; evolution's boundary is as real as the membrane that draws it. The two are said to be analogous rather than the same, and the text this leans on treats the individual self as produced by ignorance rather than by selection.
PracticeProjection log — when you are tempted to ask whether a system has a self, ask instead what distinction it maintains and at what boundary.
After AIIt converts the question about machines from what they are into where their boundary is drawn and by whom. On that framing a model's boundary is drawn by its training and its context window, and by nothing it maintains for itself.
opinionWhere the analogy strains, and the bridge

An immune cell, a bee and a hive are each a self

Which thing counts as the self depends on the level of description you pick. An immune cell, the bee it lives in, and the hive the bee lives in are each a living thing with its own world and its own lifespan.

Becausethe immune cell, the bee and the hive are offered as an illustration of the point, with their differing lifespans as the argument
LimitsThree lifespans make a nice illustration and not an argument that the choice of grain is arbitrary; some coarse-grainings track causal structure better than others, and the essay does not say how to tell.
PracticeBefore arguing about whether something is one agent or many, fix the grain you are describing it at, and notice that the answer changes with it.
After AIThe same question is now live about a running system: the call, the session, the fleet. Which one is the agent is a choice of grain, and the accountability follows the choice rather than the other way round.
opinionLight

In the Upanishads light means what you see by, not brightness

In the Upanishads the word light names whatever you see by, not a band of the spectrum. When the sun, the moon, fire and speech have all gone, the Self is what one sees by.

Becausethe reading is built on Yājñavalkya's series in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka and on Gītā 13.18, offered as an interpretation the authors say is approximate
LimitsThe essay's own closing qualification applies here first. A Vedantin can run the translation the other way, with awareness as the primary sense and information the extension, which would make the correspondence an artefact of the reading.
PracticeRead the word in its informational sense wherever the texts use it, and test the reading against the one place it has to hold: what one sees by when nothing else is left.
After AIThe role the word names — what makes the difference that can be acted on — is the same role information plays in an account of a model's world. That is what makes the analogy tempting and what makes it easy to overdraw.
opinionWhere the analogy strains, and the bridge

Living things become selves by drawing a boundary at the cell membrane

Sarvapriyananda's lectures argue that evolution makes selves in the way Vedanta describes: by drawing a line between self and world. The line is physical at the cell membrane and conceptual in the creature's own world of what it can sense.

Becausethe bridge is built from von Uexküll's umwelt extended to the inner side, hunger and pain and satiety, as an argument rather than a measurement
LimitsThe step from a membrane to an umwelt is a real one; the step from an umwelt to experience is not taken, and the authors say so. The parallel with Vedanta's illusory subject–object distinction is offered as a resonance, not an identity.
PracticeWhen you are asked whether a system has a self, ask instead what it is registering and what it treats as its own boundary, and see whether the question survives.
After AIA model has no membrane and no metabolic stake, which is exactly the difference Seth makes load-bearing. The essay's route to a self runs through staying alive, and that route is closed to anything trained rather than grown.
opinionWhere the analogy strains, and the bridge

Sarvapriyananda argues information matters only when it belongs to someone

Information that is merely present and information that belongs to someone are two different things, and only the second has any effect on the system holding it. The DNA of a live bacterium and of a dead one are identical as information.

Becausethe DNA of a live bacterium and of a dead one with the same sequence carry identical Shannon information and only one has causal consequences, and a far-infrared photon and a visible one both carry information while only the second is semantic for a human; the criterion is Bateson's difference that makes a difference, adopted rather than tested.
LimitsThe criterion is circular at the edges: what counts as a difference that makes a difference depends on which system you have already decided to treat as a subject. Bender's argument runs alongside it, that form without communicative intent is not meaning.
PracticeIf you believed it you would ask, of any output, whose umwelt it belongs to — for whom it makes a difference — before asking whether it is correct.
After AIIt is the cleanest available statement of what a model's output is not. The text on the screen is information present; whether it is anyone's depends entirely on the reader, which is where the causal consequences actually land.
opinionWhat the translation leaves out

The essay's own ending admits it never reaches felt experience

The bridge runs one way only. It carries you from Shannon information to a self with its own world of meaning (an umwelt), and stops before the felt character of awareness that the authors themselves named as the sticking point.

Becausethe essay's own closing says so — a live bacterium has semantic information and the essay does not claim it has experience — and the gap it named is still open at the end.
LimitsAn admission by the authors rather than a demonstration that the bridge cannot be built. Nothing here shows the gap is unbridgeable, only that this essay does not bridge it.
PracticeIf you believed it you would refuse to let an argument about information carry a conclusion about experience, in either direction, including the direction that denies it.
After AISeth refuses the same question as a warning against projecting an interior onto a machine; this essay refuses it as an admission that its own bridge does not reach one. They decline the same question for opposite reasons and give opposite advice about what to do next.
contestedWhat the translation leaves out

The information account explains what a creature registers, not what it feels

The essay builds from Shannon information, through evolution, to a creature's own world of meaning (its umwelt). It never reaches what awareness actually feels like, which it had named as the sticking point.

Becausethe authors concede it themselves: a live bacterium has semantic information and no claim is made about its experience
LimitsContested because the essay's own authors would place the gap differently: one of them takes semantic information as the candidate for closing it, which would admit a bacterium, and the reader is left without a criterion.
PracticeAccept the translation as far as the umwelt and stop there. Do not let a good account of what a system registers stand in for an account of what it is like to be one.
After AIThis is the gap every claim about machine experience has to cross, and neither vocabulary crosses it. The information story reaches an umwelt and stops; the Vedanta story starts on the far side and never has to cross.
contestedWhat the translation leaves out

The match between the texts and information theory turns on one word

The whole correspondence rests on a single word taken in two different senses. A Vedantin can run the same translation backwards, with the texts meaning awareness first and information only by extension.

Becausethe essay's own closing frame concedes that approximate translations are useful only so long as one remembers they are approximate
LimitsContested by construction: which sense is primary is the whole question, and neither side can settle it from inside its own vocabulary. The essay does not claim to settle it.
PracticeWhenever a translation between vocabularies turns on a single shared word, run it in the other direction and see whether it still holds.
After AIThe same one-word bridges are now doing heavy work elsewhere — learning, memory, attention, reasoning — each joining a technical sense to an older one. The test is the same: run it backwards.
contestedLight

Vedanta's light of awareness and physics' shared information play the same role

Sarvapriyananda's lectures put Vedanta's self-luminous awareness — that which shows everything else — in the same position that relational physics gives to a field of shared information between systems. In both, “light” means making something known, not a band of the spectrum.

Becausethe support is Yajnavalkya's series of failing lights ending in the Self, Gita 13.18's light of lights, and ordinary usage — an argument sheds light, we say "I see" on the telephone — and the authors call it a partial translation and decline to defend more.
LimitsThe correspondence rests on one word used in two senses. A Vedantin can reply that the texts mean awareness first and information only by extension, in which case the translation runs the other way; the essay's own closing sentence concedes that convergences are approximate.
PracticeIf you believed it you would stop treating the two vocabularies as rivals and start asking which questions each can answer — while refusing to let the correspondence carry any weight the authors themselves decline to put on it.
After AIIt is the most careful of the essays that put Vedanta beside a physical theory, and its care is the point: it is offered as a note on resonances by authors who decline to overplay them, which is the opposite of how such correspondences are usually deployed.
opinionWhere the analogy strains, and the bridge

Whether something is one self or many depends on the level chosen

Which thing counts as the self depends on how coarsely or finely you choose to describe the system.

Becausean immune cell, the bee it lives in and the hive each count as a living entity with its own umwelt, its own preserved information and its own lifespan; the example is an illustration of a choice of description rather than a finding about selves.
LimitsThe text this sits beside holds that the witness is the same in everyone and not a matter of description at all, which is a direct contradiction rather than a nuance. A choice of coarse-graining explains why the self-other line is unstable, not what is on either side of it.
PracticeProjection log — record the level at which you were describing a system when you attributed intent to it, and check whether the attribution survives a level up or down.
After AIAsking whether a model, an agent loop, or the whole deployment is the thing you are dealing with is the same question at a different level, and most disputes about what an assistant "wants" dissolve once the level is fixed.

The Bhagavad Gita, translated by Eknath Easwaran

opinionChapter 2: the whole in outline — the essay on 2.47

Easwaran says the Gita asks you to drop selfish wanting, not possessions

Reading Gita 2.47, Easwaran says what is given up is selfish wanting, not objects and not work itself. The test is the state of mind behind the act, so charity can fail it and cooking a meal can pass.

BecauseEaswaran reads kama as selfish desire rather than desire, following Gandhi's nishkama karma, and makes the state of mind the test rather than the act
LimitsA test located in the state of mind is a test nobody else can run, which Easwaran accepts: philanthropy can fail it and a kitchen can pass, and no one outside can tell which.
PracticeStop asking whether an activity is worthy and start asking what you want from it. The same task passes or fails on that alone.
After AIThe reading rules out the obvious modern renunciation — refusing the tool, doing it by hand on principle — as beside the point. What is being asked about is what you want from the work, not who did it.
contestedWhat this edition chooses

Easwaran's reading of the Gita as inner allegory is one choice

Easwaran presents Krishna as the Self within and the battlefield as the mind. That is his editorial choice, not the only way the text can be read.

BecauseEaswaran says so himself, and chapters 16 and 18, with their duty, social order and warrior's nature, resist the allegory more than chapter 2 does
LimitsTraditions that take Krishna as a personal God and the war as a war have read the same verses for as long. Easwaran's reply is Gandhi's — practise it and see — which is not an argument that settles the reading.
PracticeHold the edition's frame as a frame. Where a verse resists it, read the verse rather than the frame, and note which one you are using.
After AIEvery edition is a choice, and the choice is now easy to obscure: a summary of the Gita produced on request carries a frame that nobody selected and nobody declares. Easwaran at least names his.
opinionChapter 2: the whole in outline — verse 2.47, fourth clause

Gita 2.47 also forbids being attached to doing nothing

The verse that tells Arjuna he has a right to the action but not to its fruits ends with a fourth clause: do not be attached to inaction either. Easwaran, following Gandhi, insists that all four clauses be read together.

BecauseEaswaran, following Gandhi, insists on reading all four clauses of the verse, and the fourth closes the escape the first three seem to open
LimitsThe fourth clause is a prohibition without a criterion: nothing in the verse says how much action is enough, and chapter 3's argument that nobody can remain actionless even for a moment makes the prohibition hard to violate in any measurable way.
PracticeDo not let detachment from results become a reason to stop doing the work yourself. Keep your hands on it on a schedule you have written down.
After AIThe clause reads now as the answer to the obvious objection. Handing the work over and holding the result loosely is not what the verse permits; it names attachment to inaction as the same failure as attachment to the fruit.
opinionChapter 18: freedom and renunciation — verse 18.63

Krishna ends the Gita by telling Arjuna to decide for himself

At the end of the Gita, after seven hundred verses of teaching, Krishna tells Arjuna to reflect on all of it fully and then do as he chooses. The book offers choices, not commands.

Becauseafter seven hundred verses the teacher says reflect on this fully and then do as you choose, and Easwaran makes that verse the hinge of his reading of the whole
LimitsIt is one verse against a great many imperatives, and 18.65 two verses later is an imperative. Making 18.63 the hinge is Easwaran's editorial choice, which he says openly.
PracticeRead prescriptive material as a proposal to be tested in practice rather than as an instruction, and keep the record of what testing it did.
After AIA text that ends by handing the decision back reads differently in a period when the ordinary experience of advice is a confident answer with no such hand-back. The verse's move is the one the interface does not make.
contestedChapter 18: freedom and renunciation — verse 18.59

Krishna tells Arjuna his own nature will make him fight anyway

In Gita 18.59 Krishna tells Arjuna that deciding not to fight will not hold: his own prakriti, the nature he was made with, will compel him to fight regardless. Willpower cannot cancel what a person is.

Because18.59 says Arjuna's own prakriti will compel him, and it sits four verses from 18.63's instruction to reflect and then do as one chooses
LimitsThe text contradicts itself within the same chapter: 18.61 has the lord turning all beings as if mounted on a machine, and 18.63 hands the decision back. Easwaran does not resolve it and neither does the verse.
PracticeWhere you know your own disposition will win, arrange the situation rather than the resolution, and spend the effort on what you can actually place.
After AIThe claim has a new evidential neighbour rather than a new meaning: the deterministic case is now argued from neuroscience rather than from prakriti, and the Gita's version is the one that still asks for a decision afterwards.
opinionChapter 2: the whole in outline — verse 2.47, read with 2.48

The Gita gives you a right to your work, not its results

In verse 2.47 the Bhagavad Gita says a person has a right to the action itself and never to what the action produces. Verse 2.48 adds that yoga means staying even in success and failure.

Becauseit is the text's own instruction, read with 2.48 where yoga is defined as evenness in success and failure; no evidence is offered or available
LimitsThe verse prescribes and does not describe: there is no test that would show anyone's attachment to results had been given up, and 2.48's evenness in success and failure is a state the text asserts is reachable rather than one it demonstrates.
PracticeJudge your own work by whether you did it well, not by how it landed, and do not let the second judgement decide whether the first was worth making.
After AIWhen the fruit of the work arrives in a second and the labour behind it was not yours, the verse's separation of action from result stops being a spiritual discipline and becomes a practical necessity for anyone whose worth had been attached to output.
contestedChapter 12: the way of love — verses 12.8–12.12

The Gita ranks giving up results as both last resort and best

Chapter 12 of the Gita lists practices in descending order and puts giving up the fruit of action at the bottom, for people who can manage nothing else. Verse 12.12 then calls it the highest of them.

Becausethe descending ladder of 12.8 to 12.11 puts it last and 12.12 ranks it highest, a contradiction the essay names and resolves by saying the last resort is the one that works
LimitsContested because the text puts the same practice in two places and the reconciliation is Easwaran's rather than the text's. Whether 12.12 reverses the ladder or completes it has been argued for centuries.
PracticeTake the practice you can actually do rather than the one you admire, and do not treat the accessible one as a lesser version of it.
After AIThe rung anyone can stand on is the one that matters when the higher practices assume time and attention that the work no longer leaves. The text's claim is that peace follows from the last rung at once, not eventually.
opinionChapter 18: freedom and renunciation — verses 18.47–48, with 3.35

The Gita says all work carries fault so faultless work is impossible

The Bhagavad Gita says every undertaking carries some fault, as fire carries smoke. Since faultless work is not on offer, the only real comparison is your own work done badly against someone else's done well — and your own wins.

Becausethe argument runs from the universality of fault to the only comparison left: one's own work done imperfectly against another's done well
LimitsThe verses are used in the text to justify staying in the station of one's birth, which Easwaran's chapter notes is offered as a resolution rather than a problem; the argument from universal fault does not by itself license that conclusion.
PracticeStop comparing your work to a faultless version that does not exist, and compare it instead to the work you would be doing if you were not doing this.
After AIThe faultless alternative is now on offer at low cost, which makes the comparison the verses forbid much easier to make. What the text says is that the comparison was never the right one.
opinionChapter 3: selfless service — verse 3.27, restated at 18.14–16

The Gita says nature does the deed and the ego claims it

The Gita says nature carries out the action and the sense of I claims it as mine. That claim is what binds a person. Drop the claim and nothing about the action itself need change.

Because3.27 states it and 18.14–16 gives the analytic form: the doer is one of five factors, and to see oneself as the whole cause is called not seeing
LimitsThe five factors of 18.14 include providence, which makes the claim unfalsifiable as stated; and 18.63's instruction to reflect and then do as one chooses assumes a doer the analysis has just dissolved.
PracticeWhen reviewing your own work, separate what was done from your claim on having done it. The first can be judged; the second is what makes judging it painful.
After AIThe I-maker's claim is exactly what a model's contribution unsettles, and the text's position is that the claim was always mistaken. What changes is that the mistake is now visible from outside rather than only from inside.
opinionChapter 14: the forces of evolution — verses 14.22–25, with 14.26

The Gita tests the freed person by whether their response changes

The Gita says you can tell someone who has gone beyond the three qualities by one thing. Pleasure and pain, gold and clay, praise and blame, friend and foe all leave their response unchanged.

Becausethe verses list the inputs that leave the response unchanged — pleasure and pain, gold and clay, praise and blame, friend and foe — and 14.26 names devotion as what makes it possible
LimitsAn invariance test read off outward behaviour is worth only as much as the feedback that could disconfirm it, and none is available here.
PracticeUse your own reaction to praise and criticism of your work as the reading. If the two move you differently, the worth is still attached to the output.
After AIThe test is newly usable for a reason the text did not intend: when the work is produced with a model, praise and blame for it arrive detached from effort, and the gap between the two reactions is easy to notice.
opinionChapter 2: the whole in outline — verses 2.62–63

The Gita traces ruin back to what the mind dwells on

In Gita 2.62–63 judgment is lost at the end of a chain that starts with nothing more than dwelling on something: dwelling leads to attachment, then desire, anger, delusion, confused memory, and finally the loss of judgment.

Becausethe verses give a sequence of mental events — dwelling, attachment, desire, anger, delusion, confusion of memory, loss of judgment — with no measurement behind any link
LimitsIt is a chain of introspectible states offered as a causal sequence, with no evidence that the links run in that order or that breaking an early one prevents the later ones.
PracticeIntervene at the first link rather than the last. What you keep returning to decides what you will want, and by the time judgement is at stake it is too late to argue.
After AIThe first link is now managed by other people: what you dwell on is largely what a feed or an assistant puts in front of you, which moves the intervention point outside the practitioner the verses address.

Karma-Yoga, Swami Vivekananda

opinionThe secret of work

Vivekananda says caring about something, not seeing it, leaves the mark

Vivekananda argues that what leaves a mark on a person is attachment, not perception. Of the hundreds of faces you see in a day only the face you love stays with you, though every one of them reached your eyes alike.

Becausethe third lecture's argument is introspective: of hundreds of faces seen in a day only the loved one leaves a mark, though every face fell on the retina alike
LimitsIt is introspection offered as mechanism, and the later psychology of memory gives a more complicated account in which salience, emotion and rehearsal all do work that the single word attachment covers over.
PracticeNotice what you are still turning over at the end of the day. That is the list of things you are attached to, and it is not the same as the list of things you attended to.
After AIWhat leaves a mark and what passes through is now partly a design decision made elsewhere, and the lectures have no account of an environment engineered to produce attachment.
contestedKarma and character

Vivekananda says every act leaves a trace and the traces become character

Vivekananda holds that every action leaves a trace in the mind, that the sum of those traces is a person's character, and that character is what shows up as their will. Nothing enters from outside.

Becausethe samskara account has a habit half that later psychology measured and a thought-travelling-through-the-air half that it did not
LimitsContested because the lectures wrap a defensible account of habit inside an indefensible one of minds tuned to each other like instruments, and use the second to argue that nothing enters from outside — which the sixth lecture then contradicts.
PracticeTreat each occasion of doing the work yourself as depositing something, and each occasion of skipping it as depositing nothing. There is no third option.
After AIThe mechanism is the reason delegation costs something even when the output is fine: the impression is left by the doing, and an output you did not produce leaves none.
opinionWhat is duty?

Vivekananda says no duty can be identified by the act itself

Vivekananda argues that you cannot say which acts are duties, only which direction a person is moving in. Work done out of duty leads in the end to work done with no thought of duty at all.

Becausethe beef case, the Thugs, and the soldier who kills twenty and is proud are offered to show that no definition of duty by the act survives
LimitsThe lectures undercut it four talks later with a flat there is no duty for you and me, and the butcher's contentment with the station of his birth is offered as a resolution rather than as the problem it is.
PracticeDefine what stays yours by where it takes you rather than by the task list, and expect the list to change while the direction does not.
After AIA direction rather than a task list is the only definition that survives a tool that keeps absorbing tasks. What the lectures do not supply is any way to tell the direction from outside.
opinionEach is great in his own place

Vivekananda says refusing to fight means nothing unless you could have fought

Vivekananda argues that not fighting back because you are unable to is a sin, while not fighting back when you could is love. The two look the same from outside, so a person must first become capable and only then grow calm.

BecauseKrishna calls the non-resisting Arjuna a coward, and Buddha giving up a throne is set against a beggar giving up nothing
LimitsThe two extremes are indistinguishable from outside by the lectures' own admission, which makes the distinction unusable as a judgement about anyone else and easy to abuse as a judgement about oneself.
PracticeBefore renouncing a capability, acquire it. Declining to do something you cannot do is not a choice and does not teach you anything.
After AIThe case for learning to do something before deciding not to do it by hand is exactly this argument, and it is the one the tutor-only rule for novices rests on.
opinionThe secret of work

Vivekananda says wanting the result traps you, not the work itself

Vivekananda says that what ties a person down is not the work they do but their attachment to what it will get them — the sense of I and mine.

Becausethe lotus-leaf image and the reading of the Gita's second chapter carry it; the claim is offered as introspection rather than as measurement
LimitsA golden chain is as much a chain as an iron one, so good attachments bind too — which makes the doctrine hard to apply to anyone who is trying to care about their work at all.
PracticeWhen a piece of work will not leave you alone, look for the claim you have on its outcome rather than for a fault in the work.
After AIThe sense of I and mine is what a model's contribution disturbs, and the lectures' position is that the disturbance is a clarification: what was binding was the claim, not the work.
opinionWe help ourselves, not the world · the dog's tail and the white mice

Vivekananda says work changes the worker, not the world

Vivekananda argues that you cannot avoid working and cannot make your work come out right, so the only thing work can change is the person doing it.

Becausethe argument runs from two premises the lectures assert rather than measure — every action mixes good with evil, and every life is lived at the expense of other lives
LimitsThe lectures reverse themselves around it: the world is perfect in the fifth talk and a whirlpool to escape in the seventh, and the associated claim that the total of happiness is fixed has been contradicted by the fall of famine and infant death.
PracticeChoose work by what doing it will make of you, and measure a week by what you practised rather than by what shipped.
After AIThe claim that the only thing work can change is the worker was a spiritual proposition and is now nearly an operational description, since the product can be produced without the worker changing at all. What it costs is the argument that the product does not matter.
opinionThe secret of work

Vivekananda says work from love, not from compulsion

Vivekananda says work done from love leaves no painful reaction afterwards, while work done under compulsion does; he claims ninety-nine people in a hundred work under compulsion.

Becausethe jealous-lover case and Krishna's statement that he works because he loves the world are the argument; the ninety-nine in a hundred is rhetoric, not a count
LimitsThe distinction is drawn entirely from inside and has no outward sign, which is the same problem the Gita's invariance test has. Self-determination theory gives it measurable content that the lectures do not.
PracticeUse the painful reaction as the reading. Work that leaves one is work being done from compulsion, whatever the reason given for it.
After AIThe posture is harder to hold when the work can be produced without you, because the compulsion is no longer to do the work but to be seen to still be needed for it.

Experiences in a Concentration Camp, Viktor E. Frankl

opinionAfter liberation

Frankl found decent and cruel men among guards and prisoners alike

Frankl says knowing whether a man was a guard or a prisoner told you almost nothing about how he behaved. Decency and cruelty ran through both groups: one camp commander bought medicine with his own money; a senior prisoner was harder than any guard.

Becausethe camp commander who bought medicine from his own pocket is set against the senior camp warden, a prisoner, who was harder than any guard
LimitsTwo counter-examples against a category, offered as a moral observation rather than a claim about base rates; the Capos elsewhere in the account are described as chosen for a temperament that suited the role, which cuts the other way.
PracticeStop predicting conduct from role. Ask what a person actually did, and keep the two categories separate from the two groups.
After AIThe habit of reading conduct off a category is what the projection log is for, and it now runs in a new direction: the tool someone used is treated as evidence about how they worked.
opinionThe last freedom

Frankl reversed the question to ask what life expects of you

Frankl says to stop asking what you expect from life and to ask what life expects of you, answered by what you do hour by hour. On that view no general statement of a life's meaning is possible.

Becauseit is the therapeutic move he reports using in the camp, with the tasks differing by person and moment, and no measurement of whether it worked
LimitsFrankl insists this was not philosophy at a distance, but the evidence is his own report of his own practice, and the claim that the meaning of a life cannot be stated in general makes the doctrine unfalsifiable by design.
PracticeAnswer the question in conduct rather than in a statement. What is being asked is what the next hour requires, which is a question that has an answer.
After AIReversing the question is the move available when what you expected from the work is no longer on offer. It relocates the answer to conduct, which is the one place a model cannot stand in for you.
evidenceCamp life

Frankl saw numbness as protection and insult as what still hurt

Frankl observed in the camps that going numb protected prisoners rather than damaging them. What still reached a man through the numbness was not physical pain but being treated unjustly.

Becausefirst-hand observation: sipping soup while a corpse was dragged past, against the blow in the bread line that hurt less than its unreasonableness
LimitsIt is one observer's report of his own affect, recorded because his lack of feeling surprised him as a professional matter, and it generalises to ordinary conditions only by analogy.
PracticeTake indignation seriously as a signal. It is what still gets through when nothing else does, and it usually points at being judged by someone who does not know the work.
After AIThe observation about insult rather than pain transfers directly: what stings is not that the work got harder but being assessed by something that knows nothing about how it was done.
evidenceThe last freedom

Frankl saw that not knowing when it ends stops people planning

Frankl argues that living with no known end date stops a person aiming at the future; the Latin finis means both an ending and a goal. In the camp a day felt longer than a week.

Becausein camp a day lasted longer than a week, and the same deformation of time is known in the unemployed and in sanatorium patients with no discharge date
LimitsThe mechanism is Frankl's inference from what he watched; the cross-domain confirmation is in the unemployment literature rather than in his account, and the Latin pun on finis is an illustration and not an argument.
PracticeGive open-ended work a horizon even an arbitrary one, because a term with no end cannot be aimed at and the aiming is what keeps the work going.
After AIThe unknown limit is now the shape of anyone's working life in a field being rebuilt underneath them: no date, no visible end state, and the same difficulty in aiming at anything that Frankl described.
contestedThe last freedom

Frankl says a person can always choose their attitude to what happens

Frankl claims that everything can be taken from a person except one thing: the freedom to choose what attitude to take to the circumstances they are in.

Becausethe few men who walked through the huts giving away their last bread are offered as proof of a possibility rather than of a rule, in an account that also says the survivors were the scrupleless and the lucky
LimitsOne example proves a possibility and not a rule, which Frankl grants. His own caveat that only the scrupleless survived on average sits badly with a doctrine drawn from the few who were neither scrupleless nor lucky.
PracticeWhen a situation cannot be changed, treat the stance you take to it as the part of it that is still work, and do that work deliberately.
After AIThe claim reads as a limit rather than a consolation when what has been taken is the part of the work that made it yours. It says the stance is still available; it does not say the stance is enough.
opinionCamp life

Frankl says small troubles can hurt as much as great ones

Frankl says suffering behaves like a gas: a small amount and a large amount each fill the whole space available. So the size of a person's suffering is entirely relative, and a small thing can bring the greatest joy.

Becausethe gas analogy is illustrated by the wagon that danced when the train did not cross to Mauthausen, and Frankl offers it as an analogy
LimitsAn analogy rather than a finding, and one that cuts both ways: if size is entirely relative then no comparison between sufferings is possible, including the comparison Frankl's own book invites the reader to make.
PracticeDo not rank your own difficulty against anyone else's before deciding whether it is worth attending to. The ranking is not available from inside and does not help.
After AIThe corollary is the useful half: a trifle can give the greatest joy, which is why a small recovered piece of real work can matter out of proportion to its size.
contestedWhat the account is and is not · Since 1946

Frankl's evidence comes only from survivors, which undercuts his own case

Frankl writes that on average only those survived who had lost all scruples. That makes him one of the lucky ones, writing from inside the sample, and it undercuts the detachment his psychology would need.

BecauseFrankl's own caveat that the best of us did not return sits against a doctrine drawn from the few who were neither scrupleless nor lucky
LimitsContested in the sense that Frankl states the difficulty himself and does not resolve it; whether the doctrine survives the selection effect is a judgement the book leaves to the reader.
PracticeWhen someone draws a lesson from having come through something, ask who did not come through and whether they would have drawn it.
After AIThe same selection runs through every account of working well with a new tool: the people who report it are the ones it worked for, and the sample is assembled after the fact.
evidenceThe last freedom

People survive longer when someone or something outside them needs them

Frankl argues that people endure more when something outside themselves is waiting on them: a person who needs them, or work only they can finish. Two prisoners who meant to kill themselves were turned back this way.

Becausethe two men who meant to kill themselves were turned back by a child abroad and an unfinished series of books, and the observation has been recorded again in later studies of confinement and unemployment
LimitsFrankl's own evidence is two cases and one camp; what makes the claim evidence rather than opinion is the later confinement and unemployment literature, which was not his. Vivekananda argues the opposite: nobody depends on us.
PracticeKeep at least one piece of work that would not get done if you stopped, and be able to name who is waiting on it.
After AIThe uncomfortable version of the question is whether anything in your work is still irreplaceable, and a capable model narrows the honest answer. Frankl's argument is that the answer matters for reasons that have nothing to do with productivity.

Crafting a Job, Amy Wrzesniewski and Jane E. Dutton

evidenceSix crafters · the hospital cleaners

Hospital cleaners with one job description described two entirely different jobs

Employees change which tasks they do, who they deal with and how they see the job. Twenty-eight cleaners in one hospital, all under the same job description, described two different jobs: one minimal and unskilled, one that counted itself part of healing.

Becausetwenty-eight cleaners in one hospital under one job description described two different jobs, one minimal and unskilled, one that added tasks, timed rounds to the ward and counted itself part of healing
LimitsOne hospital, qualitative, and circulated for years as a working paper before its findings appeared in print. It shows two jobs inside one description; it does not show which way the causation ran.
PracticeBefore asking for a different job, move a boundary in the one you have: a task, a relationship, or what you take the work to be for.
After AIThe task boundary is now moved by the tool rather than by the employee, and it moves in the direction the paper's first group took — fewer tasks, less interaction. Crafting is the counter-move, and it has to be made deliberately.
evidenceThe model

How people see their work predicts what they change about it

Wrzesniewski found that people see their work as a job, a career or a calling, and that this predicts what they reshape it toward: the paid tasks, the visible tasks and powerful people, or the purpose.

BecauseWrzesniewski's 1997 survey found the three orientations in almost any occupation, and the paper applies the finding to human-services workers
LimitsThe orientations come from a self-report survey and the application to crafting targets is an extension of the finding rather than a test of it. A separate axis, intrinsic against extrinsic motivation, is layered on with its own evidence.
PracticeAsk what someone is crafting toward before judging whether they are engaged. The paying tasks, the visible tasks and the purpose are three different targets, not three levels of effort.
After AIWhich orientation someone holds decides what they experience a capable assistant as taking away, and the three answers are entirely different. Nothing about the tool distinguishes them.
opinionManagers and limits

Not everyone has the same room to reshape their job
