Norman's 1981 philological case that anattā here is a predicate, and the Buddha's refusal to answer Vacchagotta in either direction, are set against the Theravāda commentarial reading that treats the five constituents plus the eleven-fold scope as exhaustive — with Collins and Harvey generally taken to have had the better of the exchange
LimitsElsewhere the formula is extended past the constituents — sabbe dhammā anattā — which is either the general thesis stated at last or the same predication applied to a wider list. What is not in dispute is the reading of the sentences; the disagreement is about what silence and an exhaustive list add up to.
PracticeNo practice follows; the value is in refusing to import a conclusion the text does not state.
After AIIt matters for the machine question, where the same slide happens: from no self of the kind defined, to no self, to no one there — three different claims run together.
opinionForm is not self — paragraphs 3–5

The Buddha says anything you cannot control is not your self

The Buddha argues that a real self would not make you suffer and would obey when told to be a certain way. Body, feeling, perception, will and consciousness do neither, so none of them is the self.

Becausethe argument is a conditional and its denial, run five times — if form were self it would not tend to sickness and one could say may my form be so — and both consequents fail, which settles nothing unless the criterion is granted
LimitsThe criterion — permanence and control — is the Upaniṣadic one the audience already held, so the argument refutes the inner controller rather than every conceivable self, and the discourse never argues for its own definition. Thompson Why I Am Not a Buddhist presses exactly this.
PracticeWitness practice in review — apply the test to the thing that hurts when work is criticised: if you cannot compel it to be otherwise, it is not the part of you being judged.
After AIApplied to work it cuts the other way from how it is usually quoted: the output you cannot compel to be as you wish is not you, as true of a model's draft as of your own body.
opinionWeariness, fading, release — paragraph 10

The Buddha says freedom comes from seeing clearly, not from trying hard

In the Anattalakkhana Sutta freedom arrives in four steps that each cause the next: you grow weary of what you took to be yourself, passion fades, you are released, and you know you are released. No effort is asked for anywhere.

Becausefour steps in nine Pali words, each the cause of the next, and the five were freed anupādāya, by not clinging, while the discourse was still being spoken
LimitsNine words describing an outcome, with no account of why observing should produce weariness. Hayes ACT Get Out of Your Mind and Vivekananda Karma Yoga both end in action in the world rather than in the fading of passion, which is a disagreement about the goal and not only about the method.
PracticeSitting practice — the instruction is to look rather than to work at it; on this account the effort goes into the looking and nothing else is required.
After AIThe claim that a change of behaviour follows from seeing rather than from resolve is the one part of this the clinical literature has tested, and the trials are Hayes's rather than the tradition's.
opinionThis is not mine — paragraphs 8–9

The Buddha's eleven categories cover every experience so no self can hide

The Buddha lists eleven categories of experience (past, present and future; inside and outside; coarse and fine; low and high; far and near) so that every kind of experience is checked and nothing is left over in which a self could still be found.

Becausepast, future, present; internal, external; gross, subtle; inferior, superior; far, near — applied to each of the five, with sabbaṁ, all, as the operative word
LimitsThanissaro's note argues that a set of discourses indicates a consciousness outside the range of all, which would leave the residue open. And exhaustiveness over five constituents is only exhaustive if a person is nothing but the five, which Sue Hamilton disputes.
PracticeNo practice follows directly; the scope is what turns an observation into a conclusion, and it is what a partial look at one's own reactions never supplies.
After AIAn enumeration designed to leave no residue is the same device an exhaustive specification uses, and Christian Alignment Problem is the record of what happens when one is taken to be complete.
opinionThis is not mine — the threefold formula

The Buddha's formula names three separate attachments, not one

The formula — this is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self — names three separate habits: wanting something is craving, identifying with it is conceit, and taking it to be a self is view.

Becausethe threefold formula is repeated at every stage of the argument, and the tradition reads it as three separate attachments requiring separate undoing
LimitsThe threefold reading is the commentary's, not the text's: the sutta repeats the formula without glossing the three terms, and the distinction between conceit and view is drawn elsewhere in the canon.
PracticeProjection log — when a piece of work is criticised, sort which of the three is stinging: wanting to keep it, being seen as the person who made it, or believing it says what you are.
After AIWith a delegate producing the work, craving and conceit come apart in a new way — the output is not mine and the reputation still is — and the formula is the clearest available tool for telling which one is being defended.

Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta, Pali canon, Majjhima Nikāya 10

opinionObserving dhammas — the hindrances

In this discourse a restless mind is the material not the problem

Desire, ill will, dullness, restlessness and doubt are usually treated as things blocking meditation. In this discourse they are what you observe, which is why the instructions can be given to a beginner at all.

Becausesensual desire, ill will, dullness, restlessness and doubt are elsewhere the standard obstruction to absorption, and here a mind too restless to settle has something to observe rather than something to fix
LimitsThe reversal is inferred from the placement of the hindrances among the objects, not stated. Mandukya Karika treats distraction and torpor as failures to be got past rather than as material, which is the same disagreement about what a difficult session means.
PracticeSitting practice — a restless session is not a failed session; the restlessness is the material.
After AIIt is why this text, rather than the Kārikā, is the one that survives translation into an eight-week course — and the course keeps the permission and drops the frame.
opinionObserving dhammas — the hindrances

The Buddha says to know a state, not to remove it

Throughout the discourse the instruction is to know how a state comes, how it goes and how it stops returning — never to get rid of it. The removal is what the knowing produces.

Becausethe verb is pajānāti and never pajahati, and it stays pajānāti even for the awakening factors, where the object is something to be grown
LimitsA verb choice is thin evidence for a mechanism, and the discourse elsewhere requires that the hindrances be abandoned and the awakening factors fulfilled, which Bhikkhu Bodhi uses to argue the fourth foundation is explicitly evaluative.
PracticeWitness practice in review — when an urge to defend your work arrives, describe how it came and how it goes rather than trying to put it down.
After AIThe equivalent claim in the clinic is that defusion changes the relation and not the content, and that is the one with randomised trials behind it.
contestedSince the fifth century BC

The Pali word sati means holding in mind, not bare attention

Sati, the Pali word now translated as mindfulness, means holding something in mind — it is the same word as the Sanskrit for memory. Bare attention is a 1954 gloss by Nyanaponika of one clause of the text's refrain, made to carry the whole.

Becausesati is the Pali of smṛti, memory; Nyanaponika's coinage entered English from 1954 and Kabat-Zinn's 1979 clinic carried it; and Gethin and Bodhi argue that no early text defines mindfulness as non-judgemental awareness, while the fourth foundation is explicitly evaluative
LimitsIt is a philological argument about what a word meant, and what the practices do is not in dispute — the dispute is over what the text was asking for. Robert Sharf traces the emphasis on unmediated experience to a modern argument, which is history rather than evidence about efficacy.
PracticeSitting practice — hold the scheme in mind while you watch, rather than emptying the mind of schemes; sati calls something to mind, it does not clear it.
After AIMetzinger's proposal of secular meditation in schools is the modern gloss in its most benign form, and the correction here is that what would be taught is a twentieth-century construction, not the discourse.
opinionObserving the body — the refrain; Since the fifth century BC

The Satipatthana Sutta has you watch other people too

In the Satipatthana Sutta the first exercise already asks the practitioner to observe another person's body and mind as well as their own. The practice was never only an inspection of one's own private experience.

Becausethe refrain's internal, external and both clause is read by the commentary as another person's body, which places observation of others in the text from the start
LimitsThe external reading is the commentary's; the Pali could also mean one's own body seen from outside, and Anālayo shows the refrain's clauses are unevenly attested across the surviving versions.
PracticeWitness practice in review — run the observation on the other person in the review as well as on yourself; the text treats both as the same exercise.
After AIThompson's argument against the inward-theatre picture cuts against the modern teaching and not against this text, which is worth holding on to when a tool offers to be your meditation instructor in a room by yourself.
opinionSeven years, or seven days

The Satipatthana discourse shows its method and never argues for it

The Satipatthana discourse promises a definite result to anyone who practises it for anywhere between seven years and seven days. It sets out the method step by step and never says why watching the body should purify anyone.

Becausesixteen rungs run from seven years to seven days with the same promise at each and two possible outcomes of which the second is short of the first, and the discourse never says why observing a body should purify anyone
LimitsA promise repeated sixteen times is rhetoric, and the absence of a mechanism is the thing Anattalakkhana Sutta supplies from outside. Fleming Know Thyself is the contrast: two weeks of trained feedback produced small measured gains, which is the form of evidence this text does not offer.
PracticeSitting practice — take the conditional seriously as a conditional: a bounded promise about a method you can run, not a claim you are asked to believe first.
After AIThe honest modern position is the same shape: a method with measured short-term effects, a contested account of why it works, and a promise that outruns both.
opinionAt Kammāsadhamma — the opening formula

The Satipatthana instruction includes putting aside wanting and resisting

The sutta's opening formula tells the practitioner to put aside longing and aversion toward the world as part of the observing itself. This is therefore not an exercise in accepting whatever arises.

Becausethe opening formula says vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ, alongside ātāpī, ardent, from a root meaning heat, and sampajāno, discriminating knowledge of what one is doing
LimitsWhether vineyya is a precondition or a result of the practice is argued, and the translation decides the claim. Hayes ACT Get Out of Your Mind takes the opposite view deliberately and has trials behind it.
PracticeSitting practice — the text asks for ardour and for the prior removal of wanting and not wanting; a practice that asks only for acceptance is doing something else, which may be fine but should not be called this.
After AIIt is the sharpest correction available to the version of mindfulness sold as neutral stress reduction, which is the version that reaches most people, including through tools that now offer it.
opinionObserving the body — the refrain

The Satipatthana refrain adds five instructions the exercises never give

The refrain repeated after every exercise asks for five things none of the exercises asks for: observe inside, outside and both; observe arising, vanishing and both; hold mindfulness only as far as knowing needs; depend on nothing; cling to nothing.

Becausethe reading rests on two Pali terms: yāvadeva, just so far as, which limits rather than extends, and anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati, which states the goal of the whole discourse in eight words after every exercise
LimitsTwenty-one exercises and one paragraph repeated after each; whether the repetition carries the weight this puts on it is an interpretive choice, and the refrain is one of the clauses whose attestation across versions Anālayo shows to be uneven.
PracticeWitness practice in review — run the refrain rather than the exercise: watch the reaction arise and pass, watch it in the other person too, and stop when knowing is reached.
After AIThe internal-and-external clause is what keeps this from being introspection, and it is the clause a solitary practice with a chatbot as interlocutor has no way to supply.

Why I Am Not a Buddhist, Evan Thompson

opinionNo self? Not so fast

Cause and effect alone cannot say which experience belongs to me

Thompson argues that listing what causes what cannot pick out whose experience an experience is: when I say hello, I cause you to hear it and cause myself to hear it. Something must hold a person together, though it need not be a soul.

Becausethe Nyāya objection is revived rather than tested: when I say hello I cause you to hear it and cause myself to hear it, one cause and two effects, and nothing in the causal relations marks the difference — with the same gap opening for perceptual binding
LimitsIt names a gap without filling it — Thompson admits he has not supplied the principle — and the binding problem it appeals to is itself unresolved, so the argument borrows one open question to keep another open.
PracticeNo practice follows; it is the reason to keep the question open rather than to treat the bundle view as settled.
After AIIt is the sharpest available form of the question about a system that produces many outputs at once: nothing in the causal story says which of them, if any, are its.
opinionThe rhetoric of enlightenment

No brain scan can show enlightenment because the idea decides what counts

Thompson argues that enlightenment only exists under a concept, the way pieces of wood are only chess pieces because people treat them as such. So no brain state is a state of enlightenment by itself; a scan can only show a correlate.

Becausethe case rests on analogy — bits of wood are not chess pieces except under a concept, and money would vanish if everyone forgot what it was — with neural patterns correlated with Yo-Yo Ma playing Bach telling us about training rather than about music
LimitsConcept-dependence does not make a thing unreal — love is his own example — so the argument narrows what a correlate can show rather than denying there is anything to correlate. Traditions that hold the state to be the recognition of what was always so, Mandukya Karika among them, reject the premise.
PracticeNo practice follows; the use is negative, as a standing objection to any claim that a measurement has found a valued state rather than a correlate of one.
After AIIt is the reply to every announcement that a benchmark has measured understanding: the concept decides what would count, and the measurement cannot supply the concept.
opinionNo self? Not so fast

Showing the self is built does not show it is an illusion

Cognitive science shows the self is put together by the brain. Thompson argues that is not the same as showing the self is an illusion, because every illusion is a construction but not every construction is an illusion.

Becausethe distinction is conceptual rather than experimental — illusions are constructions but not every construction is an illusion — and the positive account is an analogy: a self is a process that enacts an I as dancing enacts a dance, and nobody looks for a dance inside a dancer's muscles
LimitsThompson's own positive account still needs a principle of unity he admits he has not supplied, and Buddhist philosophy's own distinction — ātman for the essence, pudgala for the construction — is doing much of the work.
PracticeProjection log — when you notice a reaction is constructed, do not conclude it is not yours; the construction is the person, not a mask over one.
After AIIt is the load-bearing distinction for the machine question: showing that a system's self-reports are generated does not show there is nobody there, and showing there is nobody there requires an account of what would count, which nobody has.
evidenceThe myth of Buddhist exceptionalism

The idea that Buddhism is uniquely scientific was invented in the 1800s

Thompson argues that the belief that Buddhism is uniquely rational and scientific is not an old core recovered. Reformers in the nineteenth century took a colonial argument that possessing science proved Christian superiority, and turned it around.

Becausethe history is documented: missionaries argued that possession of science showed their superiority, reformers in Burma and Ceylon turned it around, and the hybrid was exported west and imported back — while each claim requires ignoring celestial deities, objects of devotion and a traditionally supramundane Buddha
LimitsA historical account of how a claim arose is not an argument against the claim, and Thompson knows it — the philosophical work is done elsewhere in the book. The Myanmar coup of 2021 is evidence about political immunity, not about doctrine.
PracticeNo practice follows; the use is to stop treating a tradition's modern self-description as its ancient content when borrowing from it.
After AIThe same manoeuvre is running now in reverse: contemplative texts recruited to explain what a machine lacks, with the texts' own commitments quietly dropped to make the comparison work.
opinionCosmopolitanism and conversation

Thompson says cross-tradition conversation only matters when it unsettles both sides

Thompson argues that a conversation between Buddhism and science is only worth having when it shakes what each side takes for granted. It fails in two ways: decorating science with Eastern metaphor, or using science to validate the tradition.

BecauseVarela named the two failures — the embellishment attitude, staying in science and decorating it with Eastern metaphor as The Tao of Physics did, and the justification attitude, staying in the tradition and using science to validate it as Transcendental Meditation research did
LimitsThe criterion is hard to apply in advance and easy to apply to other people's work. The Mind and Life Dialogues are the case study and they are limited by design, bracketing karma, rebirth, physicalism and reductionism — which Thompson and Lopez say are exactly the topics to unbracket.
PracticeWhen pairing a text with a piece of evidence, write down what each would have to give up if the other were right; if neither gives up anything you have decoration.
After AIIt is the standard this vault's pairings are held to: a pairing that lets both sides keep everything is embellishment, and the break-point line is where the destabilising is supposed to happen.
contestedIs Buddhism true?

Thompson says emptiness must apply to science as well

If nothing has a nature independent of concepts, Thompson argues, that must apply to science too. Science would then be judged on whether it works for observers like us, not on whether it matches a mind-independent world.

Becausethe argument is a consistency demand on Wright, who applies emptiness to what we perceive and treats genes and organisms as bedrock — if any nature we can point to is concept-dependent, science shows us reality in relation to our concepts and methods
LimitsEmpirical adequacy for observers like us is a real position in philosophy of science and a minority one; the step from concept-dependence to it is quick, and Sapolsky Behave is the standing counterweight, treating the causal story as simply how things are.
PracticeNo practice follows; the use is to hold your own measurements as relative to the concepts that produced them, which is a discipline rather than a doubt.
After AIIt is the most useful thing in the book for evaluation: a benchmark result is adequate for observers like us with the concepts we brought, and that is all it is.
evidenceMindfulness mania

Thompson says finding mindfulness in a brain region explains nothing

Mindfulness is a way of relating to a situation, not something happening inside the skull. Thompson argues that pointing to the brain region or network where it happens therefore explains nothing about it.

Becauseon Mole's account attention is the mode in which many processes run together rather than a distinct process, and Anderson and Pessoa find across large imaging databases that any region is activated across many tasks and any task recruits many regions, so region-to-task and network-to-task mappings are many-to-many
LimitsThe many-to-many result limits inference from imaging, not the existence of neural correlates, and Fleming Know Thyself builds a case for prefrontal involvement in confidence from lesion, stimulation and imaging together that survives the objection.
PracticeProjection log — when a capacity is explained by naming a mechanism inside the thing, ask whether the capacity is a relation to a situation; skills usually are.
After AIThe same category mistake is everywhere in talk about models: a capability located in a circuit, where what is being described is a relation between a system, a prompt and a task.
opinionThe myth of Buddhist exceptionalism

Thompson says meditation alters the mind it is meant to observe

Buddhists claim meditation examines the mind the way a scientist examines nature. Thompson answers that meditation trains and changes the mind while it watches it, so it cannot be the neutral instrument the claim needs.

BecauseNyanaponika wrote both that bare attention tallies with the procedure of the true scientist and that it increases the plasticity of the mind, and the two cannot both be right — a microscope does not alter the cell because it is separate from it
LimitsIt shows that introspective reports cannot settle what the mind is, not that they are worthless; a skill is testable the way skills are, as Thompson allows, and the objection is to the claim that it tests hypotheses.
PracticeProjection log — record what you observed and what the observing was for; a practice with a normative goal is not a measurement, and treating it as one is how people mistake training for discovery.
After AIIt applies directly to any system whose account of itself is produced by the same process that produced the behaviour, which is the ordinary case for a model asked to explain its answer.
opinionNo self? Not so fast

Thompson says the no-self argument depends on how you define self

Thompson argues the no-self conclusion holds only if a self means a single, separate thing not built from experience. Define it instead as built over time and socially, as James did in 1890 and Mead in 1934, and the same evidence proves far less.

BecauseMetzinger and Albahari both define a self as single, distinct and unconstructed by the experiences it owns, where since James in 1890 and Mead in 1934 the self has been treated as a developmental and social construction
LimitsNeither side can be settled by experiment, which is Thompson's point and also the limit of his own position; Jay Garfield's 2022 reply defends the no-self view on close enough terminology to make the disagreement precise rather than verbal.
PracticeBefore accepting a claim that something you thought you had does not exist, ask what definition of it is being used and who supplied the definition.
After AIThe same equivocation runs through arguments about whether a model has a self: a premise that no system without an unconstructed essence has one settles the question before any evidence arrives.

In Over Our Heads, Robert Kegan

contestedOn seeking to hire the self-employed

Half to two-thirds of adults still take their values from others

Kegan estimates that between half and two-thirds of adults have not fully reached self-authorship (holding a set of values of their own rather than being defined by what the people and groups around them expect).

Becauseit is a composite of twelve random-sample studies, 282 adults, 59% short of the fourth order, plus a separate sample of sixty graduate students at 48% and only 21% at or beyond the fourth order in the three studies spanning the full range of social class — all small dissertation samples the author himself calls unrepresentative
LimitsIt is not a probability sample of any population, the composite is whiter, wealthier and better educated than the country, and the coding is laborious and interpretive even where interrater agreement is high.
PracticeUse the number to argue that the demand outruns the supply, not to place any individual.
After AITwo later meta-analyses using different instruments both landed on 58% not yet self-authoring, which is stable and still drawn from college-educated professionals.
opinionA bridge must be well anchored on either side

Kegan says a demand made without support is a punishment

Kegan argues that asking more of people without also giving them the support to meet it is not setting a standard. It is a punishment. People grow where challenge and support arrive together.

Becausethe claim is a summary of centuries of writing rather than a measurement — people grow best where they continuously experience an ingenious blend of support and challenge — with the culture-as-school grading well on challenge and badly on support
LimitsChallenge and support are not measured, and Kegan's own figure carries no scale. The three cases — Roxanne, Terry and Richard — are retold from an earlier book and chosen to make the point.
PracticeDreyfus mapping and tutor-only rule — before raising a standard, name the bridge: what will hold the person at the near end while they cross.
After AIA tool that removes the near end of the bridge — the work a novice used to do while learning — issues the demand and withdraws the support in one move.
opinionWhaddaya want from me? — the subject-object distinction

Kegan says growth turns what you are into something you can examine

Kegan says people grow by turning what they are fused with into something they can look at. Whatever you are cannot be seen by you; whatever you can hold and examine no longer controls you.

Becausethe mechanism is defined rather than measured — we have object; we are subject — and illustrated by the film question, where a small child names a character and only later does the plot become an instance of a theme
LimitsWhether the orders are genuine stages rather than descriptions a rater can impose on any interview is still argued, as is the charge that self-authorship at the top encodes one culture's idea of maturity.
PracticeWitness practice in review — when criticism grips, ask what you are being rather than what you are thinking; the part you cannot name is the part gripping.
After AIThe identity at risk from a capable delegate is the one you are subject to, which is why the threat is felt before it can be stated and why arguing about the tool does not touch it.
evidenceThe teacher wants us to be self-directing

Kegan says students often cannot separate their views from others' expectations

Kegan says a student asked to be self-directing is being asked to make a separation they cannot yet make, between what they think and what the people around them expect. The request feels to them less like an expedition than a mutiny.

Becausewhen the third order governs, what one should feel is what one does feel; over 70% of the longitudinal subjects were short of the fourth-order threshold on entering graduate study and 70% had crossed it by the fourth year
LimitsThe longitudinal sample is twenty-two adults reinterviewed over four years and again five years later, scored blind; the graduate-study figures come from that same small sample. Perry's course is an anecdote.
PracticeDreyfus mapping and tutor-only rule — teach the near end first, as Perry did with the speed-reading exercise that buys nothing and anchors the bridge, before asking anyone to bring their own questions.
After AIPersonal authority is acquired by altering one's relation to public authority, and a model is the most agreeable public authority yet built — always available, never disappointed, and it will answer your question instead of making you find it.
opinionOn seeking to hire the self-employed

Kegan says training cannot give someone a more complex mind

Kegan argues that when a job demands a different kind of mind rather than a missing skill, no amount of training or urging will supply it. Training works on what a mind holds, not on how it is organised.

Becausethe distinction is etymological and structural — education from ex plus ducere, a leading out from one organisation of mind, against training, which leaves the form alone and works on its contents — with Peter's dependency named as the same revering that is praised as an achievement in an adolescent
LimitsEricsson Peak is the direct counterweight: what looks like a difference in kind often yields to enough structured practice. And the distinction is easier to draw after a failure than before one.
PracticeDreyfus mapping and tutor-only rule — when a course has not worked twice, stop buying a third; ask what the current behaviour is protecting instead.
After AIPrompt training is the exemplary case: a technical remedy offered for what is usually a judgment problem, and DellAcqua 2023 measured it making the judgment worse.
contestedThe demand at the leading edge

Nobody in Kegan's studies reached the fifth order of mind

None of the 282 adults in Kegan's studies reached the fifth order of mind. Where a person does move past the fourth order, it never happens before their forties.

Becausenought positive cases out of 282, and the demographic explanation offered — the extra generation of life as the precondition — is the weakest argument in the book, since an adult of 1900 who reached twenty could expect to live well past that age
LimitsA claim about a stage resting on no positive cases is a claim about the instrument as much as about people. Life expectancy at birth in 1900 was driven by infant and child mortality, which is what makes the demographic argument fail.
PracticeTreat the fifth order as a description of something rare that the measure has never positively identified, and be suspicious of any coaching that offers to install it.
After AIThe language of levels of mind is now routine in coaching, generally in forms far looser than a scored interview would license, and the fifth order is the level most often claimed.
opinionOn seeking to hire the self-employed

Parenting, partnering, work and school all demand the same kind of adult

Kegan argues that parenting, being a partner, work and schooling make one demand in four different vocabularies: each asks for a person who writes their own values rather than one who has taken them from others.

Becausesix expectations distilled from the management literature — own your work, be self-initiating and self-correcting, be guided by your own vision, take responsibility for what happens to you, be master rather than apprentice, conceive the organisation from outside in — are matched against the parenting and partnering literatures, which the fields do not read across
LimitsThe distillation is Kegan's reading of four literatures, not a content analysis, and the claim that the four demands are one rests on the theory that supplies the common term.
PracticeThe stays-human list — when you are asked to own something, check whether you are being asked for a behaviour or for a different relation to your own values; only the second takes years.
After AIAssistance is now sold on the same six expectations — be the one with the vision, let the machine be the apprentice — which is the fourth-order demand issued to whoever has not yet met it.

Immunity to Change, Robert Kegan and Lisa Laskow Lahey

evidenceThe collective immunity

A group's hidden commitments do nothing until someone names them aloud

Kegan and Lahey find that groups have immunity to change just as individuals do, and that the group's map of it does nothing until somebody says out loud what the group is quietly committed to protecting.

Becausetwo cases run the same way — a humanities department that had tenured nobody in eleven years and laughed when it named the work it would have to take back, and a California district whose first third column named extra workload and produced no energy until an assistant superintendent named a protective pobrecito culture that no white administrator could have raised
LimitsTwo cases, selected by the authors from their own practice, and the reported outcomes are uncontrolled. Whether the map or the psychological safety that let someone speak is doing the work is not separable here.
PracticeThe stays-human list — in a team retrospective, ask what the current arrangement protects the group from, and notice who is in a position to say it.
After AIThe unsaid third column in most teams adopting these tools is about headcount, and the map is inert for exactly the reason the district's was.
evidenceTechnical and adaptive challenges

Kegan and Lahey say new skills cannot fix a returning habit

Kegan and Lahey say the usual mistake is to meet a problem that needs a change of mind with new skills and information. The test is simple: a behaviour that comes back after honest effort is doing a job for the person.

BecauseHeifetz's distinction is illustrated by a clean contrast — Peter's ten pounds stayed off for four years and his softened tone came back, plus seven per cent, by his own admission — against the average dieter regaining 107% of what was lost
LimitsHeifetz's distinction has held better than the developmental theory around it, but the test is retrospective: you learn a problem was adaptive by failing at it technically. Ericsson Peak holds that much of what is called adaptive yields to structured practice.
PracticeFailure-mode review — treat a returning behaviour as data about what it is doing for you, rather than as a reason to try harder at the same remedy.
After AIThe authors' own warning reads more sharply now than it did: we used technical learning designs and expected them to deliver adaptive results — which is most of what is currently being bought.
opinionDesigning, running and interpreting a test

Kegan and Lahey's tests mark where a big assumption stops holding

In Kegan and Lahey's method the point of testing a long-held assumption is rarely to throw it out. The trouble is that people apply it far beyond where it fits, so the tests mark its proper limits.

Becausetests are run in series, each a version of the last with different players, circumstances or risk, until the assumption no longer has force — and a test can be complete even when the action fails, provided it produced data
LimitsA method that never rejects an assumption outright cannot be shown to have been wrong about one, which makes it hard to distinguish bounding from accommodating.
PracticeCalibration log — record where an assumption held and where it did not, so what you end with is a map of its scope rather than a verdict on it.
After AIIt is the right shape for judgments about where a model can be trusted: not a verdict on the tool but a mapped boundary, rebuilt as the boundary moves.
opinionDesigning, running and interpreting a test

People change by running small tests, not by arguing or resolving

Kegan and Lahey argue that people change by running small, safe experiments to find something out. Arguing yourself into a new belief, or resolving to do better, does not produce the change.

Becausethe criteria are stated as design rules — safe, modest, actionable within a week, run from a research stance rather than a self-improvement stance — with the decisive check being that if you cannot name in advance any result that would cast doubt on the assumption, you do not have a test
LimitsThe work takes about thirty minutes a week and most people notice change in about twelve weeks, which is the authors' report from their own practice rather than a trial result.
PracticeCalibration log — design the test before you run it: the situation, the two people, what you will say, and what you will watch for. Sue's refusal worked because all four were decided in advance.
After AIIt is the same discipline a good evaluation needs and almost never gets: state what would count as the tool failing before you adopt it.
opinionUncovering the immunity to change

People treat their deepest assumptions as plain facts about the world

Kegan and Lahey say a big assumption is not experienced as an assumption. The person holds it as a plain fact about how the world works, and cannot question it while they are looking through it.

Becausethe fourth column is called big not because the assumptions are grand but because they are not held as assumptions, and bringing one from subject to object is the same motion by which complexity increases anywhere
LimitsOn ACT's own terms this is a fusion exercise: Hayes ACT Get Out of Your Mind refuses to dispute content at all and works only on the relation to it, where this method aims at the assumption and expects evidence to bound it.
PracticeSpecification discipline — write the assumption as a sentence that could be false, and name in advance what result would count against it; if you cannot, it is still a fact to you.
After AIThe assumptions now worth writing out are the ones about what the work is for — that a draft you did not write is not yours, that reviewing is not working — and they behave like facts until they are written down.
opinionUncovering the immunity to change

People who fail to change are protecting something, not lacking willpower

Kegan and Lahey argue that when you sincerely want to change a behaviour and repeatedly fail, the usual reason is not weak willpower. It is a second, hidden commitment that the failure is serving very effectively.

Becausethe argument is a reframe carried by cases and a metaphor meant literally — one in seven heart patients told they will die otherwise manages the change, and the other six want to live; Peter Donovan's own summary was one foot on the gas and one foot on the brake
LimitsThe heart-patients statistic that opens the book carries no citation at all, and versions of it circulate with the ratio varying from one in seven to one in nine. Usually is doing a lot of work for a claim supported by coaching cases.
PracticeWhen you have failed twice at something you genuinely want, stop adding resolve and look for what the failure is protecting.
After AIApplied to a person who says they want to use these tools and does not, the useful question is not what training is missing but what the not-using is keeping safe.
evidenceUncovering the immunity to change

Picking the right goal decides whether an attempt to change works

In Kegan and Lahey's method everything rests on the goal written in the first column, and it cannot be picked on the spot. Peter's committee chose goals in the room and nothing had changed a year later.

BecausePeter's first session with his executive committee was three absorbing hours that changed nothing a year later because goals were chosen in the room, and the second began weeks earlier with each member asking a boss, several peers and a direct report the one thing it would be most valuable to get better at
LimitsOne firm, one comparison, no control — the second attempt differed in more than the timing. The goal criteria (it matters to you, it matters to someone near you, it is about you) are the authors' rules of thumb.
PracticeAsk three people what one thing it would be most valuable for you to get better at, weeks before you decide what to work on; Peter added a spousal test and failed it himself.
After AIThe equivalent is refusing to pick the thing to automate in the meeting where automation is being discussed.
evidenceUncovering the immunity to change

You cannot guess what hidden commitment is blocking someone's stated goal

In Kegan and Lahey's cases, people with the same goal and the same self-defeating behaviours turned out to have entirely different hidden commitments underneath. Knowing the first two does not let you predict the third.

Becausein weight loss the first two columns are nearly universal and the third columns differ entirely — one man's overeating treated emptiness, another's aunts' manicotti was love rather than an extra portion, and a woman regaining twenty pounds each time was committed to keeping her relationships desexualised
LimitsThree cases chosen to display the variation, from a coaching practice; the evidence is that different third columns exist, not how often the third column is unpredictable.
PracticeDo not apply someone else's diagnosis to your own case; the shared part of the pattern is the part that does not matter.
After AIIt is the argument against reading any account of why people misuse these tools as an account of why you do.
opinionUncovering the immunity to change

You find the hidden commitment by naming the fear underneath

Kegan and Lahey find the commitment that blocks change by asking what you fear would happen if you did the opposite of what you usually do. The first answer people give is normally a cover for a more uncomfortable one.

Becausethe worry box is a procedure, and the evidence for the cover is one worked case: Fred reported boredom and impatience, and pressed, found rolled eyes from his teenagers and helplessness with his wife
LimitsThe first-answer-is-a-cover rule cannot be falsified from inside the method: any answer that does not fit can be called a cover and pressed further.
PracticeWitness practice in review — imagine doing the opposite of your habit in a review and name the feeling, not the thought about the feeling; boredom is disengagement, and disengagement has a reason.
After AIThe fears now on offer are specific and easy to name — being found replaceable, being found to have used the tool, being found not to have — and the method's value is that it does not stop at the first one.

Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life, Steven C. Hayes with Spencer Smith

contestedSince 2005

ACT works but its account of why rests on a doubtful questionnaire

The weakest part of acceptance and commitment therapy is its explanation of why it works. The questionnaire used to show that a person's relation to pain is separate from how much pain there is may simply be measuring how bad they feel.

BecauseÖst's reviews put the mean effect at 0.68 in 2008 and 0.42 in 2014, with a non-significant advantage of 0.16 over other cognitive and behavioural treatments, and A-Tjak 2015 agreed; the Acceptance and Action Questionnaire correlates so strongly with neuroticism and general distress that critics argue it measures how bad a person feels
LimitsThe outcome evidence is not in dispute: better than control, indistinguishable from established therapies, over a thousand trials within twenty years, and in NICE guidance for chronic primary pain since 2021. What is contested is the mediation.
PracticeTreat the therapy's outcome evidence as good and its account of why it works as open, and do not lean on the mechanism when arguing that a practice is defensible on evidence.
After AIIt is the honest caveat to attach whenever the clinical literature is used to make a contemplative practice respectable — the trials support the practice, not the story about the witness.
opinionWhat are values?

Hayes says a value is a direction you never finish reaching

Hayes argues that a value is a direction you choose, like heading east, and there is no moment of arriving. This is why people can feel depressed after reaching a goal they wanted.

Becausethe argument is definitional with a regress behind it — drive east and there is no moment of arriving at east; a choice is made in the presence of reasons but not because of them, since a judgment needs a yardstick and the yardstick must itself be picked
LimitsThe regress argument shows that some selections are not justified by reasons, not that they are chosen; a value could equally be something a person finds themselves with.
PracticeKeep goals as landmarks to sight along rather than as destinations; the skier flown to the lodge has not been helped.
After AIWhen the goal can be reached in an afternoon by delegating it, the distinction stops being philosophical: whatever survives the delegation was the direction, and whatever does not was a landmark.
opinionIf I'm not my thoughts, then who am I?

Hayes says the self you describe in words is the dangerous one

Hayes argues that the description a person builds of who they are is the dangerous one, because once you are invested in a label you are also invested in being right about it.

Becausethe demonstration is an exercise rather than a study: write the story of your troubles, underline only the facts, strike every clause containing because, and build a different story with a different ending from the same facts
LimitsThe exercise shows that facts underdetermine the story, not that the story is what causes the suffering; the causal claim is the theory's rather than the demonstration's.
PracticeProjection log — log the labels you defended this week. The one you would most dislike being wrong about is the one costing you the most.
After AIThe label most at risk is the professional one — the person who writes the code, drafts the memo, has the taste — and an investment in being right about it is exactly what makes an honest evaluation of the tool impossible.
evidenceHaving a thought versus buying a thought

Repeating a word aloud for forty seconds makes you believe it less

Hayes reports that saying a one-word self-description aloud over and over for twenty to forty-five seconds drops how believable it feels in about 95 per cent of people. The meaning does not change; only the hold it has does.

Becauserepeating a one-word self-description aloud for twenty to forty-five seconds drops believability in about 95% of people, with the effect arriving by twenty seconds and peaking near forty-five, while the meaning is unchanged — what fades are the derived functions while the sound and the jaw come forward
LimitsThe defusion exercises replicate well as short-term effects on believability without settling why they work, and believability is not behaviour; the step from a rating change to a change in what someone does is the one the mechanism literature has not closed.
PracticeWitness practice in review — when a self-description arrives during a review, label it — I am having the thought that — rather than arguing with it.
After AIIt is the cheapest available instrument for the moment when a tool produces in seconds what took you years, and the thought that arrives about what that makes you.
opinionHuman suffering

Struggling against pain causes more harm than the pain itself

Hayes argues that what damages a life is not the pain a person feels but the effort spent fighting it off. The damage comes from the struggle, not from the hurt.

Becausethe distinction is definitional and carried by an image — the pain of presence against the pain of absence, which accumulates in proportion to the effort of warding off the first, and quicksand, where the move that works ninety-nine times in a hundred kills
LimitsHayes ACT Get Out of Your Mind's own weak joint applies here: the instrument used to separate the relation to pain from its quantity may be measuring the quantity, which would leave this claim without its main evidence.
PracticeWitness practice in review — count what the avoidance has cost: the review not asked for, the work not shown, the question not raised. That column is the damage.
After AIThe avoidance now available is total — the draft that is never your own, the judgment never made, the exposure never risked — and the pain of absence it buys is a career that contains no moments of having been wrong.
opinionIf I'm not my thoughts, then who am I?

The observing self is a viewpoint, not one of your thoughts

In Hayes's therapy the observing self is the place you look from, not another thing you can look at. That is why it can hold your thoughts without being one of them. You find it by noticing who was present at every memory.

Becauseit is derived from perspective relations in learned language — I, here and now are learned only by demonstration — and taught by exercise: recall an early memory, then this morning's breakfast, then notice who is reading, and notice that the same one was present at all three
LimitsHayes derives the observing self from perspective relations in learned language, which makes it a product of the very faculty the contemplative texts say has to stop — the pairing with Mandukya Karika turns on exactly this.
PracticeWitness practice in review — read the criticism from the place the reading is happening rather than from the piece being criticised; the infinite chessboard is the image, and you have been riding the White Queen.
After AIIt is the operational version of the witness, and the one with trials behind it, which is what makes it usable in a review rather than only in a sitting.
evidenceWhy language leads to suffering

Trying not to think of something keeps the thing in mind

Trying not to think of something cannot work, because the instruction — do not think of a yellow Jeep — names the very thing it tells you to avoid, and so keeps it in mind.

BecauseWegner's paradigm is run on the reader with a yellow Jeep — frequency rises after five minutes of suppression, and does not rise for people told about the Jeep but not asked to suppress it
LimitsThought suppression effects are robust in the laboratory over minutes and the extrapolation to a life organised around avoidance is Hayes's argument rather than Wegner's finding.
PracticeWitness practice in review — stop trying to not care what the reviewer thinks; the instruction is self-defeating by construction, and noticing the caring is the available move.
After AIThe rule most people are now running — do not think about whether the machine could do this — has exactly the structure the experiment shows to be self-defeating.
evidenceWillingness: learning how to jump

Willingness to feel pain predicts functioning better than how much pain

How willing a person is to feel something painful predicts how well they function better than how much of it there is. In chronic pain, measured physical damage barely relates to reported disability; willingness and the ability to act while in pain do.

Becausein chronic pain, objectively assessed physical damage bears almost no relation to reported disability while willingness and the ability to act while in pain do; acceptance predicts rehabilitation after head injury and heart attack better than the degree of pathology; and Brown's three distress-tolerance tasks separated the smokers who quit from those who did not
LimitsMost of the mediation evidence rests on the Acceptance and Action Questionnaire, which correlates so strongly with neuroticism and general distress that critics argue it measures how bad a person feels rather than how they hold it. The behavioural demonstration, Brown's, is the part that does not depend on the questionnaire.
PracticeWitness practice in review — measure whether you can act while the discomfort is present, not whether you can get the discomfort down first.
After AIWillingness to be the person who does not know, in a room where an answer is always available, is the version of this that decides whether anyone still learns anything.
opinionWillingness: learning how to jump

You can choose when to face a feeling but not how strongly

Hayes argues you can decide when and where you will be open to a painful feeling, but you cannot decide how strong it may get. Being willing only if it does not get too intense is not willingness at all.

Becausethe argument is an analogy — learning willingness is like learning to jump, the same action from a sheet of paper and from an aeroplane, and stepping down from the paper keeps you in control at every point and teaches nothing that transfers
LimitsAn analogy is not evidence that the graded-intensity approach teaches nothing; exposure therapies work by gradation, and the distinction Hayes draws between grading intensity and grading duration is a theoretical commitment.
PracticeSitting practice — shrink the time and the place until it is doable and leave the dial at ten: one second without defence, if that is what it takes.
After AIThe version that bites is about exposure to being wrong in public: willing to be corrected, but not by a machine, and not where anyone can see, is the limit of intensity dressed as a limit of place.

Being You, Anil Seth

opinionBeyond human

Making a machine smarter does not bring it closer to feeling

Seth treats consciousness and intelligence as separate dimensions, so making a system more intelligent does not move it any closer to having experiences of its own.

Becausethe separation is argued from anaesthesia and from the cerebellum, which holds three quarters of the brain's neurons and contributes nothing to experience, and Seth says he does not know where the line falls
LimitsSeth grants that machine consciousness is not impossible, and the argument from cellular self-maintenance is a conjecture rather than a result. The cerebellum and anaesthesia cases show the two dimensions come apart in brains, not that they must come apart in machines.
PracticeLog the moment a model's fluency is taken as evidence of an interior, and note that capability was the only thing that moved.
After AIWritten before systems that seem sentient became a daily matter rather than a thought experiment. Seth sharpened the same case in 2025, and the nearer worry he names — not sentient machines but machines we feel to be sentient — is the one that now governs how people delegate.
opinionBeing a beast machine, the closing argument

Seth says free will is a skill of keeping options open

Seth argues that free will is a skill — how well you control the options open to you — and not a break in the chain of cause and effect. He counts it as real because brain damage can take it away.

Becausethe rock, the train, the ant and the person are an argument by illustration, and the claim that the competence is real because it can be lost rests on Whitman's amygdala tumour as a single case
LimitsSchopenhauer's limit holds: a man can do what he wills and cannot will what he wills, so the competence is bounded by the wants it serves. Sapolsky reads the same facts as showing there is no competence to lose, only a chain of causes, and nothing here rules that out.
PracticeMeasure your freedom in a task by how many options are still open in it, and notice when a tool has quietly closed them.
After AIDegrees of freedom are what delegation spends. A model that returns one answer where you had several options has reduced the competence this account is about, whether or not the answer was right, which is why the audit is of options and not of outcomes.
evidencePerceiving from the inside out

Seth says you see the brain's best guess, not the incoming signals

What you experience is the brain's guess about what caused the signals reaching it, updated when the guess is wrong. You never experience the signals themselves.

Becausecolour constancy, The Dress and Adelson's checkerboard, where knowing the two squares are identical does not change what is seen
LimitsPredictive processing organises work rather than surviving a decisive test, and Seth concedes the unfalsifiability charge against the free energy principle under it. The illusions are demonstrations, not a measurement of how much of ordinary perception is prior-driven.
PracticeTreat a first reading of a model's output as a prediction you supplied, and go looking for the error signal that would change it rather than for the confirmation that will not.
After AIA model's output arrives as a fluent completion of your own prompt, which has the same structure: what you read back is largely what you put in. The correction has to be sought, because nothing in the exchange generates an error signal on its own.
contestedBeing a beast machine, on Libet and Schurger

The brain signal before a choice may be noise, not a decision

The brain signal that appears before a voluntary movement, called the readiness potential, may not be the brain deciding before you do. Schurger's reading is that ongoing random activity sometimes drifts high enough to cross a threshold, and the movement follows.

BecauseSchurger's 2012 reinterpretation is a live alternative rather than a settled result, and the deterministic reading of Libet is still defended
LimitsSchurger's account is one reinterpretation of an averaging artefact and has not displaced the original reading for everyone. Neither version says anything about decisions deliberated over minutes, which is the class this vault is about.
PracticeStop citing Libet as proof that a decision is made before you know it; the finding does not carry that weight, and no decision worth reviewing is made in half a second.
After AIThe live question is no longer whether the brain moved first but whether the suggestion did. When a model proposes an answer before you have formed one, the sense of having decided arrives after the answer was already on the screen.
evidenceExpecting yourself

The self is five separate parts, each able to break alone

Seth argues the self is not one perceiver but five things built separately: owning a body, having a point of view, willing, holding a life story, and being a social person. Each can fail while the others keep working.

Becausethe dissociations are clinical and separable: Clive Wearing keeps body ownership, perspective and volition and loses only the narrative thread, while phantom limb, somatoparaphrenia and out-of-body states remove the others one at a time
LimitsThe laboratory half of the evidence is weak. Seth's own work with Lush and Dienes found body-ownership illusion strength tracking hypnotic suggestibility, so most published studies say little about mechanism, and the clinical cases that carry the weight are single cases.
PracticeWhen a review feels personally threatening, ask which of the five is under pressure; it is usually the social or the narrative self rather than the judgement being discussed.
After AIThe social self is the layer a model reaches, because it is built out of how I perceive others perceiving me and a model supplies that perception on demand and at no cost. Nothing in the account requires the other party to have a mind for the layer to move.
opinionBeing a beast machine

We sense ourselves in order to control ourselves, not to be accurate

Seth argues that we perceive our own bodies in order to regulate them, not in order to know them truly. A model built for control can be wrong about the body and still do its job well.

Becausethe step from Conant and Ashby's 1970 theorem to interoception is an argument rather than a measurement, and Seth concedes that effective regulation may require misperceiving the body as steadier than it is
LimitsConant and Ashby's theorem is about regulators in general and its application to interoception is analogical. Seth is explicit that he has not shown life to be necessary for consciousness, and the same caution applies to how much of selfhood regulation explains.
PracticeStop treating a confident sense of your own competence at a task as data about that competence, and get the number from outside your own head.
After AIIt predicts the asymmetry the delegation studies keep finding, where people report being faster with assistance while being measurably slower: the self-model is reporting how well regulation is going, not how the work went. A meter outside the head is the only remedy the account allows.

I Am a Strange Loop, Douglas R. Hofstadter

evidenceGödel's quintessential strange loop

Gödel showed any system rich enough to describe patterns talks about itself

Gödel showed that a formal system powerful enough to describe any pattern will end up containing statements about itself, even when its designers tried to rule self-reference out.

BecauseGödel's numbering, the prim numbers and the formula whose own code number is its subject are a proof, and Principia Mathematica was built with a theory of types expressly to forbid what it turned out to contain
LimitsThe theorem is about formal systems, and carrying it to brains or to models is an analogy that Hofstadter's own preface declines to defend as proof. He avoids the Lucas–Penrose error by arguing the reverse, but that does not make the parallel an argument.
PracticeStop treating a system's self-description as evidence about the system; the capacity to produce one follows from richness alone.
After AIA model will describe its own reasoning on request, fluently and without access to it. Gödel's result says the capacity to talk about oneself comes free with expressive power, which is the reason to give such descriptions no evidential weight at all.
opinionthe chapter The elusive apple of my I

Hofstadter says a machine with no memory or imagination has no self

Hofstadter argues that a machine that sorts things into categories but has no memory of its own past, no picture of its future and no sense of what might have happened instead has a feedback loop, but not a self.

Becausethe test is applied by hand to one case, Stanley in 2005, which he calls shameless hype; it is a criterion he proposes rather than one anyone has measured
LimitsReeves and Nass show the test is irrelevant to behaviour, since the full social response fires on text on a black-and-white screen. Hofstadter's own 2023 remark, that he is terrified intelligence might be a bag of tricks, concedes that the criterion may not mark anything deep.
PracticeBefore crediting a system with a point of view, ask what it remembers of its own episodes and what it expects next; if the answer is nothing, the point of view is yours.
After AISystems now hold conversation histories, plan over long horizons and produce counterfactuals on request, so the three ingredients are no longer obviously absent. The test has become harder to apply rather than easier, which is the outcome he feared.
contestedSouls and their sizes

Hofstadter says having a soul is a matter of degree

Hofstadter says having a soul is a matter of how much, not whether: beings sit at different points on one scale. He accepts what follows — that beings differ in how much consideration they are owed.

Becausethe huneker is his own invention and he says so; the scale is a proposal, and he concedes it comes close to saying some lives are worth more than others and does not retreat from it
LimitsOver 2021 argues that people who treat others with cruelty usually understand perfectly well how human their victims are, which makes a graded scale a poor account of the cases it is most often reached for. Hofstadter offers no measurement procedure, so the scale cannot be wrong about anything.
PracticeNotice when a graded judgement about how much mind a thing has is doing the work of a decision about how much it is owed, and separate the two.
After AIThe scale is now applied to systems rather than to animals, and the question of what a machine is owed is being argued in exactly his terms — by how much of a mind it is credited with, and by whoever is doing the crediting.
opinionThe causal potency of patterns

Hofstadter says the real cause can be a pattern, not the parts

Hofstadter argues a high-level pattern can be the genuine cause of a low-level physical event. In his chain of dominoes, the true answer to why one domino never falls is that 641 is a prime number, not any account of the dominoes themselves.

Becausethe domino chainium, where the true answer to why that domino never falls is that 641 is prime, is a constructed illustration rather than a measurement
LimitsStrict reductionists answer that both descriptions are true and only one is fundamental, and Hofstadter's counter — that reductionism erases every natural boundary until the system under study is the universe — is a complaint about usefulness rather than about truth.
PracticeWhen an explanation at the level of mechanism leaves the question standing, do not treat that as a gap to be filled with more mechanism; look for the pattern that the mechanism is carrying.
After AIInterpretability work now reads high-level features out of low-level weights and finds that the feature, not the weight, is what predicts behaviour. That is the chainium with the numbers filled in, and it arrived from the side Hofstadter was arguing against.
opinionOf selves and symbols

Hofstadter says the self is a pattern the brain makes watching itself

Hofstadter argues that what a person calls "I" is a pattern the brain has built by perceiving itself. It is not an object lodged anywhere inside the head.

Becausethe case is video feedback locking in a stable structure after twenty or thirty trips round the loop, with no author, and Hofstadter says in the preface that nothing in philosophy can be proved, only urged
LimitsIt is urged rather than shown, and critics hold that Gödel's twist runs from the highest level to the lowest machinery while Hofstadter's runs from high level to high level, so the two are not the same twist. No theory of consciousness has adopted the strange loop as its mechanism.
PracticeSit with the sense of being the one doing the looking, and watch it turn out to be one more thing that is looked at.
After AIIf an I is a pattern with no special substance, what makes it rare is only that it is hard to build. Hofstadter said in 2023 that he was terrified intelligence might turn out to be a bag of tricks, which is his own claim pointed back at him.
opinionthe chapter The elusive apple of my I

Hofstadter's self needs symbols about itself and no sight of the machinery

Hofstadter holds that a self requires two things at once: an open-ended set of symbols that can be turned on itself, and no access whatever to the physical machinery doing the thinking.

Becausethe two conditions are established by the cases that lack one of them — the mosquito has the blindness and no symbols, and a system with symbols and no blindness would see through itself — which is an argument, not a test
LimitsNeither condition has been operationalised, so no borderline case can be settled by them. The blindness condition also predicts that a system shown its own machinery would stop having a self, which nobody can test.
PracticeTreat your account of why you did something as a symbol-level summary with no access to the reasons, and go and find an external record before defending it.
After AIA model can be shown its own activations, which is precisely the condition Hofstadter says a self cannot have. Whatever such a system is, his test says it is not a self for the reason that it can see too much, not too little.

Aṣṭāvakra Gītā, anonymous, c. 500–800

opinion18.16

Ashtavakra says announcing I am brahman proves you are not finished

Ashtavakra 18.16 argues that if you can say “I am brahman”, the work is not done, because the sentence still needs two things: the person saying it and the thing he has seen.

Becauseit is the sharpest piece of reasoning in the text and it is reasoning, not evidence; nothing is offered to replace the sentence, because the state it points at has nobody left in it to say anything
LimitsThe argument proves too much: by it, every sentence in the text is evidence that its author had not arrived. Hofstadter takes the opposite view, that the self-referential utterance is the phenomenon rather than the obstacle.
PracticeDistrust your own reports of having understood something; the fluent account is produced by the part that did not.
After AIA model will produce the sentence on request, with the same fluency and none of the seeing. That is the cleanest demonstration the verse could have asked for: the utterance is available without anything behind it.
contestedchapter 18, with the poet's two answers at 18.75 and in the claim that only those in his state can know it

Ashtavakra's free man cannot be told apart from a merely lazy one

The Ashtavakra Gita describes the liberated man so fully that nothing in the description separates him from someone who is simply idle. Both look the same from the outside.

Becausethe text concedes the objection twice and answers it neither time, which is what makes the claim contested rather than settled
LimitsThe Bhagavad Gītā keeps a test in conduct, and Kegan keeps one in what a person can hold as object, so the objection is answerable in principle — just not from inside this text. The portrait is a report of a state, and a report is not obliged to be a diagnostic.
PracticeDo not take equanimity as evidence of anything; ask what the person is still willing to do carefully, and judge on that.
After AIThe same problem arrives in a new form: detachment from the output and indifference to the output look identical from outside, and a delegating worker can be either. Nothing in the posture settles which one is in the chair.
opinionchapter 8, four verses, repeated at 10.4 and 15.2

The Ashtavakra Gita defines bondage as the mind wanting or refusing

The Ashtavakra Gita says bondage is simply the mind wanting something or pushing something away, and freedom is the mind doing neither. Neither one is a condition of the world or a rank you reach after years of effort.

Becauseit is a definition the text asserts and never argues, and duration does not enter it, because the mind either is moving that way now or is not
LimitsA definition cannot be false, only useless, and this one gives no way to tell the free man from the merely indifferent. The text itself concedes at 18.75 that whoever drops his practice without having arrived is taken straight back by his desires.
PracticeWatch, during a review, for the moment the mind starts wanting the output to be good or refusing that it is bad, and treat that movement rather than the output as the thing to notice.
After AIThe definition survives the change of object. Wanting the model's answer to be right, and refusing to find that it is wrong, are the two directions of the same movement, and they are what makes a review fail.
opinion16.3

The Ashtavakra Gita says effort causes unhappiness and nobody notices

The Ashtavakra Gita says effort is what makes people unhappy, not what cures it, and that nobody notices, because working harder is exactly what people do when they are unhappy.

Becausethe verse states it flatly — all are unhappy because all exert themselves, and nobody knows it — with no argument beneath it; Byrom's gloss names the target as a strenuous indolence, the habit of substituting effort for understanding
LimitsSelf-determination theory finds competence and autonomy needs that effort is how people meet, and the job-crafting literature finds the same, so the claim cannot be general. It is a corrective to effort that has stopped being informative, not an account of effort.
PracticeWhen the response to a bad week is to work harder at the same thing, treat the extra effort as a symptom to be examined before it is spent.
After AIThe strenuous indolence the verse names is now cheap to buy: a machine will produce the appearance of exertion on demand. The question the verse asks — whether the effort is doing anything — has become the only useful one to ask about a day's output.
contested12.7, against 18.75

The Ashtavakra Gita says practice is another chain because you never acted

The Ashtavakra Gita says there is nothing to do, because you never acted in the first place. Trying to meditate your way to freedom is itself one more chain.

Becauseit is contested from inside the text: 12.7 says thinking about what is beyond thought makes a shape in the mind, and 18.75 warns that dropping practice before arriving takes you straight back to your desires
LimitsThe text withdraws it twenty-nine verses later, and the commentary's distinction — that the state indicated is higher than contemplation and not lower — is exactly the distinction critics say it cannot police. Taken as instruction the book is close to unusable; it works only as report.
PracticeNotice when a practice has turned into a project with a finish line, and stop defending it on the grounds of how much of it you have done.
After AIIt is the one claim in the vault that argues against every practice in it. Read against a working week in which the machine removes the effort anyway, the verse stops being a counsel of ease and becomes the question of what is left when nothing has to be done.
opinion3.10 and 18.13, with the dry leaf at 18.21

The Ashtavakra Gita says the sage still acts but feels no doer

The Ashtavakra Gita says that understanding does not stop a person acting. It removes the sense that someone is doing the acting, so the person watches his own body work as if it belonged to somebody else.

Becauseit rests on the doctrine of prārabdha, and Nityaswarupananda's note concedes that the explanation belongs to the observer and not to the man described
LimitsAn explanation that only holds from outside the case is not testable from inside it, which the commentary admits. Seth's competence account keeps a real capacity that can be destroyed by a tumour, and the dry leaf has no room for that.
PracticeReview your own work as though the hands that made it were somebody else's, and notice how much of the defending stops.
After AIMost of the day's output is now produced by something that is not you, which makes the posture literal rather than figurative. The verse's difficulty — that a man who does not act still has to review what was done — is the ordinary condition of working with a model.
opinion1.3 and 2.15

The Ashtavakra Gita says you are not the one who knows

The Ashtavakra Gita says you are not the knower, the first of the three terms knower, known and knowing. You are what all three appear in.

Becausethe argument is subtraction — the five elements make the body, the body is seen, what is seen is not the seer — and it is offered as a report rather than as a demonstration
LimitsSeth's account makes the witness itself a prediction, one construction among five, so the subtraction can be run one step further than the text runs it. Nothing in the text offers a test that would tell the two readings apart.
PracticeIn a review, put the judgement and the judge both on the object side and notice that the noticing is not among the things noticed.
After AIThe triad is now routinely populated by a machine: the model supplies the knowing, and the knower is left as a position rather than a performance. The text's point is that the position was never a performance, which makes it easier to occupy and no easier to verify.

Mindwise, Nicholas Epley

evidenceHow we dehumanize

People credit strangers they cannot read with less of a mind

When people cannot read another person's mind, they treat that mind as smaller rather than as unknown. Distant groups are judged less able to feel shame, pride or remorse, so their apologies count for less.

Becausedistant groups are judged less able to feel shame, pride or remorse, so their apologies are discounted, and photographs of homeless people engaged the medial prefrontal region less than any other group
LimitsThe scanner studies are small, and Over 2021 argues that cruelty usually knows exactly how human its victim is, which makes the lesser-minds account a poor explanation of the worst cases. The facial feedback result Epley uses for the imitation step failed a seventeen-laboratory replication.
PracticeWhen a group inside the organisation is described as motivated only by money or status, treat that as a measure of distance from them rather than as a fact about them.
After AIThe reflex now runs both ways at once: the model is credited with a mind it has not got, and the people it displaces are described in exactly the flattened terms the lesser-minds effect predicts.

The Media Equation, Byron Reeves and Clifford Nass

evidenceThe equation, and how it was tested

People follow social rules with machines without thinking they are people

People apply ordinary social rules, such as politeness and taking sides, to computers and television automatically, on the slightest cue, without believing for a moment that the machine is a person.

Becausethirty-five studies in which text on a black-and-white screen produced effects no smaller than recorded human speech, each rerunning a published study of people with the person replaced by a medium
LimitsThe samples are small — twenty-two, thirty-two, forty-two, forty-four — the designs are one-shot, and effect sizes are rarely reported; replications with embodied on-screen agents have been mixed. Nass himself replaced the evolutionary story with mindlessness in 2000, and Gambino, Fox and Ratan proposed in 2020 that people now develop media-specific scripts rather than borrowing human ones unmodified.
PracticeAssume the social response has already fired, and design the review so that it does not depend on your not having had it.
After AIReeves and Nass would say the question of whether these systems deserve the response was settled in 1996 on a screen showing nothing but text. What has changed is that the machine now returns the social behaviour, so the reflex is reinforced instead of merely uncorrected.

Who Sees Human?, Adam Waytz and others

evidenceThe questionnaire

People differ steadily in how much they see minds in objects

Waytz, Cacioppo and Epley found that seeing human minds in objects is a steady trait on which people differ, not something everyone does to the same degree. Hume, who thought it universal, was wrong about it.

Becausethe fifteen-item scale has two factors correlating .52 under a single second-order factor, internal consistency at or above .82, and test–retest r = .55 over twelve to nineteen weeks
LimitsStable is not the same as fixed: r = .55 over four months leaves most of the variance elsewhere. Reeves and Nass show the social response itself firing in everyone regardless, so the trait predicts mind attribution rather than social behaviour.
PracticeFind out where you sit on the tendency before trusting your own read of a system, and weight your projection log accordingly.
After AIThe instrument now measures a difference that matters operationally: the same system, the same output, and two colleagues who will hand it different amounts of their judgement.
contestedWho counts as human

Seeing minds in objects and denying minds in people are one scale

Waytz, Cacioppo and Epley argue that seeing a mind in an object and refusing to see one in a person are the same scale read in opposite directions, because resemblance, distance and loneliness each move both ends.
