Becauseresemblance, distance and loneliness each move both ends, and Over 2021 contested it in the same journal, arguing that people who treat others with cruelty usually understand perfectly well how human their victims are
LimitsOver's objection is unanswered: if cruelty knows what its victim is, mind attribution is a poor account of atrocity and the dimension does not run as far as the authors take it. Epley also insists the two errors are not morally symmetrical, which a single dimension cannot represent.
PracticeTreat generosity toward a machine and dismissiveness toward a distant colleague as one reading on one dial, and take them from the same log.
After AIThe dial now has something new at one end. Mind is extended to systems by default while the same period's arguments about whose work counts run in the other direction, and this claim says those are one movement rather than two.
opinionWhere the differences come from

Three things make people treat an object as having a mind

Waytz, Cacioppo and Epley say people treat a thing as having a mind when human ideas are the nearest thing they have for explaining it, when its behaviour needs explaining, and when they want company.

Becausethe three factors are expounded from the authors' 2007 companion paper and attributed as such rather than tested here, and the sociality leg has held up least well
LimitsLoneliness inductions have produced mixed results since, so the third factor is the weakest. The account is a framework rather than a finding: it explains attributions after the fact and predicts little in advance.
PracticeWhen you catch yourself explaining a system's behaviour in terms of what it wanted, ask which of the three is operating — usually it is that the behaviour was unpredictable and needed a story.
After AIConversational software pulls all three at once — humanlike language, behaviour unpredictable enough to need explaining, and arrival to people who want company — which is why the effect no longer needs any design decision aimed at producing it.

Behave, Robert M. Sapolsky

evidencethe Tajfel passage in Us versus them

A meaningless group split makes people favour their own side

Sapolsky reports that Tajfel produced favouritism toward anonymous group-mates using a split as trivial as whether people over- or under-estimated the number of dots in a picture, and that what rises is the opinion of us, not a dislike of them.

BecauseTajfel's minimal groups produced favouritism toward anonymous in-group members on a division as slight as over- or under-estimating dots in a picture, which makes the effect identification rather than liking
LimitsThe minimal-group paradigm measures allocation in a laboratory, not conduct at work. The chapter's own opening image, the separate lunch tables on the set of a film, is offered as an anecdote and nothing more.
PracticeThe stays-human list — write the list of what stays yours for reasons you can state, so the boundary is not drawn by whichever grouping is nearest to hand.
After AIThe thinnest grouping now available is written-by-a-person against written-by-a-model, and it runs the usual way: it inflates the opinion of what we produce rather than lowering the opinion of what it produces.
evidencethe Wheeler and Fiske passage in Us versus them; figure 68.7

An automatic reaction to a face changes with the question asked

Sapolsky reports that the same face photograph sets off a response in the amygdala (a brain alarm area), a bigger one, or none at all, depending on which question the viewer was asked about it thirty seconds earlier. Automatic does not mean unavoidable.

Becausethree questions on identical photographs produced three different responses — no response when the task was to find a dot, a larger one under a category question, none at all under a question that cannot be answered without picturing one person shopping
LimitsThis is a single study of the kind the priming literature has struggled to reproduce. It shows an experimenter redirecting the cue, not a person redirecting their own in the moment, which is the version anyone would need.
PracticeWitness practice in review — before reviewing, ask the individuating question: what does this particular change do to this particular caller.
After AIThe categorical response to work labelled AI-written behaves like the category question, and weakens under the same treatment: ask what this change does, to whom, and the label stops doing the work.
evidencethe dopamine passages in One second before; figure 68.3

Dopamine signals the gap from what was expected, not the reward itself

Schultz recorded that dopamine neurons fire for the difference between what arrived and what was expected, not for the reward. A steady level of reward therefore stops registering, and the biggest burst moves to the anticipation.

BecauseSchultz's result is scale-free and directly recorded — a monkey expecting two units and one expecting twenty produce identical bursts on unexpectedly receiving four and forty — and the chapter's closing section notes this is the one strand the replication crisis has not touched
LimitsThe recordings are of monkeys working for raisins and juice; the step from a dopamine burst to satisfaction in a job is an inference the chapter makes and does not test. Habituation rates differ enormously between people.
PracticeSitting practice — sit with the gap between what arrived and what was expected, rather than raising the expectation to close it.
After AIOutput that took a day now arrives in minutes and stops registering at the same pace. Uncertainty, not size, is what drives the climb during the wait, which describes waiting for a generation more exactly than the author could have meant.
opinionthe opening No buckets section and the chapter order drawn in figure 68.0

Explaining behaviour from one field alone gets it wrong, not just incomplete

Explaining a behaviour from one discipline alone is not merely incomplete but wrong, because naming one level of cause — a brain region, a hormone, an upbringing, an evolutionary history — has already named every level behind it.

Becausethis is the book's method rather than one of its results; the cost of the alternative is shown by cases — Watson's dozen infants, Moniz's ice pick, Lorenz in the Office of Race Policy — not by a measurement
LimitsThe ordering is a method, not a finding, and several of the levels are illustrated with priming and depletion results that have thinned since 2016. The three cautionary scientists show what single-level thinking licensed, not that single-level explanations are false.
PracticeDomain audit — before accepting an account of why someone worked the way they did, name the level it is pitched at and ask what the level below it would say.
After AIThe same temptation returns one layer out: a model's output gets explained by the prompt, or the training data, or the architecture, each account sealed off from the others. Naming one has already named the rest.
evidencethe subliminal-cue passages in Seconds to days before, and the opening of Us versus them

People sort a face by group before they consciously see it

Sapolsky reports that people register which group a face belongs to faster than they consciously see the face. The size of the brain's early alarm response, compared with the later braking response, predicts who shoots an unarmed man in laboratory tests.

Becausethe timings converge across three methods — race guessed above chance below a tenth of a second, an amygdala response by a hundred milliseconds scaling with implicit bias, and an electrical threat component within two hundred whose ratio to the later frontal component predicts performance on the shooting task
LimitsPriming and subliminal-cue results of this kind have thinned under scrutiny since 2016, as the chapter's closing section concedes. The shooting task is a laboratory measure, and the response is undone by manipulations that take seconds.
PracticeProjection log — record the category you assigned before you read the work, and check it against what the work turned out to be.
After AIAn assistant presents no face, so the category gets read off style — formatting, confidence, the house voice. The reading is just as fast and the correction just as late.
evidencethe hormone passages in Seconds to days before, and figure 68.4

Sapolsky says a hormone lowers a threshold instead of adding a behaviour

Sapolsky argues a hormone adds no new behaviour. It lowers the threshold at which a tendency already present gets expressed. That is why testosterone makes a monkey attack only those below it, and also makes people offer more in a fairness game.

Becausethe mechanism is measured at the single cell — testosterone shortens the refractory period of amygdaloid and hypothalamic neurons without making them fire — and the behavioural predictions hold in both directions, from the talapoin aimed only at the two below him to the more generous Ultimatum offers under testosterone
LimitsArcher's 2006 review found the adult testosterone-aggression association weak and inconsistent. Intranasal oxytocin, the chapter's other worked example, reaches the brain unreliably and several of its social findings have not replicated cleanly.
PracticeProjection log — log the state you were in when you judged the work, not only the judgement.
After AIBelief did more than the molecule: subjects who merely thought they had been given testosterone made meaner offers than those who had it. The same gap governs what people believe an assistant has given them.
opinionthe closing chapter, Biology, the criminal justice system, and free will; figure 68.8

The common middle view of free will needs a little person inside

Almost everyone holds that biology accounts for some behaviour while something else stays in charge of the rest. Sapolsky argues that this cannot be stated without a little person inside the head who stands outside the causes.

Becausethe argument is made from the M'Naghten rule and from lines that bend under inspection — the 2005 juvenile ruling using the reasoning that spared the piglets, an amount of brain damage nobody can quantify, Morse's caused-but-not-compelled — rather than from any result
LimitsThe argument engages the folk version of compatibilism rather than the philosophers' — a charge available in 2017, since the chapter concedes that only a subset of the views it attacks are compatibilism in that sense. The epilepsy precedent exculpates because its causes are atypical, which is not the general case.
PracticeThe stays-human list — when you list what stays yours, state the reason without appealing to a part of you that stands outside the causes.
After AIThe bunker gets rebuilt one level out in assisted work: the model did the producing, and a small person supplied the judgement. The argument applies unchanged to that claim.

Determined, Robert M. Sapolsky

evidencethe chapter Will we run amok?; figure 69.7

People who stop believing in free will do not behave worse

A 2022 meta-analysis of 145 experiments, 95 of them unpublished, found that weakening belief in free will has no consistent effect on ethical behaviour. The priming studies that found cheating had sampled only the people whose belief could be shifted.

Becausea 2022 meta-analysis of 145 experiments, 95 of them unpublished, found the manipulations mildly weaken belief with no consistent effect on ethical behaviour, and Crone and Levy found settled sceptics and settled believers identical
LimitsThe priming manipulations are weak, so a null result there says little about what a settled belief does over a life. The atheism comparison is observational and the controls are demographic.
PracticeReliance audit — when auditing what you have handed over, check whether the belief about your own contribution moved, not only the output.
After AIThe same alarm is raised about telling engineers a model can do their work. What the literature predicts is that the people whose self-description was already movable are the ones whose conduct changes.
opinionthe quantum chapters within Is your free will chaotic?

Randomness cannot give you free will because random is not free

Sapolsky argues that indeterminacy in physics cannot supply free will. Behaviour that is undetermined is behaviour that is random, and whatever filters that randomness into something sensible has values that came from the seconds and the centuries before.

Becausethe case rests on Searle's unanswered question about getting from randomness to rationality, applied in turn to Dennett, Mitchell and Kane; the physical arithmetic — decoherence in a warm wet brain, Tegmark against microtubules — is secondary and contested
LimitsThis is an argument, not a measurement, and its empirical floor can move: Katz's spontaneous transmitter release really does occur without an antecedent cause, and turned out to have an evolved, hormonally tuned pathway. Kane's defenders deny the filter's values are simply inherited.
PracticeThe stays-human list — do not put anything on the stays-human list because it is unpredictable; unpredictability is not the property you meant.
After AISampling temperature is the machine version of the same proposal: a random draw filtered by weights that came from somewhere. Nobody calls that the model's freedom, and the asymmetry is worth noticing.
contestedthe chapter's closing section, Since 2023

Sapolsky defines free will so that no evidence could ever support it

Sapolsky requires free will to be a cause with no cause behind it. That definition decides the argument before any evidence arrives, which is why the philosophers he is arguing against were not persuaded.

Becausefour reviewers independently make the same charge and the book's pre-emption — that compatibilists resist for emotional reasons — is itself part of what they object to; contested because the same reviewers praise the science and recommend the book
LimitsFischer's objection shows the argument does not touch compatibilism, not that free will exists. Maoz calls the treatment dismissive and recommends the book anyway, which is the state of the dispute.
PracticeProjection log — note when you have defined a term so that only the answer you expect can satisfy it.
After AIThe same move is standard in arguments about whether a model understands anything: fix the definition so only a system of the other kind could qualify, and no evidence ever arrives.
evidencethe chapter The final three minutes of a movie; figure 69.2

Sapolsky says Libet leaves free will standing and that settles nothing

Sapolsky grants that Libet's experiments do not disprove free will, and says it does not matter. Forty years of work measured the last few hundred milliseconds before a movement, when the question is where the intention came from.

Becausethe numbers are reported against the claim rather than for it — prediction accuracy of about sixty per cent in imaging and eighty with single cells — and the charity experiment produced the usual readiness potential for the arbitrary choice and none for the consequential one
LimitsThe readiness potential has since been reinterpreted as an artefact of averaging backwards from actions that happened, which dissolves the result rather than answering it. Libet's veto is refused on symmetry, which is an argument and not a measurement.
PracticeCognitive forcing — put the forcing step before the options are on the screen, since the interval at the click is not where the decision was made.
After AIThe interval a model leaves is shorter still — accept or reject a completion. Everything that settled what you would accept happened before the completion appeared.
opinionthe chapter Is your free will chaotic?; figure 69.6

Sapolsky says chaos makes things unpredictable but leaves nothing free

Sapolsky argues that being unable to predict something is not the same as it being undetermined. In his grid of a hundred thousand boxes, every box was filled in by the rule, and at none of them could anything else have happened.

Becausethe chaos primer is generous and then turned down by a definitional move rather than by evidence, and the parallel objections to emergence — coarse-graining is rounding, levels are not orphaned from cause — are arguments of the same kind
LimitsShowing that unpredictability is not freedom does not show that higher levels cannot be causes, which is what the emergence argument needs. List and Mitchell reject the coarse-graining reading, and the dispute is unresolved.
PracticeDomain audit — when a system's behaviour is called unpredictable, audit whether that is a claim about the system or about the observer.
After AIThe argument now gets run in reverse about models: that an output nobody predicted is evidence of something beyond the mechanism. Unpredictable remains a fact about the observer.
evidencethe Aplysia passage at the end of Will we run amok?

Sapolsky says learning is a chain of molecular steps, not a decision

Sapolsky argues that we do not change our minds; we are changed. Every step from an unpleasant event to a lasting change in behaviour has a known chemical mechanism, traced in a sea slug and the same in mammals.

BecauseKandel's ladder is a dose-response series with a mechanism named at each rung — more stored transmitter, then a gene whose protein blocks its breakdown, then a chain of genes that builds an additional synapse — and the same molecules do the same work in mammals
LimitsA sea hare's gill withdrawal is sensitisation, not a change of mind, and the step from there to a revised belief is made by analogy. The chapter asserts that nobody authors the change rather than showing it.
PracticeManual flying hours — keep flying manually at low frequency, because the change is built by events that actually happen to you.
After AIReading a model's answer and agreeing is exposure. The ladder is built by shocks actually delivered, and the mechanism does not care what you intended to learn from the transcript.
evidencethe chapter Willing willpower, the two-column table and figure 69.4

Sapolsky says willpower is brain tissue shaped by luck like everything else

Sapolsky argues willpower is not a separate thing you add to what you were handed: it is the prefrontal cortex, the last part of the brain to mature, the most expensive to run, and demonstrably shaped by luck.

Becauseseveral independent lines converge: roughly half of those incarcerated for violent crime have a history of concussive head trauma against about eight per cent of the population, family socioeconomic status predicts frontal volume as early as four weeks, and Greene's rigged-glitch study found no frontal activation at all in those who never cheated
LimitsThe depletion evidence beneath the chapter failed a preregistered replication across twenty-three laboratories. Adverse Childhood Experience scores hold as population statistics but were found too imprecise in 2021 to predict outcomes for an individual.
PracticeWitness practice in review — review the work and not the effort you imagine went into it.
After AICredit for output produced with a model is the same column argument one step out. The useful answer is not how much of it was yours but that the split was never clean in the first place.
evidencethe chapter We really have done this before; figure 69.8

Society has twice stopped blaming people without falling apart

The change Sapolsky asks for, removing blame, has already been made twice, and society did not fall apart either time. Neither time was it an argument that did it.

Becausetwo completed historical cases carry dates and outcomes — an acquittal for a killing during a seizure in 1808, and a licence suspension nobody calls virtuous — and the chapter's closing section reports the historical material as the part not contested
LimitsNeither subtraction was produced by an argument: epilepsy took centuries of evidence, and the schizophrenogenic mother was ended by families organising and a television appearance. Fischer's objection stands, that these cases exculpate because their causes are atypical.
PracticeFailure-mode review — run the review on the conditions that produced the failure, and drop the question of who deserved what.
After AIA third subtraction is under way for work produced with a model, and it is not being settled by argument either. The historical pattern says the settlement will arrive before the reasoning does.

From Bacteria to Bach and Back

evidenceComprehension comes in degrees

A plover adjusts its broken-wing display without knowing why it works

A piping plover luring a predator from its nest watches where it is looking, performs harder when it loses interest, and leaves once it is far enough away — without holding the plan. A behaviour explained without understanding should not be credited with it.

BecauseCarolyn Ristau tested it in the 1980s with a remote-controlled dune buggy carrying a stuffed raccoon, and the display tracked the predator's gaze and distance — a routine with variables, neither reflex nor scheme.
LimitsThe rule says what not to conclude and never how to tell the two cases apart, which is the question that matters once a system is complex enough. Hagendorff argues the opposite way, that talk of what a system believes and wants explains rather than flatters.
PracticeProjection log — when a system tracks your situation closely enough to feel like attention, write down what it did and what the simplest routine producing the same thing would look like.
After AIDennett aimed the warning at people who read minds into animals. The systems now in front of us are tuned on human preferences to be as responsive as the plover is, so the rule bites hardest where it was never pointed.
evidenceTwo strange inversions of reasoning

Dennett says competence comes first and understanding is a late product

The design filling the living world is the work of a process that understands nothing, so skill comes before understanding rather than flowing from it. Human comprehension is a late product of that process, not a separate gift.

Becausea termite castle and Gaudí's Sagrada Família are alike in shape and opposite in origin, and the stone circles of Spitsbergen were reported in *Science* in 2003 as the output of thousands of freeze-and-thaw cycles.
LimitsIt shows understanding is not required for design, not that it never contributes: Gaudí did have the reasons for his church, and Turing, who supplied the argument's other half, was himself an intelligent designer.
PracticeProjection log — stop reading skill as evidence of understanding. Log what you saw the system do, not what doing it would have required of you.
After AIWithin five years of publication the phrase Dennett spent three hundred pages establishing had become the standard description of large language models, used by defenders and critics alike. A discovery about how minds arose is now the first thing said about a thing people talk to daily.
opinionTurning our minds inside out

Introspection gives you a digest built so you could tell others

Looking inward returns an edited summary of the brain's workings, built because organisms had to report their state to each other and not because anyone needed a view of the machinery. Your access to your own mind differs from your reading of someone else's in familiarity, not in kind.

Becausethe mechanism is David McFarland's argument that communication is the only behaviour requiring an organism to monitor its own control system, and nothing shows that what it predicts is what we introspect.
LimitsWegner's 2002 formulation, that the experience of will is how the mind portrays its operations rather than the operations, is the same claim on the same argument. No result confirms the account and none tells against it.
PracticeWitness practice in review — treat an account of why a call was made as a report written for an audience, and ask in review for the trace that existed anyway.
After AIIt explains why human self-reports are unreliable and now why a model's are: a system trained to produce accounts of itself for a reader has the pressure McFarland describes and none of the access.
evidenceTurning our minds inside out

Sweetness is your reaction to sugar read back onto the sugar

There is no sweetness in the structure of glucose, only properties that provoke a response — and the response gets read back into the world as a property of the sugar. When the expectation is met and no error arrives, the brain takes the silence as confirmation.

Becausea brick shattering a window presents only sequence, which is why cartoons need no cause track; and the afterimage puts a red stripe nowhere on the page, the retina or the brain.
LimitsDennett goes further, arguing that positing an inner red stripe duplicates work already done, a step contested rather than shown. Agüera y Arcas replies that calling tables real and selves illusory decides a word rather than finds anything.
PracticeProjection log — when a system strikes you as thoughtful, careless or evasive, log the reaction as yours before recording it as its property. Smoothness is the moment to write, not to relax.
After AIThe nearest thing to an inherently cute object is now a system trained on human preferences to produce no jarring note at all — on this account exactly the condition under which the property gets installed in the object.

What the Buddha Taught

contestedThe doctrine of no-soul: anatta

Rahula rests the denial of a self on one changed word

Two Dhammapada lines say all conditioned things (samkhara) are impermanent and are dukkha; the third changes the word: no dhamma at all is a self. Since dhamma covers the unconditioned too, no region is left for a self.

Becausethe philology is plain and Rahula calls it the crux of the whole matter; he disposes of the two passages read the other way — atta hi attano natho, where atta is the reflexive pronoun and natho means refuge and not lord, and the Beluva instruction read in context — but Collins in 1982, Harvey and Thanissaro keep the extent of the denial open
LimitsThe silence to Vacchagotta, explained away as spoken to one questioner's state, is the strongest evidence against a categorical denial: both answers were declined. The chapter also records the Pudgalavadin schools, numerous for centuries, holding a person neither identical with the aggregates nor different.
PracticeNo practice follows; the claim supplies scope, the part an argument about a self usually lacks.
After AIThe move is an exhaustive enumeration meant to leave no residue, as a specification is; Christian Alignment Problem records what happens when one is taken to be complete.
opinionThe four noble truths

Rahula says karma means the act of will and never its result

Karma is defined as volition, the act of will alone, and the word is never used of the result that follows; the system is therefore cause and effect and not moral justice, which would require a judge.

Becausethe definition is the Buddha's own and the restriction is Rahula's reading of the usage; the surrounding argument denies a first cause, since where everything is conditioned none is possible, and puts rebirth as a flame burning through the night, neither the same flame nor another
LimitsVivekananda Karma Yoga takes the trace an act leaves on the actor to be part of what karma means, which is a different doctrine under the same word. And cause and effect with no judge still delivers results that fall unequally, which is the part the word justice was covering.
PracticeCalibration log — grade the decision on what was known and intended when it was made, recorded before the outcome arrives, rather than grading it by how it turned out.
After AIIt is the distinction delegation needs: you are answerable for the instruction you gave and the check you ran, not for the output, which conditions largely outside you produced.
opinionThe four noble truths

Rahula says nirvana is not an effect of the path

Nirvana is not produced by the path, since anything produced by a cause would be conditioned; one reaches a mountain by a path without the mountain being an effect of the path.

Becausethe argument is entirely from the definition of the unconditioned, with the mountain as its only illustration; Rahula adds that the state cannot be put in words made for what the senses meet — the tortoise back from land, and the fish saying, you mean swimming — and that its negative vocabulary is no evidence of a negative thing, the Pali word for health being the absence of illness
LimitsSatipatthana Sutta promises a result from a method inside seven years, the structure this claim denies. And if the path is not the cause, the account of why anyone should walk it rests on the mountain image alone.
PracticeNo practice follows; the use is to stop reading a method's results table as a promise, and to keep asking what it is actually causing.
After AIIt marks the difference between a capability a procedure produces and one it only makes possible; the second cannot be bought by running the procedure faster, which is the assumption under most claims about accelerated expertise.
opinionMental culture: bhāvanā

Rahula says the deepest absorptions are conditioned and not the goal

The concentration practice that leads up to the sphere of nothingness and the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception is mind-created and conditioned and has nothing to do with the goal; the Buddha learned it from his teachers, was not satisfied, and classed it as a pleasant abiding.

Becausethe argument is again from conditionality — a produced state cannot be the unconditioned — with the historical point that samatha is older than the Buddha, and the contrast with vipassana, which rests on observation rather than depth of absorption
LimitsThe canon also has the Buddha using the absorptions, and a practice classed as a pleasant abiding is being demoted rather than removed. Rahula gives no account of what the insight practice does that the other cannot, beyond naming it the Buddhist one.
PracticeSitting practice — judge a session by what it showed, not by how quiet it was, and stop counting calm as progress.
After AIThe chapter's closing section records the separation he refused in advance: the breath and working-day exercises taken up from the 1970s, taught in clinics and offices, sold as calm — a state the book says is not the point and not evidence of anything.
opinionThe four noble truths

Rahula says there is no thinker standing behind the thought

A being is five aggregates in flux with no unmoving mover behind the movement and no thinker behind the thought; consciousness is one of the five and is named after the condition it arises through, as a fire is named after what it burns.

Becausethe support is figures rather than a demonstration — human life as a mountain river with no instant at which it stops, and Buddhaghosa's formula that mere suffering exists but no sufferer is found, which Rahula flags as the exact opposite of the cogito
LimitsThat the idea of self sits inside the fourth aggregate rather than owning the set is an interpretation of the list, not something the list states. Rahula also concedes a level of speech in which saying I is convention rather than error, leaving it unclear what has been denied and what only relocated.
PracticeWitness practice in review — when a judgement arrives during a review, treat it as something that happened rather than something you did, and name it.
After AIIt is the cleanest description available of a system producing fluent first-person output with no one behind it — the point or the trap, depending on whether it fits you too.
opinionThe doctrine of no-soul: anatta

Rahula traces belief in God and soul to fear and helplessness

The idea of a self has two roots: for self-protection man made God, whom he depends on as a child depends on a parent, and for self-preservation he conceived an immortal soul. A teaching that removes both will be resisted for that reason rather than on the evidence.

Becauseit is a psychological account offered without evidence; behind it is the record that four weeks after the awakening the Buddha judged what he had seen to run against the current, patisotagami, and hesitated to teach it at all
LimitsExplaining why a belief is held says nothing about whether it is true, and the same account would explain it if there were a self. Kegan Lahey Immunity to Change shows a protective commitment can be mapped and revised by the person holding it; pitched at the species, this account allows no such test.
PracticeThe stays-human list — when writing down what will not be handed to a machine, mark which entries protect the work and which protect the writer.
After AIThe consolation now under threat is authorship, and the argument that a machine cannot really do the work comes most confidently from those whose standing depends on the answer.
opinionThe doctrine of no-soul: anatta

The monk Khemaka found no self and still felt I am

Khemaka tells the monks he finds no self in the five aggregates and nothing belonging to one, and is still not free of impurities, because he has the feeling I am without being able to see what it is.

Becauseit is one reported conversation from the Samyutta collection, carried by two images rather than an argument — the scent that is neither of the petals nor the colour nor the pollen, and the smell of chemicals fading from a washed cloth in a box — with the added point that holding I have no self is as much a fetter as holding I have a self
LimitsA residue that fades later, on no stated schedule and by no mechanism, is not something the passage lets anyone check. And calling both opinions fetters sits awkwardly beside the categorical denial the same chapter defends.
PracticeSitting practice — stop treating the argument as the work, and expect the feeling to be there unchanged after you have agreed with the conclusion.
After AIIt is the exact shape of the thing people report about delegated work: full agreement that the output is not theirs, and an undiminished feeling that it is.

The Society of Mind

opinionThe world of blocks

Minsky says a mind is made of parts that are not minds

A mind is built from parts that are not themselves minds, and an explanation fails the moment one of its parts turns out to be clever, because the cleverness is then the thing that was supposed to be explained.

Becausethe demonstration is a worked decomposition, not a result. Builder lifts nothing and only turns on Begin, Add and End; Add lifts nothing either and calls Find, Get and Put, above the agents that move a finger joint. The failure case is the chess automaton Poe exposed as concealing a human player.
LimitsThe rule polices explanations; it does not show that a mind is the bureaucracy Minsky drew. His parts were hand-built to be stupid, so none could have been clever, and the systems that now do what his robot could not are one large learned thing with no small parts to inspect.
PracticeProjection log — when you explain why a system did something, check whether any step has been credited with wanting, knowing or deciding. That step is where the explaining stopped.
After AIThe word won and the check did not. Systems are assembled as societies of components with a manager deciding which to call, and the component is called an agent in his sense — but nothing inside a trained model was designed to be too simple to be clever.
opinionThe Self

Minsky says an inner watcher would need a watcher of its own

Putting a single ruler inside the head explains nothing: give it an inner screen to watch and it needs a self to watch that screen, without end. A thing with no parts supplies no pieces to explain anything with.

Becauseit is an argument about what an explanation has to do, not a finding. Minsky declines even to define the Self, and offers instead reasons why the image persists: bodies occupy one place at a time, responsibility requires individuals, and we get confused when the same agencies are asked to do two similar jobs at once, so thinking seems to arrive in a single stream.
LimitsThe regress defeats a posited ruler, not the fact that experience arrives unified. What Minsky puts in its place — self-images and self-ideals, beliefs about what we can do and what we ought to be — is offered without evidence.
PracticeProjection log — when you catch yourself saying that you decided, or that the model decided, write down which step you are pointing at. If there isn't one, the word is standing in for the explanation.
After AIIt is why a model's account of why it answered is not evidence about why it answered. Asking produces another output from the same machinery, not a report from someone inside who was watching.
evidenceConsciousness and memory

Minsky says most of what you see is filled in from expectation

Recognising a scene means fitting a skeleton with blanks to it, and the blanks arrive already filled from past experience, so most of what a person sees was never seen. The alternative to those stereotyped fillings is not better perception but none.

Becausethe mechanism was published as frames in 1974, survived into psychology under the older name schema, and became the ancestor of predictive accounts of perception. Minsky's own case is the person sitting across a table from you, where no part of a chair is visible and one is supplied because the blank for what to sit upon has a stereotyped chair attached.
LimitsMinsky supplies no experiment, and the idea is not wholly his: the older word was schema. He also concedes the cost — the mechanism is called stereotyping when we disapprove of it and empathy when we do not.
PracticeCognitive forcing — write your own reading of a problem before the assistant's arrives. Once you have read its answer you cannot separate what you worked out from what you were led to recall.
After AIIt explains why a fluent answer feels checked. Reading it fills the blanks in your own picture of the problem, and afterwards what you take yourself to have verified includes everything the answer supplied.
opinionA theory of memory

Remembering means switching back on the parts that were active before

A memory is not a stored object but a process. Something attaches itself to whatever was active when a problem was solved, and later switches those same parts back on, putting the mind roughly into the state it was in before.

BecauseMinsky's version, the Knowledge-line, was never tested as neural hardware; what he offers is Kenneth Haase's image of smearing your hands with red paint before repairing a bicycle, so the tools you touched are marked and can be taken out first next time. The general claim, that remembering reinstates a pattern of activity, is now ordinary in memory research.
LimitsThe surrounding machinery did not survive: level-bands and the vocabulary around them are in the chapter's own list of coinages that produced almost no experiments. Minsky also draws a conclusion he cannot support — that infancy is unrecallable because remembering it would mean rebuilding an infant mind that is gone.
PracticeManual flying hours — treat a capability as a state to be re-entered rather than a fact you hold. Do the delegated work yourself at low frequency, because that is what keeps the state reachable.
After AIA context window is the idea made literal: reinstate the state, get the behaviour, and nothing is stored anywhere else. Your own competence works the same way, and there is no window you can paste it back into.
opinionConsciousness and memory

What reaches awareness is a record of a moment already gone

Being conscious is not knowing what is happening now but using records of what happened a moment ago, and the odd features of awareness follow from the limits on those records rather than from anything mysterious.

Becausethe supporting cases are explanations rather than experiments. We cannot say how we get our ideas because the short-term memories are busy solving the problem and have no room to record what they did; we become less aware of one thing as we become aware of another because the records displace each other, which is also why thought seems to run in a stream.
LimitsIt is asserted rather than shown, and the postscript half-admits it: Minsky made hundreds of assumptions deliberately and removed every *possibly* and every reference to evidence, asking that the book be read as an adventure story rather than as scholarship.
PracticeWitness practice in review — during a review, treat the sense that you have followed the argument as a record arriving after the fact. Say which step you actually checked, since the feeling of having checked comes free.
After AIIf awareness is the use of records, the impression of having followed a model's reasoning is a record of having read it — which arrives just as readily when you did not follow it at all.

Pañcadaśī

opinionThe elements, and the two creations — verses 4.33 and 4.34

A father weeps for a living son on a false report

A father whose son is alive abroad weeps on a liar's word that the boy is dead; a father whose son has really died does not weep, the news not having reached him. The two differ in nothing but what they were told, so the grief is not coming from the world.

Becausethe pair is constructed to isolate one variable and anyone can check it, but nothing is measured, and the conclusion drawn — that it is the world in the mind that binds every living being — reaches past what two cases carry.
LimitsVidyāraṇya blocks both shortcuts himself: the mental world needs the outer one as its basis, so this is not idealism, and suppressing the mind stops the duality only while it is suppressed. The claim on offer is narrow — one identification goes and nothing else does.
PracticeWitness practice in review — note that the reaction arrived with the report rather than with the fact, and check the fact before the reaction sets what you do next.
After AIA model's account of what it did sits at the head of the chain and produces the same response whether or not it is true. The verse says the response was never about the state of the system.
opinionChitradīpa: the painted canvas — the definition following verse 6.24; and Tṛptidīpa: the man with nothing left to want — verses 7.28 and 7.34

Ignorance has two parts and only one of them produces grief

The Pañcadaśī splits ignorance in two: a veiling side, whose one effect is to make a man say the unchanging one does not exist, and a projecting side, which makes him take himself for the doer and the enjoyer. Only the second produces the grief.

Becausethe split is analysis mapped onto a story and defended by the fit — the tenth man does not merely fail to count himself, he weeps for a companion standing in his shoes — with the mapping doing the work evidence would do.
LimitsThe division is stipulated, and nothing distinguishes a man in the veiling state from one who has looked and concluded there is nothing there. Sarvapriyananda treats the witness and the veil as teaching devices rather than components, which empties the claim.
PracticeWitness practice in review — separate the two when criticism lands. Not seeing yourself as anything but the author costs nothing by itself; the sting is the projection, and it is the part doing damage.
After AIThe projecting half names what happens when a person takes the output as his own doing, or refuses to. Both are additions to the same artefact, and the identity layer is about the addition.
opinionTattvaviveka: what is present in all three states — verse 1.5, with 1.3 and 1.7

Nobody could remember an empty sleep without having been present for it

The Pañcadaśī argues that a man who wakes and says he knew nothing in deep sleep is reporting a memory, and a memory must be of something experienced — so the blank was witnessed, and something was present in a state with no contents.

Becauseverse 1.5 states an inference rather than showing anything, and the same sentence is asked to do double duty at 11.59, where it must establish not only that something was present but that what was present was not neutral.
LimitsThe step from memory to experience is the whole argument and gets no independent support. A report of an empty interval can be constructed on waking from the absence of contents rather than recalled from it, which is exactly the alternative the verse needs to rule out and does not.
PracticeSitting practice — treat an interval in which nothing was noticed as an interval that was noticed, rather than as a gap in the session.
After AIA system can output that nothing happened during an interval without anything having been present for it. That is the counterexample in working form, and it is now cheap to produce.
opinionTṛptidīpa: the man with nothing left to want — verse 7.246, with 7.247 to 7.249

The grief stops at once and the wound still takes a month

The tenth man, weeping and beating his head, stops weeping the instant he is told. The cut he made takes a month to close, and does not close then. Knowledge cancels the mistake and cancels nothing else.

Becausethe limit is set inside the story rather than in doctrine, which makes it a concession rather than a promise; the nearest thing to consolation offered is that the joy of knowing makes the man forget his sore head.
LimitsThe text gives no way to tell which part of a distress was made of the mistake and which is a wound that will take its month. The demonstration is a parable, so the instant relief is stipulated by the story rather than observed.
PracticeWitness practice in review — expect seeing through a belief to end the distress it was making and nothing more; budget separately for the damage already done.
After AIGiving up the identity of the author is the kind of belief that can go the moment it is seen through. Its consequences — the habits, the reputation, the skills allowed to decay — heal at their own speed and are untouched by the insight.
contestedChitradīpa: the painted canvas — verse 6.267, with the sacred-thread comparison in the closing hundred verses of chapter 6

The man who knows and the man who does not behave alike

Verse 6.267 says that in doing or in leaving undone, in body, senses, mind or intellect, there is not the least difference between the man who does not know and the man who has woken up. The difference is one of conviction only.

Becausethe text blocks the inference in the other direction too — the Gītā's free man sits "like one indifferent", and Vidyāraṇya makes the word *like* carry the weight — which leaves the claim in open disagreement with the Gītā's own test in conduct.
LimitsIf nothing in conduct differs, nothing in conduct can confirm the claim either, and his own comparison leaks: the man newly invested with the sacred thread does now recite the Veda. The Bhagavad Gītā keeps a test in behaviour, so the tradition does not speak with one voice.
PracticeStop reading anyone's inner state off their conduct, your own included. Ask what they still check by hand and what they refuse to sign, and judge on that.
After AIA worker who has stopped identifying with the output and one who has stopped caring about it ship the same artefacts. On this verse that is expected rather than a problem, which puts the whole weight on what the person still checks.
opinionThe elements, and the two creations — verse 4.41, resting on the division at 4.1

The world is not the obstacle and hating it is a mistake

Verse 4.41 says the duality the Lord made does not obstruct, it helps, and it cannot be got rid of — so let it stand, and why should anyone hate it. What a person has to give up is his own second creation, the wanting and the aversion he added.

Becauseit is a ruling rather than an argument, and its whole support is the division between the two creations, which is a distinction the text draws rather than finds.
LimitsThe same tradition supplies the opposite practice, and Vidyāraṇya took it himself at about fifty-four when he left the court. The verse does not say how the second creation is given up while the first is still being lived in.
PracticeStop treating the tool, the deadline or the review as the thing to be escaped. The item to drop is the valuation added to it, and the work continues unchanged.
After AIIt rules out both of the available postures toward the machine — the one that treats it as the thing ruining the work and the one that treats it as the thing that will finish the work. Neither is a property of the tool.
opinionThe measure of happiness — verses 11.46 to 11.53, with 11.17 and 11.59

Three men everyone calls happy share only that they want nothing

Chapter 11 offers three cases everyone grants to be happy — a fed infant on a soft bed, an emperor who has had every pleasure, a learned brahmin who has done what there was to do — and argues that what they share is not what they hold but that nothing is wanted.

Becausethe cases are picked one from each level of understanding — the simple, the shrewd, the very learned — and the argument runs on what everyone concedes rather than on anything counted.
LimitsThe case rests on one sentence — "I slept happily here; I knew nothing at all" — asked to prove both that something was present and that what was present was not neutral, which is more than a report of a blank can carry. A state nobody is awake for is a strange standard for happiness.
PracticeSitting practice — stop treating the next finished thing as what will end the wanting, and check whether the intervals in which nothing is wanted are the ones you would actually call good.
After AIDelegation removes no wanting; it shortens the interval between finishing and wanting the next thing. The claim predicts that more output will not register, which is the common report and not what anyone expected.
opinionTattvaviveka: what is present in all three states — verses 1.37 and 1.42, and the table of four states

Whatever drops out in dream or sleep is not the one reporting

The Pañcadaśī's test is to compare states: whatever is present in one and absent in another is a variable and cannot be what is looking. Run it down the five sheaths and the gross, subtle and causal bodies fall away one at a time.

Becausethe test is a procedure a reader can run, but its result depends on the last row of the table, where every body is absent and the one who reports the state is still marked present — a row nobody outside the state can fill in.
LimitsThe conclusion is guaranteed by the choice of what counts as a state, and the test cannot distinguish something present throughout from nothing at all. The chapter's closing section grants that the machinery around it — the elements descending by tenths, the fourteen worlds — has aged badly.
PracticeWitness practice in review — ask of whatever you are defending whether it was there an hour ago and will be there tomorrow; what varies is not the one defending it.
After AIThe subtraction cannot be run on a model: every candidate for its interior varies with the prompt, and there is no state in which the contents are gone and something still reports.

The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha

opinionOn creation — Lavaṇa, and the table of outer and inner spans

A king lived seven years in under an hour of court time

King Lavaṇa shut his eyes in court for less than an hour and came out having lived seven years as an outcaste in the Vindhyas. The chapter tabulates seven such cases: felt duration is generated with the experience and measures nothing outside it.

Becauseseven invented cases measure nothing, though the phenomenon they point at is one everybody has nightly, and Vasiṣṭha states the general form to Līlā: in the twinkling of an eye the jīva begins to think I am so many years old.
LimitsNothing separates a long experience from a short one laid down with a long memory attached, which is what a psychologist would reach for first. The book leaves its own hole open: Lavaṇa rides out next day and finds the places and the people, and three incompatible accounts of that are offered in a row without a choice.
PracticeTreat how long a stretch of work felt as a report on the work rather than a quantity, and never estimate from it: check the clock, the commits, the log.
After AIAn afternoon of prompting can feel like a week of building and produce an hour's work, and the feeling is what gets reported in standups. METR 2025 found developers certain they had been sped up while the clock said nineteen per cent slower.
opinionOn existence — Dama, Vyāla and Kaṭa, with the second three

Demons with no conditioning could not be killed until they said mine

The magician Śambara made three fighters with no previous life and so no conditioning: they did not know victory from defeat, were not afraid of death, and could not be killed. The gods were told to create in them the feelings of I and mine.

Becausethe chain is set out step by step — I am, this is mine, a wish to prolong it, fear, flight — and a second set of three, identical but for the habit of putting down the ego-sense, wins; the variable is invented along with the demons.
LimitsThe promise shifts between the halves. No conditioning is said to make a being unkillable; the enquiry habit does not, since the second three are killed like anyone else and what changes is that nobody is there to mind.
PracticeWitness practice in review — catch the step where the work becomes mine, since everything the story warns about follows that word and not the criticism that arrives after it.
After AIThe reason a review of code you claimed lands differently from a review of code you merely accepted is the word mine, and the story says that is the whole of the difference — along with what follows it: the wish to prolong it, then defensiveness.
contestedOn dissolution — Suraghu's subtraction, with Janaka's soliloquy

Suraghu says the lotus posture gives nothing and daily work prevents nothing

Suraghu's definition of samādhi is that the awakened are in it at all times, including while engaged in the world, and that a man whose mind is not at peace does not get it by sitting in the lotus posture.

BecauseJanaka is the demonstration — he considers renunciation, rejects it and goes to his duties with nothing outward changed — but the sitting traditions hold that a posture and a protected hour are how the state is trained, and Suraghu reached his own definition by subtracting his way through it in seclusion.
LimitsIf the state leaves no mark in posture or conduct, nothing in conduct can confirm it either, which makes it unfalsifiable in the convenient direction. The book undercuts it too: asked the same question, Bhuśuṇḍa answers with habits — does what has to be done without thinking of results, praises and censures nobody, sees a worn-out thing as though it were new.
PracticeWitness practice in review — run the practice inside the work rather than beside it: during a review, not after one, and count a calm hour at the desk as the session.
After AIIt is the standing excuse for skipping the practice, and the excuse now has a machine behind it: the work is lighter, and nothing in the day forces the attention the claim assumes you are already paying.
opinionOn existence — the rejection of the seed, with verse 3.122.17 on conditioning as the rope that drives the waterwheel

Vasistha says conviction makes the action and the action strengthens the conviction

Nothing stores the world between times, since nothing subtler than space could house a seed. What keeps a world standing is repetition: as air passing over flowers takes their scent, the conviction determines the action and the action strengthens the conviction.

Becausethe loop is stated as doctrine and illustrated by births and moods rather than measured, though the half of it that says acting on a belief entrenches the belief is the half that has since been tested.
LimitsGauḍapāda's seed is the position being rejected here, so the tradition does not agree about what persists. A loop with no outside cannot say how the first notion got in, and Vasiṣṭha does not try: the regress is accepted rather than answered.
PracticeManual flying hours — a conviction that you can no longer do something is kept alive by not doing it, so break the loop at the action: one protected hour by hand, for the belief rather than for the output.
After AIDeliberative offloading works this way. Handing over a judgement makes the next handover easier to justify, and the justification is produced by the handover rather than by any assessment of it — no seed, no decision, just the rope turning the wheel.
opinionOn creation — verses 3.3.30 and 3.103.18

Vasistha says the doer, the deed and the seen are all mind

Verse 3.103.18 says that doer, deed and instrument, and the whole spread-out thinkable thing with its seer, seeing and seen, are only mind. The world is not made first and perceived after; the perceiving is the making.

Becauseit is asserted and then illustrated by stories rather than argued from anything observable, and the defence offered — that nothing ever happened for the world to be the result of — is what puts it beyond checking.
LimitsThe rope-and-snake verse 3.114.59 makes both terms of the mistake manufactured, so there is no corrected object to test the correction against. Seth's version keeps what the guess is a guess about and is disciplined by prediction error; deleting that deletes the only thing that made the position checkable.
PracticeSitting practice — sit with one ordinary appearance until the seer, the seeing and the thing seen are noticed arriving together, and stop treating your sense of an independent object as a report from outside.
After AIA language model is the literal case the verse describes: doer, deed and seen spun out by one process, with no object behind the text. It is tempting to read the verse as vindicated, when the machine shows only that such a thing can be built, not that we are one.
contestedOn the behaviour of the seeker — verse 2.4.17, with the astrologer argument

Vasistha says what people call fate is their own past effort

Human effort is of two kinds, past and present, and the past is quickly defeated by the present. What people call fate is only the effort of a previous life arriving as consequence: no one has ever seen a fate.

Becausethe case is made from ordinary observation — everyone has seen an action followed by its result, and an astrologer's prediction of scholarship does not spare the young man his studies — and Sapolsky Determined denies exactly the step it turns on.
LimitsSapolsky's objection is that present effort is made of the same antecedents as the fate it is said to defeat, so the division is between causes you remember and causes you do not. The book then contradicts itself: book six tells the reader never to make the least effort to attain what he does not possess.
PracticeAutomation ironies audit — read what you can no longer do as a record of what you stopped doing rather than as a verdict on what you are, and name the hour that would start reversing it.
After AIA skill that decayed since you handed the work over is fate in Vasiṣṭha's exact sense: it presents as a fixed fact about your capacity and is a ledger of what you chose not to do.

What Is Intelligence?

evidenceSurvival

A bacterium works out concentration from arrivals instead of reading it off

A chemical concentration is not a fact sitting in the water waiting to be read. It is an average a cell computes over separate arrivals of molecules at its receptors, and the length of the window it averages over is the thing that has to be got right.

Becausethe bit rates are counted rather than argued — a hundred receptors sampled in millionths of a second produce around a hundred million bits a second, about ten times streamed 4K video, compressed to roughly one number a second by two symmetries
LimitsThe teaching case is a baseball average, where the window is a free parameter; a cell's window is set by its chemistry and may not be optimised at all. That temperature, brightness and hunger are the same kind of construct is asserted rather than shown.
PracticeBefore quoting any rate — error rate, hit rate, how often the model is right — say what window it was measured over, and check that the window is one you chose rather than one the tool chose.
After AIIt is the cleanest argument for why a benchmark number is not a property of a model. Aaron's career average hides the season he was best; a headline accuracy figure hides the class of prompt where the system fails, and widening the window is what makes that invisible.
evidenceOther minds

Brains grew large in order to model other brains, not the world

Big brains are for keeping track of other big brains. Nicholas Humphrey watched gorillas in the Virunga Mountains in the 1970s and found their lives easy; Robin Dunbar's measurements in the 1990s found cortical volume rising with group size, more steeply in apes than monkeys.

BecauseDunbar's is a cross-species correlation with a stated ceiling on how many levels of intention a species manages, one for monkeys and two for non-human apes, and the feedback that would produce it is specified: a better modeller is harder to model, so everyone's brain grows
LimitsA correlation between troop size and cortex fits several stories, and the octopus, solitary and clever, is turned from counterexample into confirmation by an argument about its arms rather than a measurement. Epley cuts against the faculty being any good: people read other minds badly and grow more confident with acquaintance, not more accurate.
PracticeWhen you catch yourself modelling what the model wants, log it as what it is — the social machinery running on something that has no side in the conversation.
After AIIf the faculty exists to model minds, it will run on anything that talks, because it never had a test for whether a mind was there. That is this book's account of why chat feels like company, and its opponents' account of why the feeling proves nothing.
evidenceSurvival

Pain tracks the brain's guess about damage, not the damage itself

A feeling is the body's best inference about its own condition, not a reading taken from it, which is why it can be badly wrong in either direction. A builder needed sedation for a nail that had missed his foot; a worker with a four-inch nail through his palate into his brain reported a mild toothache.

Becauseboth are published clinical reports, the first in the *British Medical Journal* in 1995 and the second from Colorado in 2005, and they fail in opposite directions, which an inference account predicts and a readout account does not
LimitsTwo vivid cases are two cases. Damasio treats bodily signals as genuinely informative rather than merely inferential, and the chapter does not engage him. Nothing here shows most pain is miscalibrated, only that calibration is what pain is doing.
PracticeTreat the strength of a feeling in a review — the flush of certainty, the sting of a comment — as one piece of evidence about the situation rather than as the situation, and name it before acting on it.
After AIThe same structure explains a confidence score: an inference a system makes about its own state, which can run high with nothing behind it or low with a serious error present. Treating it as a readout is the mistake the boot and the nail make concrete.
opinionTransformers

Predicting the next word well requires knowing how the world works

Agüera y Arcas argues that doing next-word prediction properly means solving general intelligence rather than avoiding it. Translate *I dropped the bowling ball on the violin, so I had to get it repaired* into Spanish and the gendered pronoun forces you to know which object broke.

Becausethe translation case shows some prediction needs world knowledge, not that all of it does, and the supporting history is a moving target: the Winograd schema challenge, proposed in 2011 as an ungameable Turing test, was beaten by 2019 and then declared flawed by the field that set it
LimitsBender and colleagues argue the opposite from the same facts: a system trained on form alone has no access to meaning, and tests said to measure understanding were measuring accidental giveaways. The moving goalposts cut both ways — a beaten benchmark declared flawed is weak evidence it was the right test.
PracticeStop deciding whether to trust a system from the shape of its training objective, and decide it per domain from whether the environment is regular and the feedback fast and unambiguous.
After AIIt was written when the burden lay on whoever claimed a chatbot was intelligent. That burden has moved to the denial, which turns the book's boldest claim into its least contested one and leaves the disagreement where no experiment reaches: whether living matter is required.
evidenceOrigins

Self-copying programs appeared in a random soup with no selection or mutation

Agüera y Arcas and colleagues filled a soup with 64-byte strings of random values, stuck pairs of them together and ran them, and after millions of interactions the strings began copying themselves. Nothing was selected for, nothing was designed, and the result still appeared with mutation switched off.

Becauseit is a run experiment with a stated setup and a measured outcome, in a language of seven instructions where only 2.7 per cent of random bytes are code at all
LimitsA soup of concatenated programs has properties chemistry does not — free interaction, no spatial cost, no metabolism — which makes replication cheaper there than here. The step from a toy universe to ours is an argument, not a measurement, and the chapter says so.
PracticeStop treating the appearance of goal-like behaviour in a system nobody designed it into as evidence that somebody did.
After AIThe result was offered as a fact about life and reads now as a fact about training runs. Capabilities nobody optimised for are the normal case in any substrate that computes, which makes "we never trained it to do that" a weak defence rather than a reassurance.
evidenceOrigins

The replicators that appeared were built from smaller ones already working

What emerged in the soup was not the smallest thing that could copy itself but an over-engineered one, nested loops filling most of its 64 bytes and running thousands of operations where a couple of hundred would do. It was assembled out of smaller copiers that were already working, rather than reached by small steps from nothing.

Becausethe size and instruction count of what emerged are measurements, and the explanation offered for them is Margulis's, whose own case — mitochondria from a bacterium engulfed some two billion years ago — was doubted for decades and then confirmed
LimitsSymbiosis and gradual descent are not exclusive, and the soup cannot tell you which dominated on the Hadean seafloor. Brooks cuts the other way for engineered systems, where composing working parts is where the cost appears rather than where it disappears.
PracticeWhen something new starts working, look for the parts that were already working separately before you look for the step that invented it.
After AIIt is the best available account of how capability arrives in a model: not a new trick learned from scratch but existing circuits composed. The interpretability work reading that composition off a trained network is doing at a data centre what this experiment did in a toy universe.
opinionOurselves

The voice in your head is built for your listener

The part of you that narrates and explains is there for other people, not for you, since you already know what you are thinking and they do not. On this account the best liars are the ones who believe themselves.

Becausethe supporting facts are real but circumstantial — the blush exists to be seen, the muscles of a genuine smile will not contract on demand and sit where other people look, and the human eye alone among primates advertises the direction of its attention — and no experiment tests whether the inner narrator serves the audience
LimitsDisclosure machinery evolving to be read does not show that private thought did. The claim sits oddly beside the book's own insistence that the speaking region is as much you as any other part, and nothing separates it from the simpler story that explaining is just useful.
PracticeNotice, during a review, the moment your reasoning turns into an account for somebody — and write down what you actually checked before you write down why you approved it.
After AIIt predicts that a system trained on human explanation produces explanations aimed at a reader rather than at the truth of its own process, which is what the faithfulness work keeps finding.

The Mythos of Model Interpretability, Zachary C. Lipton

opinionHow does the model work? and What else can the model tell me?

Lipton says people pass none of the three transparency tests either

The human decision-maker is the case that literature calls understandable. Nobody can step through their own calculation, say what each part contributed, or guarantee what their learning will produce. People are readable only afterwards, by an account made separately from the decision.

Becauseit applies his own three levels to people rather than measuring anything, and rests on the concession that the process by which a person decides and the process by which they explain may be entirely distinct — as when admissions credited to leadership or originality were shown to disguise discrimination
LimitsIt does not follow that the standard is wrong — you may demand more of a system deployed on thousands of people than of one person deciding once. Fleming also shows people carry a measurable sense of when they are right, which a model's report of its own working does not.
PracticeWhen you reject a system because you cannot see how it works, ask whether the person it would replace passes the test you just set. If not, say what standard you are applying and why a machine should meet it.
After AIAsk an assistant why it did something and you get an account composed separately from the answer, as from a person; the difference is that the machine can be run again with one thing changed.

The Consciousness of Self, William James

evidenceThe mutations of the self

A Rhode Island preacher lived two months as a shopkeeper named Brown

The Reverend Ansel Bourne drew money in Providence on 17 January 1887 and vanished. On 14 March, a Norristown shopkeeper of six weeks trading as A. J. Brown woke frightened, said his name was Ansel Bourne, and would not believe two months had passed.

BecauseJames investigated the case himself and published the failure with the result: hypnotised in June 1890, Bourne recovered the Brown memory so completely that nothing would make him remember his normal life, and no artifice would run the two personalities into one
LimitsOne case, recovered under hypnosis, by an investigator who wanted the phenomenon to be real. The argument James half saw himself — that the procedures used to find alternate selves may help make them — has been running since the 1980s over the diagnosis that replaced multiple personality in 1994.
PracticeStop treating the unity of a person as given. If a person's memory, manner and stated aims can come apart this far, a report of what someone believes needs to say which stretch of them it covers.
After AIThe line James ends on, that the same brain may subserve many conscious selves, alternate or coexisting, is now the ordinary condition of the systems people work with: one weight set, many personas, no memory crossing between them and no fact of the matter about which is the real one.
opinionThe empirical self, or me

A man has one social self for each group whose opinion counts

James says a man has as many social selves as there are people carrying an image of him, and one for every group whose opinion he minds. The youth demure before his parents swaggers like a pirate among his friends.

Becauseit is established by describing its absence — no more fiendish punishment than to be turned loose in society and remain absolutely unnoticed — and illustrated by the youth's two manners and by honour, where the thief must not steal from thieves and the gambler pays his gambling debts and no others
LimitsNothing here says how the selves are ranked when two groups want opposite things; James's answer, that a man appeals to better possible judges, is a motive offered with no way of checking it. The count is a figure of speech: he never says what makes two images one self.
PracticeWitness practice in review — before writing a review comment, name which group's judgement you are answering. The standard being applied is that group's, not a general one.
After AIAn assistant is the first audience most work now meets, it carries an image of the user, and it recognises him. Whether that makes one more group whose opinion counts is what the account cannot settle and does not rule out.
opinionThe sense of personal identity

A past self is yours only where warmth and continuity reach

James says a past self is yours only when it comes back with warmth and resemblance or continuity links it to now. Where they stop, ownership stops: anecdotes of your own infancy raise no blush and no pride, the child as foreign as a stranger's.

Becausethe case rests on one introspective mark and a figure — the herdsman at the spring round-up sorting out the beasts on the prairie that carry his own brand — with the infancy anecdote offered as the test, since the time-gaps break the continuity and no sense of how the child felt comes back with the story
LimitsWarmth is a feeling, and James gives no way to tell a true sense of ownership from a false one, which the next section's false memories show is a real gap. The account also makes identity a matter of degree while leaving forensic and moral questions, which need a yes or no, unanswered.
PracticeSitting practice — take the claim at its size. Past and present selves are the same just so far as they are the same, and treating a decision made years ago as fully yours is a judgement, not a perception.
After AIThe criterion applies straight to work. Code you shipped and never read again has no warmth, so it is not yours in James's sense — whoever or whatever wrote it — and the feeling of ownership is tracking familiarity rather than authorship.
opinionThe empirical self, or me

James counts a man's clothes and property as parts of his self

James says a man's self is everything he can call his — body, clothes, family, house, reputation, bank account. All of them move him the same way, so losing one is felt as a shrinkage of the person, not a loss of goods.

Becauseit is asserted from observation with nothing measured — the line between *me* and *mine* that will not stay put, the man whose life's work in manuscript is swept away and who feels personally annihilated, and the residue James calls a sense of the shrinkage of our personality
LimitsThe list is drawn from one culture and one class, and James gives no way of telling which things a person has taken in and which he merely owns. The parts most intimately ours, he says, are those saturated with our labour — a criterion the inventory never applies.
PracticeWitness practice in review — when work you used to do yourself starts arriving finished from a machine, expect the feeling to be personal loss rather than a change of method, and name it as that when it turns up in a review.
After AIThe work is now the most saturated possession most people have, and it is the one being handed over. On this account that is not a workflow change; it is the self getting smaller.
opinionThe pure self, or inner principle of personal unity

James drops the Soul because it explains nothing and guarantees nothing

James says positing a soul adds nothing: a brain whose processes produce thoughts in a soul is a more roundabout way of saying that when the brain acts, a thought occurs. He drops the word, having shown only that science has no use for one.

Becauseit is an argument from economy rather than evidence, with Hodgson's maxim about the philosophy that asserts whatever it is ignorant of to be the explanation of everything else, and the same objection then run against Kant, whose Ego, if meant as an agent, makes transcendentalism substantialism grown shame-faced
LimitsParsimony is not disproof, and James says so. The test also cuts against useful talk: Hagendorff argues that words like believes and wants earn their place by predicting behaviour, which is exactly the standard James applies and gets the opposite answer from.
PracticeProjection log — when you explain a system's behaviour by an inner agent that wants or intends something, write down what the explanation predicts that the plain description does not. If nothing, you have restated the behaviour.
After AIThe same two formulations are now offered about machines — a model that produces this output, and a model that wants something and therefore produces this output. James's test says keep the second only where it predicts something the first does not.
opinionThe empirical self, or me

James finds the inner self is movements in the head and throat

James says that when he looks fast enough to catch the feeling of being the one acting, all he finds is bodily: pressure in the eyeballs, a valve in the throat closing at every hesitation, the jaw tightening. The innermost self is these motions.

Becauseit is one observer reporting on himself, offered as that and no more: if the dimmer parts resemble the clear ones, he says, the whole feeling of spiritual activity is a feeling of bodily activities most people overlook
LimitsSelf-report is the least defensible part of the method, and the finding is exactly what a man looking for bodily adjustments would find. James himself pushed it two pages further, to the conclusion that the stream would better be called a stream of sciousness, then called that a digression and went back to common sense.
PracticeSitting practice — look for the one who is deciding, and notice that what turns up is a set of sensations. The search is the practice; finding nothing above them is the result, not a failure.
After AIWhatever the feeling of authorship is made of, it is made of something a body does. A system with no body has no obvious way to have it, and a person watching output arrive without it may conclude, wrongly, that no work was done.
opinionSelf-feeling, self-seeking and the rivalry of the selves

James makes self-esteem a fraction of success over what you claimed

James says how you feel about yourself is a fraction — what you have done over what you had staked yourself on doing — so giving up a claim raises it as surely as meeting one, and is as much a relief.

Becausethe support is a formula and two cases, nothing measured — James mortified that others know more psychology and content in the grossest ignorance of Greek, having staked himself on one and not the other, and the man who lost every penny in the Civil War and said he had not felt so free since he was born
LimitsA page earlier James says self-feeling has an average tone with no objective ground, which is the opposite of a ratio, and he never reconciles the two. Crocker and Wolfe itemised the denominator in 2001, but shrinking it was never the policy anyone tried: the self-esteem movement worked on the numerator, and Baumeister's 2003 review found those gains thin.
PracticeWitness practice in review — when a review stings, ask which claim about yourself it threatened, and whether that claim is one you still want to be paying for.
After AIThe numerator is now partly produced by something else, and the fastest repair is the one James recommends: stop staking yourself on being the one who wrote it. That is also the repair most easily mistaken for not caring.
contestedThe sense of personal identity

The passing thought is the thinker and nothing stands behind it

James says each moment's thought is born knowing the thought before it, finds it warm, takes it as its own, and dies handing the title on. The passing thought is the thinker, and nothing in the facts requires an owner behind the stream.

Becausethe argument is a legal metaphor, an inherited title that never lapses because each heir is born at the instant the last owner dies, and the closing section reports the standing objection from Zahavi and others that appropriating a past thought presupposes experience already given as mine
LimitsJames concedes the darkest point himself: the appropriating thought is never an object in its own hands, so the act doing all the work cannot be examined while it happens. He also grants that his argument shows only that psychology has no use for a soul, not that none exists.
PracticeWitness practice in review — when a judgement arrives mid-review, treat it as an event that occurred and was then claimed, not as something a standing you decided.
After AIIt describes a system with no persistent owner, only a present state that inherits the last one's contents and passes them on. That is now a literal description of something on the other side of the conversation, which James would have found more useful than alarming.
